English Words: adverb: in groups; in flocks; in herds
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 成群的鸟从湖面上飞过。
English Usage in a sentence: Flocks of birds flew over the lake.
Notes: Often used as 成群的…… or 成群结队 “in groups.”

English Words: noun: stink; foul smell; bad odour
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 垃圾桶里散发出一股臭气。
English Usage in a sentence: A foul smell was coming from the rubbish bin.
Notes: Usually refers to an unpleasant smell. 臭味 is also common.

English Words:
verb: to stimulate; to provoke; to irritate
noun: stimulation; excitement
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这部电影的剧情非常刺激。
English Usage in a sentence: The plot of this movie is very exciting.
Notes: Can mean exciting, emotionally provoking, or physically irritating, depending on context.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 即使时间不多，他还是从容地完成了演讲。
English Usage in a sentence: Even though there was little time, he still completed the speech calmly.
Notes: More polished than 冷静; often describes someone handling pressure without rushing.

English Words: adverb: from it; from among it; from this
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们可以从中学到很多经验。
English Usage in a sentence: We can learn a great deal of experience from it.
Notes: Usually refers back to something already mentioned, such as an event, group, or process.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她唱了一首非常动听的歌。
English Usage in a sentence: She sang a very beautiful-sounding song.
Notes: Usually describes music, singing, a voice, or words that sound appealing.

English Words:
determiner: multiple; more than one
adjective: several
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个问题涉及多个部门。
English Usage in a sentence: This issue involves multiple departments.
Notes: Common in writing and reports. In casual speech, several specific items are often expressed with 几个 or 好几个.

English Words: adverb: with all one’s strength; strenuously
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他奋力向终点跑去。
English Usage in a sentence: He ran toward the finish line with all his strength.
Notes: Often used in narration with verbs such as 跑, 挣扎, 挥动, or 拼搏.

English Words: verb: to work; to do manual labour
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大家快点干活，不然今天做不完。
English Usage in a sentence: Everyone, work faster, or we will not finish today.
Notes: Casual term, especially for physical work or chores. 工作 is broader and more neutral.

English Words: noun: high altitude; high in the air
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 飞机正在万米高空飞行。
English Usage in a sentence: The aeroplane is flying at an altitude of ten thousand metres.
Notes: Common in aviation, construction, weather, and safety contexts.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子发高烧了，得马上去看医生。
English Usage in a sentence: The child has a high fever and needs to see a doctor immediately.
Notes: Common phrase: 发高烧 “to have/run a high fever.”

English Words: adverb: every one; each and every one
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们个个都高兴得跳了起来。
English Usage in a sentence: Every one of the children was so happy that they jumped up.
Notes: Emphasizes that every member of a group has the stated quality or action.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 老板答应月底把工钱发给大家。
English Usage in a sentence: The boss promised to pay everyone their wages at the end of the month.
Notes: Often used for payment to labourers or temporary/manual workers. 工资 is more general and formal.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 酒店为贵宾准备了特别的房间。
English Usage in a sentence: The hotel prepared special rooms for VIP guests.
Notes: Polite/formal term used in hospitality, events, and announcements.

English Words: fixed pattern: to cause someone to suffer a bad result
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这场大雨害得我们没法出门。
English Usage in a sentence: This heavy rain caused us to be unable to go out.
Notes: Usually followed by an unwanted result: 害得我迟到, 害得大家担心.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 谢谢你的好意，不过我自己可以处理。
English Usage in a sentence: Thank you for your kindness, but I can handle it myself.
Notes: Common phrase: 一番好意 “a kind intention.” It can be politely declined.

English Words:
noun: behind; at the back
noun: later; afterwards
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他坐在教室后头，没有注意到老师进来。
English Usage in a sentence: He was sitting at the back of the classroom and did not notice the teacher come in.
Notes: More colloquial than 后面. It can refer to position or a later point in time.

English Words: verb: to lose heart; to become discouraged
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 失败一次并不代表你应该灰心。
English Usage in a sentence: Failing once does not mean you should lose heart.
Notes: Common phrase: 别灰心 “don’t lose heart.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他发烧后一直觉得脑袋昏沉。
English Usage in a sentence: After getting a fever, he kept feeling groggy and heavy-headed.
Notes: Can describe a person’s mental state, weather, light, or atmosphere.

English Words: verb: to converse; to talk with each other
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 两人坐在咖啡店里交谈了很久。
English Usage in a sentence: The two talked in the café for a long time.
Notes: More formal than 聊天; emphasizes a two-way conversation.

English Words: adverb: as soon as possible; as quickly as possible
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请你尽快回复我的邮件。
English Usage in a sentence: Please reply to my email as soon as possible.
Notes: Common in requests, work messages, and everyday speech.

English Words:
verb: to marvel at; to exclaim in admiration
noun: amazement; admiration
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 游客们都为这座古老建筑而惊叹。
English Usage in a sentence: The tourists all marvelled at this ancient building.
Notes: Stronger than 觉得厉害; often used for impressive scenes, skill, beauty, or achievements.

English Words:
verb: to recover; to regain health
noun: recovery
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 医生说他很快就能康复。
English Usage in a sentence: The doctor said that he would recover soon.
Notes: Used mainly for recovery from illness or injury; more formal than 好起来.

English Words: verb phrase: to have enough time; to make it in time
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 别着急，我们还来得及赶上火车。
English Usage in a sentence: Do not worry; we still have time to catch the train.
Notes: Negative form 来不及 means “too late / not enough time.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 狮子正在寻找下一只猎物。
English Usage in a sentence: The lion is looking for its next prey.
Notes: Can be literal for animals, or figurative for a target/victim.

English Words: verb: to spread; to be passed down; to circulate
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个传说已经流传了几百年。
English Usage in a sentence: This legend has been passed down for hundreds of years.
Notes: Often used for stories, songs, customs, sayings, and rumours.

English Words: noun: house number; doorplate; address plaque
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请确认一下门牌号码是不是写错了。
English Usage in a sentence: Please check whether the house number was written incorrectly.
Notes: 门牌号 means “house number/address number.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 博物馆正在展出一幅世界名画。
English Usage in a sentence: The museum is exhibiting a famous world painting.
Notes: 名 means famous; often used for well-known paintings by notable artists.

English Words: noun: men and women; male and female
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这所学校招收男女学生。
English Usage in a sentence: This school admits both male and female students.
Notes: Common in notices, statistics, signs, and formal descriptions.

English Words: verb: to study; to attend school; to read aloud
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他小时候在乡下念书。
English Usage in a sentence: He went to school in the countryside when he was young.
Notes: In this sense, it commonly means “to go to school/study,” especially in spoken Chinese.

English Words: adjective: poor; impoverished; from a poor family
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他虽然家境贫寒，却一直努力念书。
English Usage in a sentence: Although his family was poor, he always studied hard.
Notes: More literary/formal than 穷; commonly used as 家境贫寒.

English Words:
noun: chess piece; game piece
noun: pawn; tool used by others
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 在这场权力斗争中，他不想成为任何人的棋子。
English Usage in a sentence: In this power struggle, he did not want to become anyone’s pawn.
Notes: Literal for a board-game piece; figuratively, someone manipulated by another person.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 目前的情形比我们想象中复杂。
English Usage in a sentence: The current situation is more complicated than we imagined.
Notes: Similar to 情况, but often used in more descriptive or formal wording.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这颗卫星是人造的，不是天然形成的。
English Usage in a sentence: This satellite is man-made, not naturally formed.
Notes: Common compounds include 人造卫星 “artificial satellite” and 人造材料 “synthetic material.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 每个人都有自己的弱点。
English Usage in a sentence: Everyone has their own weaknesses.
Notes: Can describe a personal flaw, a weak spot, or a tactical vulnerability.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们在海边用沙子堆城堡。
English Usage in a sentence: The children used sand to build castles at the beach.
Notes: 沙 is also common, especially in compounds such as 沙滩 “beach.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你刚病好，要多注意身子。
English Usage in a sentence: You have just recovered from an illness, so take good care of your health.
Notes: More conversational than 身体; often refers to health or physical condition.

English Words: verb: to be interviewed; to receive an interview
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这位作家在受访时谈到了新书的创作过程。
English Usage in a sentence: This writer discussed the creation process of the new book during an interview.
Notes: Mainly used in news/reporting language. 受访者 means “interviewee.”

English Words: verb phrase: to count as; to be considered; to be regarded as
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这次旅行算是一次难忘的经历。
English Usage in a sentence: This trip counts as an unforgettable experience.
Notes: Often softens a statement: 算是吧 “I suppose so / you could say that.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 公主带着几名随从离开了城堡。
English Usage in a sentence: The princess left the castle with several attendants.
Notes: Common in historical and fantasy stories; not normally used for modern employees.

English Words: verb: to understand and show consideration for
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 希望你能体谅我的难处。
English Usage in a sentence: I hope you can understand and take my difficulties into consideration.
Notes: Usually means empathetically understanding another person’s situation.

English Words: noun: head; head section; upper part
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他在比赛中不小心撞到了头部。
English Usage in a sentence: He accidentally hit his head during the match.
Notes: More formal/medical than 头; also used for the front or upper section of an object.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他向来不喜欢在别人面前说大话。
English Usage in a sentence: He has never liked boasting in front of others.
Notes: Usually refers to a long-established habit or consistent pattern.

English Words: adjective: filial; dutiful to one’s parents
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她很孝顺，经常回家陪父母。
English Usage in a sentence: She is very filial and often goes home to spend time with her parents.
Notes: A culturally important value; usually describes respectful care for one’s parents or elders.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 小孩从斜坡上跑了下来。
English Usage in a sentence: The child ran down the slope.
Notes: Can describe a natural slope, ramp, or slanted surface.

English Words: suffix: specialist; scholar; expert in a field
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他是一位研究海洋生物的科学家。
English Usage in a sentence: He is a scientist who studies marine life.
Notes: Not normally used alone. It is a suffix in words such as 科学家 “scientist,” 文学家 “writer/literary figure,” and 语言学家 “linguist.”

English Words: verb: to provide for one’s old age; to support elderly parents
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他努力工作，希望以后能安心养老。
English Usage in a sentence: He works hard in hopes of being able to live comfortably in old age later.
Notes: Can mean planning/providing for one’s own old age or supporting elderly family members.

English Words: noun: nursing home; retirement home; elderly-care home
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她的奶奶住在附近的一家养老院。
English Usage in a sentence: Her grandmother lives in a nearby nursing home.
Notes: Refers to a residential care institution for elderly people.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 路边开满了五颜六色的野花。
English Usage in a sentence: The roadside was full of colourful wildflowers.
Notes: Literally flowers growing naturally in the wild; can also have a negative figurative meaning in some contexts, so use the literal meaning carefully.

English Words:
adjective: first-rate; top-class
noun: the top rank; first class
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家餐厅的服务是一流的。
English Usage in a sentence: This restaurant’s service is first-rate.
Notes: Can describe quality, skill, products, or people. 一流的 is very common.

English Words:
noun: duty; obligation
adjective: voluntary; unpaid
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 帮助有困难的人是我们应尽的义务。
English Usage in a sentence: Helping people in difficulty is a duty we should fulfil.
Notes: 义务劳动 means voluntary/unpaid labour; 权利和义务 means “rights and obligations.”

English Words: verb: to stay away from; to be far from
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 为了健康，你应该远离烟酒。
English Usage in a sentence: For your health, you should stay away from tobacco and alcohol.
Notes: Can mean physical distance or deliberately avoiding something harmful.

English Words: noun: a long queue; a long line resembling a dragon
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 演唱会门口排起了长龙。
English Usage in a sentence: A very long queue formed at the concert entrance.
Notes: A vivid expression for a long line of people, vehicles, or objects.

English Words: verb: to grasp; to master; to have under control
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她已经掌握了这项工作的基本方法。
English Usage in a sentence: She has already mastered the basic method for this work.
Notes: Can refer to knowledge, skills, information, timing, or control.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这些旧书都装在纸箱里。
English Usage in a sentence: These old books are all packed in cardboard boxes.
Notes: Usually a box made of cardboard.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 会议主席宣布会议正式开始。
English Usage in a sentence: The chairperson announced the official start of the meeting.
Notes: Title for the person presiding over a meeting or leading an organization.

English Words: noun: note; written message; slip of paper
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 桌上留着一张字条。
English Usage in a sentence: A note was left on the table.
Notes: Usually a short handwritten message.

English Words: verb: to paint; to create a drawing or painting
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他喜欢坐在窗边安静地作画。
English Usage in a sentence: He likes to sit by the window and paint quietly.
Notes: More literary than 画画; used for creating visual art.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 服务员把饮料放在托盘上端了过来。
English Usage in a sentence: The waiter brought the drinks over on a tray.
Notes: Common for trays used to carry food, drinks, or items.

English Words: verb phrase: to have a high fever; to run a high fever
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他昨天晚上突然发高烧了。
English Usage in a sentence: He suddenly developed a high fever last night.
Notes: 发烧 means “to have a fever”; 发高烧 specifically means a serious/high fever.

English Words: adverb: coming and going; back and forth
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 街上人来人往，非常热闹。
English Usage in a sentence: People were constantly coming and going on the street; it was very lively.
Notes: Often appears as 人来人往 for a busy place full of people.

English Words: noun: old people’s home; nursing home
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家老人院照顾了许多没有家人陪伴的老人。
English Usage in a sentence: This old people’s home cares for many elderly people without family companionship.
Notes: Used in Singapore and Malaysia. In Mainland Chinese, 养老院 is the more standard/common term.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们在雪地里堆雪人。
English Usage in a sentence: The children are building a snowman in the snow.
Notes: Refers to ground covered with snow, not simply “snow.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 风儿轻轻吹过树梢。
English Usage in a sentence: The breeze gently blew through the treetops.
Notes: 儿 adds a soft, poetic tone. In ordinary speech, say 风.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 清晨的森林里传来阵阵鸟语。
English Usage in a sentence: Bursts of birdsong came from the forest in the early morning.
Notes: Often appears in 鸟语花香, describing a pleasant natural setting.

English Words: fixed pattern: when walking; once someone starts walking
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他走起路来一瘸一拐的。
English Usage in a sentence: When he walks, he limps.
Notes: Used after a subject to describe the manner of walking: 她走起路来很快.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这里太危险了，快逃！
English Usage in a sentence: It is too dangerous here—run!
Notes: Common in urgent speech, games, and dramatic scenes. 快点逃 is slightly more complete.

English Words: verb: to exhaust; to use up completely
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他费尽力气才把箱子搬上楼。
English Usage in a sentence: He exhausted all his strength just to carry the box upstairs.
Notes: Usually followed by something: 费尽力气, 费尽心思, 费尽周折.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你怎能因为一次失败就放弃？
English Usage in a sentence: How can you give up because of one failure?
Notes: More emphatic and literary than 怎么能; often used in rhetorical questions.

English Words: verb: to place; to position; to set down properly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把这尊雕像安放在大厅中央。
English Usage in a sentence: Please place this statue in the centre of the hall.
Notes: Implies deliberately placing something in an appropriate position; more formal than 放.

English Words: adverb: on time; according to schedule
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请大家按时提交报告。
English Usage in a sentence: Please submit the report on time.
Notes: Usually means meeting a planned time. Do not confuse with 准时, which emphasizes punctuality at an exact time.

English Words: verb: to arrange; to place on display
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 书架上摆放着许多小说。
English Usage in a sentence: Many novels are arranged on the bookshelf.
Notes: Focuses on positioning or arranging objects neatly.

English Words: verb: to set out goods for sale; to sell from a stall
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 小贩在路边摆卖水果。
English Usage in a sentence: The vendor is selling fruit from a roadside stall.
Notes: Especially common in Singapore/Malaysia Chinese. In Mainland Chinese, 摆摊卖东西 is more usual.

English Words:
noun: decoration; ornament; display item
verb: to arrange; to set out
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这些古老的摆设让房间更有特色。
English Usage in a sentence: These old ornaments give the room more character.
Notes: As a noun, it can also mean something useless that only looks decorative: 只是个摆设.

English Words: verb: to set up a stall; to hawk goods from a stall
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他周末会去夜市摆摊卖小吃。
English Usage in a sentence: On weekends, he sets up a stall at the night market to sell snacks.
Notes: Common for informal market vending.

English Words: verb phrase: to set up a stall; to run a street stall
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她辞职后开始在市场摆摊子。
English Usage in a sentence: After resigning, she started running a stall at the market.
Notes: More conversational than 摆摊. 摊子 literally means “stall.”

English Words: verb phrase: to be unable to do; cannot manage to accomplish
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个要求太高了，我实在办不到。
English Usage in a sentence: This requirement is too demanding; I really cannot manage it.
Notes: Stronger than 不会 or 不行; means something is not feasible or beyond one’s ability.

English Words: noun: newspapers and magazines; the press
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这件事已经被各大报章报道了。
English Usage in a sentence: This matter has already been reported by major newspapers.
Notes: Common in Singapore/Malaysia Chinese. In Mainland Chinese, 报纸 or 报刊 is more common.

English Words: fixed expression: do not misunderstand; do not get the wrong idea
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 别误会，我不是在责怪你。
English Usage in a sentence: Do not misunderstand—I am not blaming you.
Notes: Used to prevent someone from interpreting your words or actions wrongly.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 现在说这件事不太方便。
English Usage in a sentence: It is not very convenient to discuss this matter right now.
Notes: Polite wording in phrases such as 不方便 and 如有不便，敬请原谅.

English Words: verb phrase: unwilling to admit defeat; competitive; unyielding
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她是个不服输的人，失败后会继续努力。
English Usage in a sentence: She is someone who refuses to admit defeat and will keep trying after failure.
Notes: Usually positive for determination, though it can imply stubborn competitiveness.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个决定实在不合情理。
English Usage in a sentence: This decision is truly unreasonable.
Notes: Means it does not accord with ordinary human feeling or sound reasoning.

English Words: adjective: unfilial; not dutiful to one’s parents
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他觉得自己没能照顾父母，是一种不孝。
English Usage in a sentence: He felt that failing to care for his parents was unfilial.
Notes: Strong, culturally loaded term related to filial piety; more common in serious or traditional contexts.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 不幸的是，比赛因为大雨取消了。
English Usage in a sentence: Unfortunately, the match was cancelled because of heavy rain.
Notes: Common phrase: 不幸的是 “unfortunately.” As a noun, it refers to a sad event or misfortune.

English Words: adjective: worthless; not worth much money
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这些旧东西不值钱，但对我很有纪念意义。
English Usage in a sentence: These old things are not worth much money, but they have great sentimental value to me.
Notes: Usually refers to low monetary value, not necessarily no personal value.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 奶奶用布袋装了几个苹果。
English Usage in a sentence: Grandmother put several apples into a cloth bag.
Notes: A bag made from cloth; in Singapore, 环保布袋 may refer to a reusable shopping bag.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她很有写作才华。
English Usage in a sentence: She has great talent for writing.
Notes: Often refers to intellectual, artistic, literary, or creative talent.

English Words: verb: to question; to inquire into; to investigate by asking
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 警察正在查问事情发生的经过。
English Usage in a sentence: The police are questioning people about what happened.
Notes: More formal and investigative than 问; often used by police, authorities, or in reports.

English Words:
adverb: throughout the year; year-round
adverb: for many years
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这里常年气候温暖。
English Usage in a sentence: The climate here is warm all year round.
Notes: Can describe a continuing state over the whole year or a long period.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 车轮陷进泥里了。
English Usage in a sentence: The wheel got stuck in the mud.
Notes: Usually refers to a vehicle wheel.

English Words: noun: sense of achievement; feeling of accomplishment
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 完成这个项目后，我很有成就感。
English Usage in a sentence: After completing this project, I feel a strong sense of achievement.
Notes: Very common when talking about motivation, work, studies, or hobbies.

English Words:
verb: to reach adulthood
adjective: adult; grown-up
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他今年已经成年了。
English Usage in a sentence: He has reached adulthood this year.
Notes: 成年 generally means reaching the legal age of adulthood; in China this is normally 18.

English Words:
verb: to soar into the sky
adjective: towering; sky-high
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 火箭拖着火焰冲天而起。
English Usage in a sentence: The rocket shot skyward trailing flames.
Notes: Often used in vivid descriptions: 火光冲天 “flames soaring into the sky”; 怒气冲天 “furious rage.”

English Words: verb: to come forward; to intervene; to appear personally
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这件事需要负责人亲自出面处理。
English Usage in a sentence: The person in charge needs to come forward personally to handle this matter.
Notes: Implies taking visible responsibility or personally dealing with an issue.

English Words: verb: to sell; to offer for sale
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家店出售各种旅行用品。
English Usage in a sentence: This shop sells all kinds of travel supplies.
Notes: More formal/commercial than 卖; common in advertisements and notices.

English Words: fixed expression: apart from this; besides this
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 除此，我们还需要考虑时间的问题。
English Usage in a sentence: Besides this, we also need to consider the issue of time.
Notes: Usually appears as 除此之外. Used alone, 除此 is less common and needs a following clause.

English Words: fixed expression: besides this; apart from that; in addition
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 除此以外，没有其他需要补充的内容。
English Usage in a sentence: Besides this, there is nothing else that needs to be added.
Notes: A formal connector used to add another point or exclude what was already mentioned.

English Words: verb: to spread; to become widely known
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个消息很快就在学校里传开了。
English Usage in a sentence: The news quickly spread throughout the school.
Notes: Usually used for news, rumours, stories, or information spreading among people.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把窗户关上，外面太吵了。
English Usage in a sentence: Please close the window; it is too noisy outside.
Notes: 窗户 is the standard everyday word; 车窗 specifically means a vehicle window.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他匆忙拿起外套就出门了。
English Usage in a sentence: He hurriedly picked up his coat and went out.
Notes: Often used as 匆忙地 + verb, or in the phrase 行色匆忙.

English Words: conjunction: thereby; thus; as a result
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们改进了流程，从而提高了工作效率。
English Usage in a sentence: We improved the process, thereby increasing work efficiency.
Notes: Formal connector showing a result caused by the preceding action; uncommon in casual speech.

English Words: verb: to save money; to deposit money
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我每个月都会存一点钱。
English Usage in a sentence: I save a little money every month.
Notes: Can mean saving cash or depositing money into a bank account.

English Words:
verb: to send away; to get rid of
verb: to pass time
verb: to deal with casually
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他看电影来打发无聊的下午。
English Usage in a sentence: He watches movies to pass a boring afternoon.
Notes: Meaning depends heavily on context. 打发人 can mean “send someone away,” sometimes dismissively.

English Words:
verb: to beat to death
adverb: absolutely; no matter what
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 打死我也不相信他会骗人。
English Usage in a sentence: No matter what, I will not believe that he would lie.
Notes: Literally means “beat to death,” but 打死……也…… is a common emphatic pattern meaning “absolutely not.”

English Words: verb: to hit the target; to strike
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他一枪打中了靶心。
English Usage in a sentence: He hit the bullseye with one shot.
Notes: Used when a shot, thrown object, or attack hits its intended target.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你要有胆量承认自己的错误。
English Usage in a sentence: You need the courage to admit your mistakes.
Notes: Similar to 胆子, but 胆量 sounds a little more formal.

English Words: adverb: in public; in front of everyone
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 老师没有当众批评他。
English Usage in a sentence: The teacher did not criticize him in front of everyone.
Notes: Often used when an action happens before a group of people.

English Words: verb phrase: to get into one’s hands; to obtain
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 奖金还没到手，他已经开始计划怎么花了。
English Usage in a sentence: The bonus is not in his hands yet, but he has already started planning how to spend it.
Notes: Often refers to money, goods, opportunities, or something finally obtained.

English Words: verb: to order dishes; to order food
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你们先点菜，我去接个电话。
English Usage in a sentence: You order the food first; I will take a call.
Notes: Used at restaurants. 点单 is also common, especially for ordering generally.

English Words: verb: to begin construction; to start work on a project
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这座新大楼下个月就要动工了。
English Usage in a sentence: Construction on this new building will begin next month.
Notes: Usually used for construction, renovation, engineering, or a substantial project.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 爷爷每天早上都有读报的习惯。
English Usage in a sentence: Grandfather has a habit of reading the newspaper every morning.
Notes: More literary/formal than 看报纸.

English Words: verb: to go on holiday; to vacation
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们计划暑假去海边度假。
English Usage in a sentence: We plan to go on holiday at the beach during summer vacation.
Notes: Usually implies travelling somewhere for rest and leisure.

English Words: noun: holiday home; vacation house; holiday cottage
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们在海边租了一间度假屋。
English Usage in a sentence: They rented a holiday home by the sea.
Notes: A house intended for short-term holiday stays.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这是一栋多层办公楼。
English Usage in a sentence: This is a multi-storey office building.
Notes: Can describe layers, floors, structures, systems, or packaging.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我不想去，一来太远，二来也没有时间。
English Usage in a sentence: I do not want to go: first, it is too far, and second, I do not have time.
Notes: Normally paired with 一来. It introduces the second reason in an explanation.

English Words: verb: to panic; to feel flustered or anxious
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 找不到手机时，他一下子发慌了。
English Usage in a sentence: When he could not find his phone, he suddenly panicked.
Notes: Usually describes an anxious, unsettled feeling when something goes wrong.

English Words: verb: to turn yellow; to become yellowed
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这本旧书的纸已经发黄了。
English Usage in a sentence: The pages of this old book have already turned yellow.
Notes: Common for aged paper, teeth, leaves, or white objects becoming yellow.

English Words: verb: to give out awards; to present prizes
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 学校将在下午的典礼上发奖。
English Usage in a sentence: The school will present awards at the afternoon ceremony.
Notes: 发奖金 means “give out bonuses”; 颁奖 is more formal for an award ceremony.

English Words: verb: to come from; to originate from
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这句感谢是发自内心的。
English Usage in a sentence: This gratitude comes from the bottom of my heart.
Notes: Most commonly used in 发自内心 “from the heart.”

English Words: noun: ticket; penalty notice; fine notice
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他因为违停收到了一张罚单。
English Usage in a sentence: He received a parking ticket for illegal parking.
Notes: Usually refers to an official notice requiring a fine to be paid.

English Words: verb: to turn pages; to leaf through a book
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她一边翻书，一边做笔记。
English Usage in a sentence: She turned the pages while taking notes.
Notes: Can mean turning pages or casually looking through a book.

English Words:
noun: dislike; aversion
verb: to dislike; to resent
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我对他这种说话方式很反感。
English Usage in a sentence: I strongly dislike his way of speaking.
Notes: Stronger than 不喜欢; often means someone’s words or behaviour make you uncomfortable.

English Words: verb: to go back on one’s word; to regret and change one’s mind
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你已经答应了，不能现在反悔。
English Usage in a sentence: You have already agreed, so you cannot back out now.
Notes: Often has a negative tone, implying someone breaks a promise or prior decision.

English Words: adverb: to insist on; to be determined to
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他非要在下雨天出去跑步。
English Usage in a sentence: He insists on going out for a run on a rainy day.
Notes: Implies insistence despite opposition, difficulty, or lack of necessity.

English Words: verb phrase: to be unable to distinguish; cannot tell apart
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这两个颜色太接近了，我分不清。
English Usage in a sentence: These two colours are too similar; I cannot tell them apart.
Notes: Can apply to people, sounds, directions, facts, or concepts.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家咖啡店在市中心开了新的分店。
English Usage in a sentence: This coffee shop opened a new branch in the city centre.
Notes: Main shop is 总店; 分店 is a branch.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 消防员奋勇冲进火场救人。
English Usage in a sentence: The firefighters bravely rushed into the fire to rescue people.
Notes: Often used in formal or heroic narration; common phrase 奋勇向前.

English Words: verb: to admit defeat; to concede
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他虽然输了比赛，却不肯服输。
English Usage in a sentence: Although he lost the match, he refused to admit defeat.
Notes: 不服输 means “refuse to concede / be unwilling to give up.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 那名妇人带着孩子站在路边。
English Usage in a sentence: The woman was standing by the roadside with her child.
Notes: More formal or old-fashioned than 女人. It can specifically imply an adult/married woman.

English Words:
verb: to be unable to catch up with
verb: to miss; to fail to make it in time
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们走快一点，不然赶不上末班车。
English Usage in a sentence: Let us walk faster, or we will miss the last bus.
Notes: Can mean failing to catch transport, failing to keep up, or not being as good as something else.

English Words: verb phrase: to be in a hurry; to race against time
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我现在赶时间，晚点再跟你说。
English Usage in a sentence: I am in a hurry right now; I will talk to you later.
Notes: Common when you have a deadline or need to arrive somewhere quickly.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这部电影的结局非常感人。
English Usage in a sentence: The ending of this movie is very moving.
Notes: Used for stories, scenes, actions, speeches, or kindness that emotionally moves people.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这幅画以高价卖给了一位收藏家。
English Usage in a sentence: This painting was sold to a collector for a high price.
Notes: Can be neutral, or imply that something is overpriced depending on context.

English Words:
adjective: individual; particular; a small number of
adverb: individually
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 个别学生还没有交作业。
English Usage in a sentence: A small number of students have not submitted their homework yet.
Notes: Usually means only a few exceptions, not every person.

English Words: noun: common point; similarity; thing in common
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这两个人有很多共同点。
English Usage in a sentence: These two people have many things in common.
Notes: Opposite: 不同点 “differences.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 汤还在锅子里煮着。
English Usage in a sentence: The soup is still cooking in the pot.
Notes: More conversational/regional than 锅. In some contexts it can refer to a wok or cooking vessel generally.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这次的过错主要在我。
English Usage in a sentence: The fault for this incident lies mainly with me.
Notes: More serious than a small mistake; often implies responsibility or blame.

English Words: verb phrase: with tears in one’s eyes; holding back tears
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她含着泪向大家道别。
English Usage in a sentence: She said goodbye to everyone with tears in her eyes.
Notes: Often used in emotional narration. 含泪 means the same thing in a more compact literary form.

English Words: adjective: very annoyed; angry and frustrated
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他又忘了约定的时间，真让人好气。
English Usage in a sentence: He forgot the agreed time again—he is really annoying.
Notes: Colloquial, often used in 好气又好笑 “both annoyed and amused.”

English Words: noun: skilled person; capable hand; expert
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她做菜真是一把好手。
English Usage in a sentence: She is truly very skilled at cooking.
Notes: Common patterns: 一把好手 “an expert” and 干活的好手 “a capable worker.”

English Words: verb: to shout; to call out loudly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子在远处呼喊妈妈。
English Usage in a sentence: The child called out for his mother in the distance.
Notes: Usually louder and more urgent than 叫.

English Words: noun: flower stand; trellis; plant rack
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 院子里的花架上爬满了藤蔓。
English Usage in a sentence: The flower trellis in the yard was covered in vines.
Notes: Also figurative in 花架子: something decorative or impressive-looking but impractical.

English Words: verb: to give a cheerful farewell; to see off ceremonially
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 同事们为即将退休的经理举行了欢送会。
English Usage in a sentence: The colleagues held a farewell party for the manager who was about to retire.
Notes: More formal and positive than 送别; common for organised farewell events.

English Words: verb: to exchange for; to obtain in exchange
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他用多年的努力换取了今天的成功。
English Usage in a sentence: He exchanged years of hard work for today’s success.
Notes: Often figurative: use effort, sacrifice, or something given up to obtain a result.

English Words:
verb: to mix; to blend
adjective: mixed; blended
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把面粉和水混合在一起。
English Usage in a sentence: Please mix the flour and water together.
Notes: Can refer to physical substances, languages, groups, styles, or feelings.

English Words: noun: fire scene; site of a fire
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 消防员迅速冲进火场救人。
English Usage in a sentence: The firefighters quickly rushed into the fire scene to rescue people.
Notes: Usually refers to the place where a fire is actively burning or has occurred.

English Words: verb: to be selected; to be chosen
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她获选为今年的优秀员工。
English Usage in a sentence: She was selected as this year’s outstanding employee.
Notes: More formal than 被选上; common in announcements, competitions, and reports.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家医疗机构提供全天候服务。
English Usage in a sentence: This medical institution provides around-the-clock service.
Notes: Can refer to a company division, government body, school, medical provider, or other organized entity.

English Words: verb: to pretend to be; to disguise oneself as
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他假扮成送货员进入大楼。
English Usage in a sentence: He disguised himself as a delivery worker to enter the building.
Notes: Often used in stories, investigations, games, and role-play.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请勿疲劳驾车。
English Usage in a sentence: Please do not drive while fatigued.
Notes: More formal than 开车; common in road-safety notices and reports.

English Words: verb: to reduce; to alleviate; to lessen
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 适当休息可以减轻压力。
English Usage in a sentence: Appropriate rest can reduce stress.
Notes: Often used for pain, stress, burden, punishment, or severity.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 各国健儿在赛场上奋力拼搏。
English Usage in a sentence: Athletes from various countries competed with all their strength in the arena.
Notes: Common in sports reporting; sounds more formal and literary than 运动员.

English Words: verb phrase: to reason; to be reasonable; to explain with logic
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们先别生气，好好讲道理。
English Usage in a sentence: Let us not get angry first; let us talk things through reasonably.
Notes: Can mean reasoning with someone, or saying that someone is reasonable: 他很讲道理.

English Words: verb phrase: to explain clearly; to make clear
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你先把事情的经过讲清。
English Usage in a sentence: First, explain clearly what happened.
Notes: Often used when someone’s explanation needs to be clearer.

English Words: verb: to explain a question; to go through a problem
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 老师正在给学生讲题。
English Usage in a sentence: The teacher is explaining problems to the students.
Notes: Usually refers to a teacher explaining how to solve an exercise, test question, or homework problem.

English Words: verb phrase: to keep one’s word; to be trustworthy
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 做生意一定要讲信用。
English Usage in a sentence: In business, one must keep one’s word.
Notes: 信用 here means trustworthiness/credibility. Opposite idea: 不讲信用.

English Words:
verb: to compete; to contend with
noun: contest; confrontation
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 两支球队将在决赛中较量。
English Usage in a sentence: The two teams will compete in the final.
Notes: Can refer to sports, skills, strength, strategy, or a confrontation between opponents.

English Words: noun: Ministry of Education; Education Ministry
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 教育部发布了新的课程规定。
English Usage in a sentence: The Ministry of Education issued new curriculum regulations.
Notes: Usually an official government department. The exact English title varies by country.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请先到接待处登记。
English Usage in a sentence: Please register at the reception desk first.
Notes: Common in offices, hotels, hospitals, and event venues.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 在没有足够证据前，不要太早下结论。
English Usage in a sentence: Do not jump to a conclusion before there is enough evidence.
Notes: Common phrase: 下结论 “to draw/reach a conclusion.”

English Words: verb: to grip tightly; to hold firmly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子紧抓着妈妈的手不放。
English Usage in a sentence: The child held tightly onto his mother’s hand and would not let go.
Notes: Can be literal, or figurative: 紧抓机会 “seize an opportunity firmly.”

English Words: verb: to fulfil one’s responsibilities; to do one’s duty
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 作为老师，她一直很尽责。
English Usage in a sentence: As a teacher, she has always been very responsible.
Notes: Usually praises someone for conscientiously fulfilling a role or duty.

English Words: verb: to enter a room; to go indoors
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 外面下雨了，快进屋吧。
English Usage in a sentence: It is raining outside—come indoors quickly.
Notes: More specific than 进去: it means entering a house or room.

English Words: verb phrase: cannot withstand; cannot bear; cannot stand up to
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这座旧桥经不起太大的重量。
English Usage in a sentence: This old bridge cannot withstand too much weight.
Notes: Can describe physical resistance, emotional pressure, repeated use, or close examination.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个木制玩具设计得十分精巧。
English Usage in a sentence: This wooden toy is designed very exquisitely.
Notes: Emphasizes something small, delicate, skillfully made, and clever in design.

English Words:
adjective: fine; precise; detailed
verb: to refine; to make meticulous
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这件衣服的做工非常精细。
English Usage in a sentence: The workmanship of this clothing is very fine.
Notes: Focuses on precision and careful detail; common for craftsmanship, work, data, and management.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大家把文件整理得井然有序。
English Usage in a sentence: Everyone organized the files in perfect order.
Notes: Usually used as 井然有序. On its own, 井然 is uncommon.

English Words: verb: to admire; to hold in high esteem
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我很敬佩她面对困难时的勇气。
English Usage in a sentence: I greatly admire her courage in the face of difficulties.
Notes: Stronger and more respectful than 喜欢 or 佩服.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这副眼镜的镜片有点脏。
English Usage in a sentence: The lenses of these glasses are a little dirty.
Notes: Can refer to glasses lenses, camera lenses, or optical lenses.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们在酒楼为爷爷庆祝生日。
English Usage in a sentence: They celebrated Grandfather’s birthday at a Chinese restaurant.
Notes: Usually a traditional Chinese-style restaurant, often suitable for group meals and banquets.

English Words: fixed expression: according to an investigation; according to a survey
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 据调查，越来越多人选择在家工作。
English Usage in a sentence: According to a survey, more and more people are choosing to work from home.
Notes: Common in news, reports, articles, and formal presentations.

English Words:
noun: test paper; exam paper
noun: rolled-up item
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 老师正在批改学生的卷子。
English Usage in a sentence: The teacher is marking the students’ exam papers.
Notes: Most commonly means an exam/test paper. The other meaning depends on context, such as a rolled-up blanket or document.

English Words:
verb: to start construction
verb: to begin work after a break
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 春节假期结束后，公司今天正式开工。
English Usage in a sentence: After the Lunar New Year holiday, the company officially resumed work today.
Notes: For construction, it means work begins; for workplaces, it often means returning to work after a holiday.

English Words:
verb: to open one’s heart
adverb: freely; heartily
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大家开怀大笑，气氛十分轻松。
English Usage in a sentence: Everyone laughed heartily, and the atmosphere was very relaxed.
Notes: Common phrases: 开怀大笑 “laugh heartily” and 开怀畅谈 “talk openly.”

English Words:
verb: to open for business
verb: to begin doing business
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家新店下周正式开张。
English Usage in a sentence: This new shop officially opens for business next week.
Notes: Used for shops/restaurants beginning business. It can also refer to making one’s first sale: 今天还没开张.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 父亲习惯每天早上坐在阳台看报。
English Usage in a sentence: Father has a habit of sitting on the balcony to read the newspaper every morning.
Notes: Shorter and more conversational than 读报.

English Words: verb phrase: to see clearly; to make out clearly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这里太暗了，我看不清你的脸。
English Usage in a sentence: It is too dark here; I cannot see your face clearly.
Notes: Negative form 看不清 is especially common.

English Words:
verb: to align with; to keep in line with
verb: to emulate; to follow the example of
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们要向先进团队看齐。
English Usage in a sentence: We should follow the example of the advanced team.
Notes: Can be literal for lining up, or figurative for matching a standard or role model.

English Words: verb: to underestimate; to look down on
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你不要看轻自己的能力。
English Usage in a sentence: Do not underestimate your own ability.
Notes: Can mean undervaluing someone/something, or treating them with contempt.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 蛋糕已经放进烤箱了。
English Usage in a sentence: The cake has already been put into the oven.
Notes: Usually an oven for baking or roasting.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他的口才很好，很会说服别人。
English Usage in a sentence: He is very eloquent and good at persuading people.
Notes: Refers specifically to the ability to speak effectively and persuasively.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们坐快车去市中心，会更快到。
English Usage in a sentence: We will get to the city centre faster if we take the express train.
Notes: Usually an express train or bus that makes fewer stops. It can also contrast with 慢车.

English Words: noun: purpose of one’s visit; reason for coming
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请问您今天的来意是什么？
English Usage in a sentence: May I ask the purpose of your visit today?
Notes: Polite/formal term, often used when receiving a visitor.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 一位老妇坐在公园的长椅上。
English Usage in a sentence: An elderly woman was sitting on a park bench.
Notes: More literary and detached than 老太太; usually used in narration.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 那位老妇人每天都会来这里散步。
English Usage in a sentence: That elderly woman comes here for a walk every day.
Notes: Similar to 老妇 but slightly fuller. In direct polite address, 老太太 is usually safer.

English Words: noun: elderly gentleman; respected old man
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 那位老先生正在安静地看书。
English Usage in a sentence: That elderly gentleman is reading quietly.
Notes: A respectful way to refer to or address an older man.

English Words: verb phrase: to become exhausted; to be worn out
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你今天忙了一整天，肯定累坏了。
English Usage in a sentence: You have been busy all day; you must be exhausted.
Notes: 坏 here intensifies the result. Common patterns include 饿坏了, 吓坏了, 急坏了.

English Words:
noun: inside and outside
adverb: approximately; about
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他里外找了一遍，还是没找到钥匙。
English Usage in a sentence: He searched both inside and outside, but still could not find the key.
Notes: 里外 can mean “inside and outside,” or approximate quantity/time: 走了里外十分钟.

English Words: noun: board member; council member; director
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她是这个协会的理事之一。
English Usage in a sentence: She is one of the board members of this association.
Notes: A formal organizational role, often in associations, societies, charities, or companies.

English Words: adverb: sternly; harshly; in a severe voice
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 父亲厉声叫他马上回来。
English Usage in a sentence: Father sternly told him to come back immediately.
Notes: Used in narration to describe a severe, angry, or commanding tone of voice.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们因为工作原因长期分居两地。
English Usage in a sentence: They have lived separately in two places for a long time because of work.
Notes: Often used in phrases such as 两地分居 “living apart in different places.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 烈火很快吞没了整栋房子。
English Usage in a sentence: The blazing flames quickly engulfed the entire house.
Notes: More vivid and dramatic than 火; often used in news and narration.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 两国与邻国保持良好的关系。
English Usage in a sentence: The two countries maintain good relations with their neighbouring countries.
Notes: Used mainly in political, geographical, and news contexts.

English Words:
verb: to circulate; to be in circulation
verb: to distribute; to circulate commercially
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这本书目前已经在全国流通。
English Usage in a sentence: This book is currently in circulation nationwide.
Notes: Can refer to money, goods, information, blood, or transport moving/circulating.

English Words: noun: stairway entrance; bottom/top of the stairs
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他站在楼梯口等朋友下来。
English Usage in a sentence: He stood at the stairway entrance waiting for his friend to come down.
Notes: Refers to the area where a staircase begins, ends, or connects to a corridor.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 路途遥远，我们得早点出发。
English Usage in a sentence: The journey is long, so we need to leave early.
Notes: More literary than 路程; emphasizes the journey or route itself.

English Words: verb: to talk nonsense; to speak carelessly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你别乱说，他根本没有做过那种事。
English Usage in a sentence: Do not talk nonsense; he has never done that kind of thing.
Notes: Usually criticizes someone for saying untrue, careless, or inappropriate things.

English Words:
noun: green tea
noun: “green tea” person; fake-innocent/manipulative person
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我平时喜欢喝不加糖的绿茶。
English Usage in a sentence: I usually like drinking green tea without sugar.
Notes: Literal meaning is the drink. As internet slang, 绿茶/绿茶婊 describes someone perceived as acting innocent while being manipulative; it is insulting.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 门将扑出了对方的点球。
English Usage in a sentence: The goalkeeper saved the opponent’s penalty kick.
Notes: Football/soccer term. 守门员 is the more general everyday term.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 海边的夜景非常迷人。
English Usage in a sentence: The seaside night view is very captivating.
Notes: Can describe a person, voice, scenery, smell, or quality that strongly attracts people.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 做面包需要面粉、酵母和水。
English Usage in a sentence: Making bread requires flour, yeast, and water.
Notes: Usually wheat flour unless another type is specified.

English Words: noun: appearance; look; face; overall condition
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这座小镇的面貌这几年改变了很多。
English Usage in a sentence: The appearance of this small town has changed greatly in recent years.
Notes: Can describe a person’s appearance, or the overall state/character of a place or organization.

English Words:
noun: face; appearance
noun: true nature; real character
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 经过调查，这件事的真相终于露出了面目。
English Usage in a sentence: After investigation, the true nature of the matter was finally revealed.
Notes: Common phrases: 真面目 “true face/nature” and 面目全非 “changed beyond recognition.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 把面粉和水混合后揉成面团。
English Usage in a sentence: After mixing flour and water, knead it into dough.
Notes: Used in cooking and baking.

English Words:
noun: famous brand; designer brand
noun: name badge; nameplate
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她买了一双名牌运动鞋。
English Usage in a sentence: She bought a pair of brand-name sports shoes.
Notes: Most commonly means a well-known brand. In schools/events, 名牌 can mean a name badge, depending on context.

English Words: noun: maternal love; a mother’s love
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 母爱常常被认为是无私的。
English Usage in a sentence: A mother’s love is often regarded as selfless.
Notes: More literary and abstract than 妈妈的爱.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 毕业多年后，他回到母校参加校庆。
English Usage in a sentence: Many years after graduating, he returned to his alma mater for the school anniversary.
Notes: Refers to a school one previously attended, especially with affection or pride.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 仓库里堆着几个装货的木箱。
English Usage in a sentence: Several wooden crates for goods were piled up in the warehouse.
Notes: A box made of wood, often used for storage or transporting goods.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这块蛋糕上面有一层奶油。
English Usage in a sentence: This cake has a layer of cream on top.
Notes: In Mainland Chinese, 奶油 often means cream or butter depending on context. 黄油 specifically means butter.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这双鞋很耐穿，穿了两年还没有坏。
English Usage in a sentence: These shoes are very durable; they have not worn out after two years.
Notes: Usually describes clothes, shoes, or fabric that last well through repeated use.

pinyin: nǐ yī yán wǒ yī yǔ
English Words: fixed expression: everyone talks at once; people speak one after another
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大家你一言我一语地讨论起来。
English Usage in a sentence: Everyone started discussing it, each speaking one after another.
Notes: Describes lively group conversation, sometimes with people talking over one another.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 火场上方冒出了浓烟。
English Usage in a sentence: Thick smoke rose above the fire scene.
Notes: Often used in fire reports and vivid descriptions.

English Words:
verb: to favour one side; to be biased
adjective: partial; unfairly biased
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你不能因为喜欢弟弟就这么偏心。
English Usage in a sentence: You cannot be so biased just because you like your younger brother.
Notes: Often used when someone treats one child, person, or side more favourably than another.

English Words: noun: number of votes; vote count
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他的票数最多，因此当选了。
English Usage in a sentence: He received the most votes and was therefore elected.
Notes: Used for elections, competitions, polls, and voting results.

English Words:
verb: to rush into fire
verb: to fight a fire
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 飞蛾扑火，往往用来比喻明知危险却仍然前往。
English Usage in a sentence: A moth flying into a flame is often used as a metaphor for knowingly heading toward danger.
Notes: Most commonly appears in 飞蛾扑火. For firefighters extinguishing a fire, 扑救 or 灭火 is clearer.

English Words: verb: to fight; to extinguish; to rescue from danger
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 消防员正在全力扑救大火。
English Usage in a sentence: The firefighters are doing everything they can to fight the blaze.
Notes: Common in news reports for fighting fires or responding to disasters.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请在期限内提交申请。
English Usage in a sentence: Please submit the application within the deadline.
Notes: Often used for applications, contracts, payments, and formal requirements.

English Words: noun: the day before; previous day
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 比赛前一天，队员们都很紧张。
English Usage in a sentence: The day before the match, all the players were nervous.
Notes: Refers to the day immediately before a specified event or date.

English Words: verb: to feel fortunate; to be glad
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我很庆幸当时及时做出了决定。
English Usage in a sentence: I am very glad that I made the decision in time then.
Notes: Expresses relief or gratitude that something good happened or something bad was avoided.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他的球艺进步得很快。
English Usage in a sentence: His ball-playing skills have improved quickly.
Notes: Usually refers to skill in ball sports, especially table tennis, badminton, or football depending on context.

English Words: verb: to miss class; to be absent from a lesson
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他因为生病缺课了两天。
English Usage in a sentence: He missed two days of classes because he was ill.
Notes: Can refer to a student missing classes or a teacher failing to teach a scheduled lesson.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他准备得很充分，然而比赛还是输了。
English Usage in a sentence: He prepared thoroughly; however, he still lost the competition.
Notes: Formal written connector. In everyday speech, 但是 or 可是 is more natural.

English Words:
verb: to compromise; to make concessions
noun: concession; compromise
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 为了达成协议，双方都作出了一些让步。
English Usage in a sentence: To reach an agreement, both sides made some concessions.
Notes: Often used in negotiation, argument, politics, or conflict resolution.

English Words:
verb: to give up one’s seat
verb: to yield a position; step aside
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请给有需要的人让位。
English Usage in a sentence: Please give up your seat for people who need it.
Notes: Can be literal on public transport, or figurative for yielding a job, role, or position.

English Words: noun: human life; a person’s life
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 救人命是最重要的事。
English Usage in a sentence: Saving lives is the most important thing.
Notes: Often used in serious contexts involving safety, accidents, crime, or rescue.

English Words: noun: silhouette; figure of a person
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 远处的雾中出现了一个人影。
English Usage in a sentence: A human figure appeared in the distant fog.
Notes: Often used when a person is seen indistinctly, from far away, or in dim light.

English Words: verb: to tolerate and yield; to put up with for harmony
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 为了家庭和睦，她一直选择忍让。
English Usage in a sentence: For the sake of family harmony, she has always chosen to tolerate and yield.
Notes: Usually means giving way patiently to avoid conflict; can imply enduring unfair treatment.

English Words: verb: to admit defeat; to concede
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 不到最后一刻，他绝不认输。
English Usage in a sentence: Until the very last moment, he will never admit defeat.
Notes: Similar to 服输. 认输 emphasizes openly accepting that one has lost.

English Words: fixed expression: as follows; the following
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 具体安排如下。
English Usage in a sentence: The specific arrangements are as follows.
Notes: Used before a list, explanation, or details in formal writing.

English Words: verb: to become absorbed; to be engrossed
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她看小说看得很入神，连我叫她都没听见。
English Usage in a sentence: She was so absorbed in the novel that she did not even hear me call her.
Notes: Common pattern: 看得入神, 听得入神, 想得入神.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 农民发现山猪跑进了田里。
English Usage in a sentence: The farmer discovered that a wild boar had run into the field.
Notes: 野猪 is the more standard/common word in Mainland Chinese. 山猪 is used regionally, including in Taiwan and some Southeast Asian contexts.

English Words: verb: to discuss; to deliberate; to consult about
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们明天开会商讨这个计划。
English Usage in a sentence: We will hold a meeting tomorrow to discuss this plan.
Notes: More formal than 讨论; often used for plans, solutions, and important decisions.

English Words: noun: body and mind; physical and mental well-being
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 运动对身心健康都有好处。
English Usage in a sentence: Exercise benefits both physical and mental health.
Notes: Common compounds: 身心健康, 身心疲惫.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家店最近的生意很好。
English Usage in a sentence: This shop’s business has been very good recently.
Notes: Can mean a business generally, a commercial deal, or how well a shop is doing.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 市镇理事会负责维护住宅区的公共设施。
English Usage in a sentence: The town council is responsible for maintaining public facilities in the residential area.
Notes: Common in Singapore/Malaysia-style local-government contexts; the exact responsibilities vary by country.

English Words: noun: defeated opponent; someone one has beaten
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他曾经是我的手下败将，这次却变得很强。
English Usage in a sentence: He was once an opponent I defeated, but this time he has become very strong.
Notes: A dramatic expression, often used in martial arts, games, sports, or fiction.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这张椅子坐起来很舒适。
English Usage in a sentence: This chair is very comfortable to sit in.
Notes: Can describe physical comfort, an environment, clothing, or a pleasant state.

English Words:
noun: aquatic animals; aquatic life
noun: the Shui ethnic group
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 水族馆里有许多不同种类的水族。
English Usage in a sentence: There are many different kinds of aquatic animals in the aquarium.
Notes: Usually refers to aquatic creatures in this context. 水族 can also specifically mean the Shui ethnic group in China; 水族馆 means “aquarium.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 地上散落着玻璃碎片。
English Usage in a sentence: Broken glass shards were scattered on the ground.
Notes: Can be literal broken pieces, or figurative fragments of memory or information.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 爷爷正在陪孙女玩积木。
English Usage in a sentence: Grandfather is playing with building blocks with his granddaughter.
Notes: Specifically a son’s daughter in traditional kinship terminology; for a daughter’s daughter, 外孙女 is used.

English Words: verb: to curry favour with; to try to please
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他总是讨好老板，希望得到升职。
English Usage in a sentence: He is always trying to please the boss in hopes of getting promoted.
Notes: Often has a negative tone, implying excessive or insincere attempts to please someone.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这件外套今天特价，只要五十元。
English Usage in a sentence: This coat is on special today and costs only fifty yuan.
Notes: Common in shops and advertisements. 特价商品 means “discounted/special-price goods.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她被提名为最佳女演员。
English Usage in a sentence: She was nominated for Best Actress.
Notes: Used in awards, elections, committees, and formal selection processes.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家餐厅的甜点很受欢迎。
English Usage in a sentence: The desserts at this restaurant are very popular.
Notes: Usually food served after a meal; 甜品 is also common, especially for sweet snacks/desserts.

English Words: verb: to obey; to follow someone’s advice or instruction
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你应该听从医生的建议，好好休息。
English Usage in a sentence: You should follow the doctor’s advice and rest properly.
Notes: Usually followed by advice, instructions, arrangements, or a person’s guidance.

English Words: verb: to share and enjoy together
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 让我们同享这份快乐。
English Usage in a sentence: Let us share and enjoy this happiness together.
Notes: Common in slogans, invitations, and polished writing. In everyday speech, 一起分享 is more natural.

English Words:
noun: deskmate; person sharing one’s desk
verb: to share a table
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我和他小学时是同桌。
English Usage in a sentence: He and I were deskmates in primary school.
Notes: Most commonly means a classmate who shares the same school desk.

English Words:
noun: brain; mind
noun: mental ability; thinking
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你先冷静下来，别让头脑发热。
English Usage in a sentence: Calm down first; do not let your head get carried away.
Notes: Can refer literally to the brain, or to intelligence and thought: 头脑清醒.

English Words: verb: to write or scribble on; to mark with writing
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请不要在墙上随意涂写。
English Usage in a sentence: Please do not scribble on the walls.
Notes: Usually refers to writing/marking casually on a surface, often where it should not be done.

English Words: verb: to promote; to implement; to put into effect
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 学校正在推行新的阅读计划。
English Usage in a sentence: The school is implementing a new reading programme.
Notes: Common for policies, systems, methods, and reforms.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 吃完饭后，我负责拖地。
English Usage in a sentence: After eating, I am responsible for mopping the floor.
Notes: Short for 拖地板; refers specifically to cleaning a floor with a mop.

English Words: verb phrase: to bend down; to stoop
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他弯下身捡起地上的钱包。
English Usage in a sentence: He bent down to pick up the wallet from the ground.
Notes: Similar to 弯腰, but it emphasizes bending one’s body downward.

English Words: verb: to be completed; to finish construction/work
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这座桥预计明年完工。
English Usage in a sentence: This bridge is expected to be completed next year.
Notes: Usually used for construction, engineering, renovation, or a substantial job.

English Words: noun: usual times; the past; normal routine
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 今天他比往常早到了半小时。
English Usage in a sentence: He arrived half an hour earlier than usual today.
Notes: Common pattern: 和往常一样 “as usual.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你为何突然决定离开？
English Usage in a sentence: Why did you suddenly decide to leave?
Notes: More formal/literary than 为什么. Common in writing and serious questions.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 贵的东西未必就是最好的。
English Usage in a sentence: Expensive things are not necessarily the best.
Notes: Used to challenge an assumption without saying it is definitely false.

English Words:
noun: questions and answers; Q&A
verb: to ask and answer
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 活动最后安排了一个问答环节。
English Usage in a sentence: A question-and-answer session was arranged at the end of the event.
Notes: Common in education, interviews, articles, and events.

English Words: verb: to find out clearly by asking
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我得先问明地址，才知道怎么去。
English Usage in a sentence: I need to find out the address clearly first before I know how to get there.
Notes: Usually means asking questions until a matter, fact, or reason becomes clear.

English Words: noun: wedding banquet; wedding celebratory drinks
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们周末要去喝朋友的喜酒。
English Usage in a sentence: We are going to attend a friend’s wedding banquet this weekend.
Notes: Common in Singapore/Malaysia and traditional Chinese usage. 喝喜酒 means attending a wedding meal/banquet.

English Words: verb: to enjoy a comfortable life; to enjoy good fortune
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 父母辛苦了一辈子，也该享福了。
English Usage in a sentence: Our parents worked hard all their lives; they should be able to enjoy a comfortable life now.
Notes: Often refers to living comfortably after hardship, especially in old age.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这是一次小型的社区活动。
English Usage in a sentence: This is a small-scale community event.
Notes: Used for events, machines, businesses, vehicles, and facilities.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我想向你表达我的谢意。
English Usage in a sentence: I would like to express my gratitude to you.
Notes: More formal than 谢谢. Common phrase: 表示谢意.

English Words: adjective: willing from the heart; content to do so
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我心甘情愿帮助你。
English Usage in a sentence: I am willing to help you from the bottom of my heart.
Notes: Usually used as 心甘情愿, meaning “entirely willing.” 心甘 alone is uncommon.

English Words: adjective: soft-hearted; easily moved to pity
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她看到流浪猫就会心软。
English Usage in a sentence: She becomes soft-hearted whenever she sees stray cats.
Notes: Can be positive for kindness, or negative when someone cannot be firm enough.

English Words: verb: to newly build; to construct anew
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这里新建了一所小学。
English Usage in a sentence: A primary school was newly built here.
Notes: Often used in construction, planning, and reports.

English Words: adjective: novel; new and unusual; curious
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子对这个新奇的玩具很感兴趣。
English Usage in a sentence: The child is very interested in this novel and unusual toy.
Notes: Describes something unfamiliar and interesting because it is new.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 做生意最重要的是讲信用。
English Usage in a sentence: In business, the most important thing is being trustworthy.
Notes: Can mean a person/company’s reliability, or financial credit: 信用卡 “credit card.”

English Words: verb: to rest and recuperate; to convalesce
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 医生建议他请假在家休养。
English Usage in a sentence: The doctor advised him to take leave and recuperate at home.
Notes: Usually after illness, injury, exhaustion, or a major operation.

English Words: noun: coast; shore; along the bank or coast
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 沿岸地区发布了暴雨警报。
English Usage in a sentence: Coastal areas issued heavy-rain warnings.
Notes: Can refer to areas along a sea, river, lake, or other body of water.

English Words: verb: to bite and injure; bite wound
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他被狗咬伤了手。
English Usage in a sentence: He was bitten on the hand by a dog.
Notes: Can be a verb or a noun-like description: 被咬伤 “was bitten/injured by a bite.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请按医生的指示服用药物。
English Usage in a sentence: Please take the medication according to the doctor’s instructions.
Notes: More formal/technical than 药. Can include prescription drugs and medical substances.

English Words: adjective: unacceptable; no good; should not be done
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这种浪费食物的行为很要不得。
English Usage in a sentence: This kind of food-wasting behaviour is unacceptable.
Notes: Used to criticize behaviour, habits, or attitudes that should not be accepted.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 田野里有一只野兔飞快地跑过去。
English Usage in a sentence: A wild rabbit ran quickly across the field.
Notes: Wild rabbit; hares are often also called 野兔 in everyday Chinese.

English Words: fixed expression: in the blink of an eye; before one knows it
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 一转眼，暑假就快结束了。
English Usage in a sentence: Before we knew it, summer vacation was almost over.
Notes: Emphasizes that time passes very quickly. Similar to 转眼间.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我小时候常去姨妈家玩。
English Usage in a sentence: I often went to my maternal aunt’s home to play when I was young.
Notes: Usually means one’s mother’s sister. In some regions, it can also euphemistically mean menstruation.

English Words: conjunction: so that; in order to make it easier to
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请留下联系方式，以便我们通知你。
English Usage in a sentence: Please leave your contact details so that we can notify you.
Notes: Formal connector used before the intended purpose or convenience.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他凭着坚强的意志完成了比赛。
English Usage in a sentence: He completed the competition through strong willpower.
Notes: Often refers to mental strength and determination in difficult situations.

English Words:
verb: to guide; to lead
noun: guidance
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 老师耐心地引导学生自己找到答案。
English Usage in a sentence: The teacher patiently guided the students to find the answer themselves.
Notes: Can be physical guidance, teaching guidance, or directing someone’s thinking/behaviour.

English Words: verb: to conduct business; to be open for business
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家店每天上午十点开始营业。
English Usage in a sentence: This shop opens for business at ten every morning.
Notes: Common on shop notices: 营业时间 “business hours” and 正在营业 “open.”

English Words:
noun: shadow
noun: trace; reflection; likeness
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 阳光下，他的影子被拉得很长。
English Usage in a sentence: In the sunlight, his shadow was stretched very long.
Notes: Can be literal, or figurative: 看不到……的影子 means “cannot see any trace of…”

English Words:
adjective: crowded; congested
verb: to crowd together
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 早上的地铁非常拥挤。
English Usage in a sentence: The metro is very crowded in the morning.
Notes: Describes crowded places, traffic, rooms, or people pressed closely together.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请大家有序排队进入会场。
English Usage in a sentence: Please line up orderly to enter the venue.
Notes: Often used in public notices and organized settings. 井然有序 is a stronger, more literary version.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这本书适合幼儿阅读。
English Usage in a sentence: This book is suitable for young children.
Notes: Usually refers to children below primary-school age.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她的孩子明年要上幼儿园。
English Usage in a sentence: Her child will start kindergarten next year.
Notes: Generally for preschool education before primary school.

English Words: verb: to reserve; to book in advance
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们已经预订了周六晚上的餐厅。
English Usage in a sentence: We have already booked a restaurant for Saturday night.
Notes: Common for hotels, flights, tickets, restaurants, and products. 订 is more casual.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请预先告诉我你的到达时间。
English Usage in a sentence: Please tell me your arrival time in advance.
Notes: More formal than 提前; often used in instructions and planning.

English Words: verb: to cross over; to go beyond; to surpass
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们越过小河，继续往前走。
English Usage in a sentence: They crossed the small river and continued forward.
Notes: Can be literal for crossing an obstacle, or figurative for exceeding a boundary or limit.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 花园里长满了杂草。
English Usage in a sentence: The garden is overgrown with weeds.
Notes: Refers to unwanted plants growing among crops, gardens, or paths.

English Words: noun: miscellaneous items; clutter; odds and ends
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请不要把杂物放在走廊里。
English Usage in a sentence: Please do not leave miscellaneous items in the corridor.
Notes: Common for assorted objects without a specific category, often things that create clutter.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 购买这款产品可以获得一份赠品。
English Usage in a sentence: Buying this product comes with a free gift.
Notes: Common in promotions and sales. A free sample can also be called 赠品.

English Words: verb: to occupy; to take up; to use
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个会议会占用你多少时间？
English Usage in a sentence: How much of your time will this meeting take up?
Notes: Can refer to taking up space, time, resources, equipment, or a phone line.

English Words: verb: to last as long as; to reach a length of
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这场演讲长达两个小时。
English Usage in a sentence: This speech lasted as long as two hours.
Notes: Usually followed by a duration, distance, number, or quantity. It emphasizes that the amount is notably large.

English Words: noun: true face; true nature; real identity
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 经过调查后，他终于露出了真面目。
English Usage in a sentence: After the investigation, his true nature was finally revealed.
Notes: Often used when someone’s hidden identity, motive, or character is exposed.

English Words:
adjective: calm; composed
verb: to calm oneself
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 遇到紧急情况时，你要保持镇定。
English Usage in a sentence: When facing an emergency, you need to remain calm.
Notes: Similar to 冷静, but often emphasizes not panicking in an urgent situation.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 正如你所说的，这个问题不能忽视。
English Usage in a sentence: Just as you said, this problem cannot be ignored.
Notes: Formal connector used to introduce agreement, comparison, or support for a point.

English Words: verb: to stop; to prevent; to put an end to
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 老师马上制止了两名学生的争吵。
English Usage in a sentence: The teacher immediately stopped the two students from arguing.
Notes: Usually means stopping improper, dangerous, or unwanted behaviour.

English Words: verb: to farm; to cultivate fields
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他的父母在乡下种田。
English Usage in a sentence: His parents farm in the countryside.
Notes: Specifically farming crops in fields. 种地 is also common.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他生了一场重病，需要长期休养。
English Usage in a sentence: He became seriously ill and needs a long period of recuperation.
Notes: Common phrase: 身患重病 “to suffer from a serious illness.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她的项链在灯光下泛着柔和的珠光。
English Usage in a sentence: Her necklace gave off a soft pearly lustre under the light.
Notes: Often appears in 珠光宝气, describing someone dressed in a glittering, luxurious way.

English Words:
verb: to be the main speaker
noun: principal speaker
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这场讲座由一位历史学家主讲。
English Usage in a sentence: This lecture is presented by a historian as the main speaker.
Notes: Often used for lectures, courses, talks, and seminars.

English Words: verb: to indicate clearly; to state; to specify
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请在表格上注明你的联系方式。
English Usage in a sentence: Please clearly state your contact details on the form.
Notes: Common in forms, documents, labels, and instructions.

English Words: noun: designated person; specially assigned staff member
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 公司安排专人负责接待来宾。
English Usage in a sentence: The company assigned dedicated staff to receive the guests.
Notes: Usually appears as 专人负责, 专人处理, or 专人接待.

English Words:
verb: to concentrate on; to focus on
adjective: focused; attentive
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她专注地听着老师的讲解。
English Usage in a sentence: She listened attentively to the teacher’s explanation.
Notes: Can describe focus on a task, a field, or a person’s concentrated state.

English Words: verb: to pass on a message; to relay
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请转告他，会议改到明天举行。
English Usage in a sentence: Please tell him that the meeting has been moved to tomorrow.
Notes: Used when asking someone to convey a message to another person.

English Words:
verb: to turn; to make a turn
noun: bend; turn
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 到了前面的路口左转弯。
English Usage in a sentence: Turn left at the intersection ahead.
Notes: Can be literal for roads/vehicles, or figurative: 说话别转弯抹角 “do not beat around the bush.”

English Words:
verb: to renovate; to decorate
noun: renovation; interior fitting-out
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这间店正在装修，下周才会开业。
English Usage in a sentence: This shop is being renovated and will not open until next week.
Notes: Usually refers to interior renovation or decoration of a home, office, or shop.

English Words:
verb: to pursue; to seek
noun: pursuit; aspiration
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他一直在追求更有意义的生活。
English Usage in a sentence: He has always pursued a more meaningful life.
Notes: Can refer to goals, ideals, love, career, knowledge, or material things.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大家自发组织了一次清洁活动。
English Usage in a sentence: Everyone spontaneously organized a cleaning activity.
Notes: Emphasizes that people acted on their own initiative, without being ordered.

English Words: adverb: always manages to; can always
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她总能在困难的时候想到办法。
English Usage in a sentence: She can always think of a solution in difficult times.
Notes: 总 adds the sense of “consistently/always,” often expressing admiration or a repeated pattern.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这间公寓的租金每个月很高。
English Usage in a sentence: The rent for this apartment is high every month.
Notes: Usually money paid for renting a home, room, shop, office, or land.

English Words:
verb: to block; to obstruct
noun: blockage; obstruction
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大雨导致道路严重阻塞。
English Usage in a sentence: Heavy rain caused severe road blockage.
Notes: Used for traffic, pipes, communication, blood vessels, and processes. 堵塞 is also common.

English Words: noun: ground floor of an HDB block; void-deck level
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 居民在组屋底层举行社区活动。
English Usage in a sentence: Residents held a community event on the ground floor of the HDB block.
Notes: Singapore term. 组屋 means HDB public housing; the bottom level often contains a void deck or shared facilities.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 每位组员都要负责一部分工作。
English Usage in a sentence: Every group member needs to be responsible for part of the work.
Notes: Used for school groups, project teams, committees, and other organized groups.

English Words: verb: to sit and stand; to move about restlessly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他因为担心结果而坐立不安。
English Usage in a sentence: He was so worried about the result that he could not sit still.
Notes: Usually used in 坐立不安 “too anxious/restless to sit still.” 坐立 alone is uncommon.

English Words: verb: to cook dishes; to prepare food
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我父亲周末喜欢在家做菜。
English Usage in a sentence: My father likes cooking at home on weekends.
Notes: Focuses on preparing dishes. 做饭 can more broadly mean preparing a meal.

English Words: verb: to cook; to prepare a meal
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 今天晚上轮到我做饭。
English Usage in a sentence: It is my turn to cook tonight.
Notes: Broader than 做菜; may include cooking rice and preparing the whole meal.

English Words: fixed expression: both annoyed and amused
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 看到他认真的表情，我真是又好气又好笑。
English Usage in a sentence: Seeing his serious expression, I was both annoyed and amused.
Notes: Used when someone’s actions are irritating but also funny.

English Words: verb: to use together; to use concurrently
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这两种方法可以并用，提高学习效率。
English Usage in a sentence: These two methods can be used together to improve learning efficiency.
Notes: Common in technical, medical, and formal writing. Means two or more things are used at the same time.

English Words: noun: work ID; employee identification card
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 进入办公区前请出示工作证。
English Usage in a sentence: Please show your employee ID before entering the office area.
Notes: Common in workplaces, restricted buildings, and security procedures.

English Words:
noun: major brand; famous name
noun: big star; important person
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这场演唱会请来了不少大牌歌手。
