English Usage in a sentence: This concert invited quite a few big-name singers.
Notes: Can mean a prestigious brand or a famous/influential person. Sometimes it implies someone acts arrogant because of their status.

English Words:
verb: to be unable to keep up with
verb: to fail to catch up
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 老师讲得太快了，我有点跟不上。
English Usage in a sentence: The teacher is speaking too fast; I am having trouble keeping up.
Notes: Can refer to speed, learning progress, trends, or physical movement.

English Words: verb: to love and care for one another
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 家人之间应该互爱互助。
English Usage in a sentence: Family members should love and help one another.
Notes: Not very common alone; it is most natural in the paired phrase 互爱互助.

English Words: verb: to help one another; mutual assistance
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 邻居之间应该互相帮助、互助友爱。
English Usage in a sentence: Neighbours should help one another and live in mutual friendship.
Notes: Common in community, school, workplace, and organizational contexts.

English Words: verb: to meet up; to join together; to converge
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们在地铁站出口会合吧。
English Usage in a sentence: Let us meet up at the metro station exit.
Notes: Used when people coming from different places meet at an agreed location.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 双方进行了激烈的讨论。
English Usage in a sentence: The two sides had an intense discussion.
Notes: Can describe competition, conflict, debate, movement, or emotion.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我有点急事，得马上离开。
English Usage in a sentence: I have an urgent matter and need to leave immediately.
Notes: Usually a personal matter requiring immediate attention.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 天气太热了，喝一杯冰水真解渴。
English Usage in a sentence: The weather is so hot; drinking a glass of iced water really quenches thirst.
Notes: Can be literal, or figurative: 解渴 for satisfying a strong desire.

English Words: verb: to start a class/course; to open a new cohort
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家培训中心下个月开班教中文。
English Usage in a sentence: This training centre will start a Chinese class next month.
Notes: Common for tuition centres, training courses, and organized lessons.

English Words: verb: to view; to regard; to treat as
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们应该怎样看待这个问题？
English Usage in a sentence: How should we view this issue?
Notes: Often used for opinions, attitudes, people, and situations.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 老师认为他的品行一直很好。
English Usage in a sentence: The teacher believes that his conduct has always been very good.
Notes: Refers especially to a person’s moral behaviour and character.

English Words: verb: to peek; to look secretly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他偷偷看了一眼手机上的消息。
English Usage in a sentence: He secretly glanced at the message on his phone.
Notes: Usually implies looking without permission or without wanting to be noticed.

English Words: verb: to reunite; to gather together as a family
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 春节是家人团聚的重要日子。
English Usage in a sentence: The Lunar New Year is an important time for families to reunite.
Notes: Usually refers to family members meeting again after being apart.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我买了两张周末演出的戏票。
English Usage in a sentence: I bought two tickets for this weekend’s performance.
Notes: Often refers to tickets for opera, theatre, or a stage performance. 演出票 is broader.

English Words: verb phrase: to be unable to understand; cannot make sense of
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我怎么也想不通他为什么这样做。
English Usage in a sentence: I simply cannot understand why he did this.
Notes: Often describes a mental block, confusion, or difficulty accepting something.

English Words: verb: to rent; to hire; to borrow for payment
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 游客可以在这里租借自行车。
English Usage in a sentence: Visitors can rent bicycles here.
Notes: Usually for temporarily using an item for a fee. 租 is more common in everyday speech.

English Words:
determiner: previous; earlier
prefix: some time before
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我前些天见过他一次。
English Usage in a sentence: I saw him once a few days ago.
Notes: Usually needs a following time word, such as 前些天 “a few days ago” or 前些年 “a few years ago.”

English Words: verb phrase: to be able to cope with; to be able to handle
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 工作虽然很多，但我还应付得来。
English Usage in a sentence: Although there is a lot of work, I can still handle it.
Notes: Focuses on whether one has enough ability, time, or energy to manage a situation.

English Words: adverb: actually; indeed; on the other hand
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个地方不大，倒是很安静。
English Usage in a sentence: This place is not big, but it is quite quiet.
Notes: Often introduces a contrast, correction, or unexpected positive point. Its exact translation depends on context.

English Words:
adjective: friendly; mild; amiable
noun: harmony; friendliness
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他待人很和气，大家都喜欢和他合作。
English Usage in a sentence: He is very friendly toward others, so everyone likes working with him.
Notes: Can describe a person’s manner or a peaceful atmosphere: 和和气气.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这是一项很有价值的研究。
English Usage in a sentence: This is a very valuable piece of research.
Notes: Can mean monetary value, practical usefulness, or intellectual/social worth.

English Words: fixed expression: that is true; that is a fair point
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: A：他做事很慢。B：那倒是，不过他很认真。
English Usage in a sentence: A: He works slowly. B: That is true, but he is very careful.
Notes: Used to acknowledge that the other person has made a valid point.

English Words: fixed expression: is no exception either
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这条规定对新员工也不例外。
English Usage in a sentence: This rule is no exception for new employees either.
Notes: Used after stating a general rule, to say that another person or thing is included too.

English Words: verb: to distinguish clearly; to tell apart clearly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你要分清事实和猜测。
English Usage in a sentence: You need to clearly distinguish facts from guesses.
Notes: Usually followed by two or more things that need to be distinguished.

pinyin: zhù rén wéi kuàilè zhī běn
English Words: fixed expression: helping others is the foundation of happiness
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 老师常告诉我们，助人为快乐之本。
English Usage in a sentence: The teacher often tells us that helping others is the foundation of happiness.
Notes: A moral saying. In everyday speech, 帮助别人会让人快乐 sounds more natural.

English Words: adverb: here; at this point; in this matter
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我在此向大家表示感谢。
English Usage in a sentence: I hereby express my thanks to everyone.
Notes: More formal than 在这里; common in letters, notices, and speeches.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你对自己太过严格了。
English Usage in a sentence: You are overly strict with yourself.
Notes: Often followed by an adjective or verb: 太过紧张, 太过相信.

English Words: verb: to fall ill; to contract a disease
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 长期熬夜容易得病。
English Usage in a sentence: Staying up late for a long time can easily make you ill.
Notes: More general than 生病; can imply catching or developing an illness.

English Words: fixed expression: to keep saying; to constantly mention
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: “谢谢”是她常常挂在嘴边的话。
English Usage in a sentence: “Thank you” is something she often says.
Notes: Often describes words, promises, complaints, or ideas that someone repeats frequently.

English Words: verb: to meet; to run into each other
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们明天中午在公司附近碰面吧。
English Usage in a sentence: Let us meet near the office tomorrow at noon.
Notes: More casual than 见面; can mean an arranged meeting or encountering someone.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他不小心撞到了脑后。
English Usage in a sentence: He accidentally hit the back of his head.
Notes: Common figurative phrase: 把……抛到脑后 “put something out of one’s mind.”

English Words:
verb: to ask for money
adjective: expensive; costly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这次修车很要钱。
English Usage in a sentence: This car repair is very expensive.
Notes: Usually means asking someone for money. In some regional/casual usage, 很要钱 means “very costly.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大自然中有许多奇妙的现象。
English Usage in a sentence: There are many wonderful phenomena in nature.
Notes: Describes something unusual, fascinating, and difficult to explain.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 观众席上坐满了来看比赛的人。
English Usage in a sentence: The spectator stands were full of people who came to watch the match.
Notes: Refers to seats or an area reserved for spectators.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把餐具放回原来的位置。
English Usage in a sentence: Please put the tableware back in its original place.
Notes: Includes items such as bowls, plates, cups, spoons, forks, and chopsticks.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大猩猩是体型最大的灵长类动物之一。
English Usage in a sentence: Gorillas are among the largest primates.
Notes: Do not confuse with 猩猩, which can refer more broadly to apes in everyday usage.

English Words:
noun: tour guide
verb: to guide a tour
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 导游正在向游客介绍这座古城的历史。
English Usage in a sentence: The tour guide is introducing the history of this ancient city to the tourists.
Notes: Can refer to the person or the activity of guiding tourists.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 学校东边有一个大公园。
English Usage in a sentence: There is a large park on the east side of the school.
Notes: More conversational than 东方 or 东部.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 古时的人们常用马车出行。
English Usage in a sentence: In ancient times, people often travelled by horse-drawn carriage.
Notes: More literary than 古代; used when describing the past in general.

English Words: verb: to practise martial arts; to train one’s skills
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他每天清晨都会到公园练功。
English Usage in a sentence: He goes to the park every morning to practise martial arts.
Notes: Often refers to martial-arts training, qigong, or traditional physical practice.

English Words:
noun: faucet; tap
noun: leader; leading position
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把水龙头关紧，别让水一直流。
English Usage in a sentence: Please turn off the tap tightly; do not let the water keep running.
Notes: 水龙头 means “faucet.” 龙头 can also mean the leader or leading company in an industry.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 外面正下着倾盆大雨。
English Usage in a sentence: It is pouring rain outside.
Notes: Usually used only in 倾盆大雨 “torrential rain.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们在院子里堆了一个雪人。
English Usage in a sentence: The children built a snowman in the yard.
Notes: Usually a figure made from snow.

English Words: noun: eye socket area; rim around the eyes
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她哭了很久，眼圈都红了。
English Usage in a sentence: She cried for a long time, and the rims of her eyes became red.
Notes: Common phrase: 眼圈红了, meaning someone is close to tears or has been crying.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 夜空中挂着一轮明月。
English Usage in a sentence: A bright moon hung in the night sky.
Notes: Used in descriptive writing; more poetic than 晚上的天空.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请点击页面右上角的按钮。
English Usage in a sentence: Please click the button in the top-right corner of the page.
Notes: Usually followed by 角: 右上角.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大厅中央有几根粗大的柱子。
English Usage in a sentence: There are several thick pillars in the centre of the hall.
Notes: Can refer to structural columns, poles, or posts.

English Words: verb: to hawk goods; to call out to sell
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 小贩在街边大声叫卖水果。
English Usage in a sentence: The vendor loudly called out to sell fruit by the roadside.
Notes: Usually refers to vendors attracting customers by shouting.

English Words: fixed expression: wish you; wishing you
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 祝您一路平安！
English Usage in a sentence: I wish you a safe journey!
Notes: Polite formula that needs something after it, such as 祝您健康, 祝您成功, or 祝您生日快乐.

English Words: noun: the whole night; all night
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他担心孩子的病情，整晚都没睡。
English Usage in a sentence: He was worried about the child’s illness and did not sleep all night.
Notes: Similar to 一整晚; emphasizes the entire night.

English Words: verb: to tear; to break; to damage accidentally
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我不小心把纸袋弄破了。
English Usage in a sentence: I accidentally tore the paper bag.
Notes: 弄 often implies causing something to happen, often accidentally.

English Words: noun: footpath; walking trail; pedestrian path
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 公园里修了一条新的步道。
English Usage in a sentence: A new walking path was built in the park.
Notes: Can refer to an urban pedestrian path or a nature/hiking trail.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 节日期间，街道两旁挂满了彩旗。
English Usage in a sentence: During the festival, colourful flags were hung along both sides of the street.
Notes: Often used to describe celebrations, parades, and festive scenes.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大熊猫主要生活在中国的山区。
English Usage in a sentence: Giant pandas mainly live in China’s mountainous regions.
Notes: Usually refers specifically to the giant panda; 熊猫 is common in everyday speech.

English Words: noun: egg roll; rolled wafer biscuit
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家店的蛋卷又香又脆。
English Usage in a sentence: This shop’s egg rolls are fragrant and crispy.
Notes: Can mean a rolled egg dish or a crisp rolled biscuit, depending on regional food context.

English Words: verb: to give the starting command; to issue an order
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 裁判举起发令枪，准备发令。
English Usage in a sentence: The referee raised the starting pistol, preparing to give the start signal.
Notes: Used especially in races and drills. 发令枪 means “starting pistol.”

English Words: verb: to go weak; to feel limp
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 看到那么高的地方，他的腿都发软了。
English Usage in a sentence: Seeing such a high place made his legs go weak.
Notes: Often describes legs/body becoming weak from fear, exhaustion, illness, or shock.

English Words: noun: monkey king; leader of a monkey group
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这群猴子里有一只特别强壮的猴王。
English Usage in a sentence: There is an especially strong monkey leader in this group of monkeys.
Notes: Can be literal, but often evokes Sun Wukong, the Monkey King from Journey to the West.

English Words:
verb: to time; to keep time
noun: timing; timekeeping
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 比赛开始后，工作人员马上开始计时。
English Usage in a sentence: After the match started, the staff immediately began timing it.
Notes: Common in sports, experiments, cooking, and timed activities.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 乐团今晚将演出一首著名的交响乐。
English Usage in a sentence: The orchestra will perform a famous symphony tonight.
Notes: Can refer to a symphonic work or symphonic music generally.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 长时间低头会让颈项感到酸痛。
English Usage in a sentence: Looking down for long periods can make the neck feel sore.
Notes: More literary/formal than 脖子. In medical writing, 颈部 is more common.

English Words: verb phrase: to take and give to; to bring to someone
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把这份文件拿给经理。
English Usage in a sentence: Please take this document to the manager.
Notes: Usually followed by the recipient: 拿给我, 拿给老师.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 天气这么热，喝一杯冰奶茶吧。
English Usage in a sentence: The weather is so hot—have a cup of iced milk tea.
Notes: Can mean tea with milk, or the sweet bubble-tea-style drink depending on context.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 两个孩子躲在角落里说悄悄话。
English Usage in a sentence: The two children were whispering in the corner.
Notes: Usually a quiet/private conversation intended not to be heard by others.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你还记得那本书的书名吗？
English Usage in a sentence: Do you still remember the title of that book?
Notes: 书名号 《 》 are the title marks used for books and other works in Chinese.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这条街有很多有名的小吃。
English Usage in a sentence: This street has many famous local snacks.
Notes: Often refers to inexpensive, casual local food rather than packaged snacks.

English Words: verb: to imitate; to copy someone’s manner
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 小孩子最喜欢学样大人说话。
English Usage in a sentence: Children especially like imitating the way adults speak.
Notes: More commonly heard in some regional varieties. 模仿 is the standard neutral word.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们在比赛中获得了亚军。
English Usage in a sentence: They won second place in the competition.
Notes: 冠军 is first place; 亚军 is second place; 季军 is third place.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们在湖边找到了一个适合露营的营地。
English Usage in a sentence: We found a campsite by the lake that was suitable for camping.
Notes: Can be for camping, military use, training, or organized activities.

English Words: fixed expression: to imitate what one sees; to follow an example blindly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子看到哥哥玩手机，也有样学样地拿起玩具电话。
English Usage in a sentence: The child saw his older brother using a phone and copied him by picking up a toy phone.
Notes: Often means imitating another person’s behaviour; it can be neutral, humorous, or mildly critical.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 答案显示在屏幕右下角。
English Usage in a sentence: The answer is displayed in the bottom-right corner of the screen.
Notes: Usually followed by 角: 右下角.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这碗面里有鱼圆和青菜。
English Usage in a sentence: This bowl of noodles contains fish balls and vegetables.
Notes: Common in Singapore/Malaysia Chinese. In Mainland Chinese, 鱼丸 is more common.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 长颈鹿用长长的脖子吃树叶。
English Usage in a sentence: Giraffes use their long necks to eat leaves from trees.
Notes: The standard word for giraffe.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请在表格左下角签名。
English Usage in a sentence: Please sign in the bottom-left corner of the form.
Notes: Usually followed by 角: 左下角.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我在日历上圈出了考试日期。
English Usage in a sentence: I circled the examination date on the calendar.
Notes: Also written as 日曆 in traditional Chinese.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 王后正在花园里散步。
English Usage in a sentence: The queen was taking a walk in the garden.
Notes: Usually the wife of a king in historical or fantasy settings.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 河面上漂着几片落叶。
English Usage in a sentence: Several fallen leaves were floating on the river’s surface.
Notes: Refers specifically to the top surface of a river.

English Words: verb: to lose baby teeth and grow adult teeth
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子六岁左右开始换牙。
English Usage in a sentence: Children begin losing their baby teeth and growing adult teeth at around six years old.
Notes: Usually refers to children replacing baby teeth with permanent teeth.

English Words: verb: to perform a dragon dance
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 春节期间，社区举行了舞龙表演。
English Usage in a sentence: During Lunar New Year, the community held a dragon-dance performance.
Notes: A traditional Chinese festive performance using a long dragon costume.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们排队玩滑梯。
English Usage in a sentence: The children lined up to play on the slide.
Notes: Usually the slide found in a playground.

English Words: noun: cooked rice; rice as a meal
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 今天晚饭有米饭、鱼和蔬菜。
English Usage in a sentence: For dinner today, there is rice, fish, and vegetables.
Notes: Refers to cooked rice. 大米 refers to uncooked rice grains.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 爷爷在菜园里种了很多青菜。
English Usage in a sentence: Grandfather grows many vegetables in the vegetable garden.
Notes: A garden used specifically for growing vegetables.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我的铅笔钝了，借我一下卷笔刀好吗？
English Usage in a sentence: My pencil is blunt; may I borrow your pencil sharpener?
Notes: Also called 削笔刀. Used to sharpen pencils.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 日本是一个著名的岛国。
English Usage in a sentence: Japan is a well-known island nation.
Notes: Used in geography and news for a country made up of one or more islands.

English Words: verb: to wave; to beckon with one’s hand
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她站在门口向我们招手。
English Usage in a sentence: She stood at the door and waved to us.
Notes: Can mean greeting someone with a wave or signalling them to come closer.

English Words: verb: to gather nectar; to collect honey
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 蜜蜂在花丛中忙着采蜜。
English Usage in a sentence: Bees are busy gathering nectar among the flowers.
Notes: Usually describes bees collecting nectar; people collect honey with 采蜂蜜.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们手拉手走进教室。
English Usage in a sentence: The children walked into the classroom hand in hand.
Notes: Can be literal, or figurative for cooperation and unity.

English Words: verb: to be rescued; to be saved
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 落水的孩子终于得救了。
English Usage in a sentence: The child who fell into the water was finally rescued.
Notes: Can refer to rescue from physical danger, or figuratively being saved from a difficult situation.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 邻里之间应该互相帮助。
English Usage in a sentence: Neighbours should help one another.
Notes: Refers collectively to people living nearby or the local neighbourhood relationship.

English Words: verb: to play in water; to splash around in water
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们在浅水区开心地戏水。
English Usage in a sentence: The children happily played in the shallow water.
Notes: Usually describes playful water activities, especially by children.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 冬天我们去山上滑雪。
English Usage in a sentence: In winter, we go to the mountains to ski.
Notes: Can refer to recreational skiing or the sport generally.

English Words: verb: to climb high; to climb up high places
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 小孩子不要随便爬高，容易受伤。
English Usage in a sentence: Children should not climb high places casually, because they can easily get hurt.
Notes: Often appears in warnings about climbing trees, furniture, or other high places.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 烤好的面包表面呈金黄色。
English Usage in a sentence: The surface of the baked bread is golden yellow.
Notes: Common for food, sunlight, crops, leaves, and other warm golden colours.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请在正确答案旁边画一个圆圈。
English Usage in a sentence: Please draw a circle beside the correct answer.
Notes: More conversational than 圆形; can also refer to a social circle in some contexts.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这件衬衫的领子有点脏。
English Usage in a sentence: The collar of this shirt is a little dirty.
Notes: Usually refers to the part around the neck of a shirt, jacket, or dress.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 故事里的仙女拥有神奇的力量。
English Usage in a sentence: The fairy in the story has magical powers.
Notes: Common in myths, fairy tales, and fantasy. It can also flatteringly describe a very beautiful woman.

English Words: noun: Dragon King; ruler of the waters
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 传说中，龙王住在海底的龙宫里。
English Usage in a sentence: In legends, the Dragon King lives in an underwater dragon palace.
Notes: A mythological Chinese deity who rules seas, rivers, or rain.

English Words: noun: sole of the foot; foot pad
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他走了很久，脚掌都疼了。
English Usage in a sentence: He walked for a long time, and the soles of his feet hurt.
Notes: Refers to the underside of the foot. 脚底 is more conversational.

English Words: verb: to become obsessed with; to become really fond of
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他最近迷上了摄影。
English Usage in a sentence: He has recently become really interested in photography.
Notes: Implied strong interest, sometimes bordering on obsession.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 王子即将继承王位。
English Usage in a sentence: The prince is about to inherit the throne.
Notes: Refers to the position and authority of a king or monarch.

English Words: verb: to claim; to collect as one’s own
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请失主到服务台认领遗失物品。
English Usage in a sentence: Owners of lost items, please claim them at the service counter.
Notes: Common for lost property, parcels, pets, awards, or responsibility.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 院子里种着几棵竹子。
English Usage in a sentence: Several bamboo plants are growing in the yard.
Notes: 竹 is also common, especially in compounds such as 竹林 “bamboo forest.”

English Words: verb: to dream of; to see in a dream
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我昨晚梦见小时候的朋友了。
English Usage in a sentence: I dreamed about a childhood friend last night.
Notes: Usually followed by a person, place, event, or thing seen in a dream.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这里没有的话，我们去别处找找。
English Usage in a sentence: If it is not here, let us look somewhere else.
Notes: More compact than 别的地方.

English Words: verb: to fetch water; to draw water
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 以前人们常到井边打水。
English Usage in a sentence: In the past, people often went to the well to fetch water.
Notes: Usually means obtaining water from a well, tap, or source. It can also mean bailing water out, depending on context.

English Words: noun: copper coin; ancient Chinese coin
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 博物馆里展出了许多古代铜钱。
English Usage in a sentence: The museum displayed many ancient Chinese copper coins.
Notes: Usually refers to traditional Chinese coins, often round with a square hole in the centre.

English Words: adverb: just by chance; it so happened
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我刚巧路过，就进来看看。
English Usage in a sentence: I happened to be passing by, so I came in to take a look.
Notes: Similar to 正好, but emphasizes coincidence.

English Words: noun: meal; cooked food and dishes
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 桌上的饭菜已经凉了。
English Usage in a sentence: The food on the table has already gone cold.
Notes: Refers collectively to rice/staple food and the dishes served with it.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 地铁站附近有一个卖旧书的书摊。
English Usage in a sentence: There is a bookstall selling second-hand books near the metro station.
Notes: A small stall or stand selling books, often temporary or outdoors.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 摊主热情地向我们介绍各种小吃。
English Usage in a sentence: The stall owner enthusiastically introduced the different snacks to us.
Notes: Refers to the person who owns or runs a market/roadside stall.

English Words: verb: to take a boat; to travel by boat
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们搭船到对面的岛上去。
English Usage in a sentence: We took a boat to the island opposite.
Notes: Common in Singapore/Malaysia Chinese. In Mainland Chinese, 坐船 is more common.

English Words: verb: to gesture; to demonstrate with hand movements
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他说不清楚，只好用手比画。
English Usage in a sentence: He could not explain it clearly, so he had to gesture with his hands.
Notes: Also written 比划. Can mean making gestures or informally comparing/trying something out.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把报告的页码检查一遍。
English Usage in a sentence: Please check the page numbers in the report once.
Notes: Used in books, documents, reports, and printing.

English Words: verb: to copy out by writing; to transcribe
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把这段课文抄写三遍。
English Usage in a sentence: Please copy out this passage three times.
Notes: Usually means copying text by hand.

English Words:
verb: to collect; to keep as a collection
noun: collection
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他喜欢收藏旧邮票。
English Usage in a sentence: He likes collecting old stamps.
Notes: Can refer to collecting physical objects or saving online content.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 元宵节时，人们常常猜灯谜。
English Usage in a sentence: During the Lantern Festival, people often solve lantern riddles.
Notes: Riddles traditionally written on lanterns, especially during the Lantern Festival.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 墙上的时钟已经停了。
English Usage in a sentence: The clock on the wall has stopped.
Notes: Usually a clock rather than a watch. 手表 means wristwatch.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个字谜的谜底是什么？
English Usage in a sentence: What is the answer to this Chinese-character riddle?
Notes: A riddle whose answer is usually a Chinese character or word.

English Words: noun: answer to a riddle; solution
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我想了很久，还是猜不出谜底。
English Usage in a sentence: I thought for a long time but still could not guess the answer to the riddle.
Notes: Specifically the answer/solution to a riddle.

English Words:
verb: to spin around in circles
verb: to run around frantically
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 为了准备活动，他忙得团团转。
English Usage in a sentence: He was running around frantically preparing for the event.
Notes: Often figurative: 忙得团团转 means being extremely busy and rushed.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 天气太热了，她拿着扇子不停地扇风。
English Usage in a sentence: The weather was too hot, so she kept fanning herself with a hand fan.
Notes: Usually a handheld fan, not an electric fan.

English Words: noun: column of water; jet of water
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 喷泉喷出高高的水柱。
English Usage in a sentence: The fountain sprayed out high columns of water.
Notes: A stream of water rising or shooting out in a column-like shape.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 衣服都放在卧室的柜子里。
English Usage in a sentence: All the clothes are kept in the cabinet in the bedroom.
Notes: A general word for storage furniture. Specific types include 衣柜 “wardrobe” and 书柜 “bookcase.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 妈妈准备了一桌丰盛的晚餐。
English Usage in a sentence: Mum prepared a plentiful dinner.
Notes: Most often describes meals with many good dishes; can also describe resources or harvests.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这碗汤里有几个肉丸。
English Usage in a sentence: There are several meatballs in this bowl of soup.
Notes: Usually balls made of minced meat. In some regional contexts, 肉圆 is also used.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 天气热的时候，我喜欢穿短袖。
English Usage in a sentence: When the weather is hot, I like wearing short sleeves.
Notes: Usually shorthand for a short-sleeved shirt: 短袖衬衫 / 短袖上衣.

English Words: verb phrase: to wish one could; to be dying to
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我恨不得马上飞到家里。
English Usage in a sentence: I wish I could fly home immediately.
Notes: Expresses a very strong wish to do something immediately.

English Words: verb: to tour; to visit for sightseeing
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们明天准备游览这座古城。
English Usage in a sentence: We plan to tour this ancient city tomorrow.
Notes: More formal than 逛; usually for visiting scenic, historical, or tourist places.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他的门牙掉了一颗。
English Usage in a sentence: One of his front teeth fell out.
Notes: Refers to the teeth at the front of the mouth.

English Words: verb: to hang upside down; to be inverted
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 蝙蝠倒挂在洞顶睡觉。
English Usage in a sentence: The bats hang upside down from the cave ceiling to sleep.
Notes: Can be literal or figurative, such as 价格倒挂 “an inverted price relationship.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 一只黄狗趴在门口晒太阳。
English Usage in a sentence: A yellow dog was lying at the entrance in the sun.
Notes: A literal description of a dog with yellow/tan fur.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 医生让他抬腿，检查膝盖有没有受伤。
English Usage in a sentence: The doctor asked him to lift his leg to check whether his knee was injured.
Notes: Can be literal, or part of a pattern such as 抬腿就走 “get up and leave immediately.”

English Words: noun: ice layer; layer of ice
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 湖面结了一层厚厚的冰层。
English Usage in a sentence: A thick layer of ice formed on the lake.
Notes: Refers to a continuous layer of ice on water, land, or another surface.

English Words: verb: to make fun of; to tease; to mock
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你不应该取笑别人的口音。
English Usage in a sentence: You should not make fun of other people’s accents.
Notes: Usually negative, especially when it embarrasses or hurts someone.

English Words: adjective: overly fond of playing; playful to excess
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他小时候很贪玩，不爱做作业。
English Usage in a sentence: He loved playing too much as a child and did not like doing homework.
Notes: Often used for children; mildly critical, implying play distracts from responsibilities.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大雨后，路边出现了很多积水。
English Usage in a sentence: After the heavy rain, a lot of standing water appeared by the roadside.
Notes: Common in weather reports and road-safety notices.

English Words: verb: to relocate; to move and settle elsewhere
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们去年移居到了澳大利亚。
English Usage in a sentence: They relocated and settled in Australia last year.
Notes: Usually implies moving one’s residence to another city or country for a longer period.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他举起酒杯向大家敬酒。
English Usage in a sentence: He raised his wine glass to toast everyone.
Notes: Usually a glass or cup used for alcoholic drinks.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这棵树还很矮小。
English Usage in a sentence: This tree is still short and small.
Notes: Can describe people, animals, plants, or objects. For people, it can sound blunt, so use carefully.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 祝您身体安康，万事如意。
English Usage in a sentence: I wish you good health and that everything goes well.
Notes: A formal, warm blessing, especially for elders or in written greetings.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请抓紧门的把手。
English Usage in a sentence: Please hold tightly onto the door handle.
Notes: Can refer to a door handle, drawer pull, or handle on a tool/container.

English Words: verb: to fill with displayed items; to be covered with
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 桌上摆满了生日礼物。
English Usage in a sentence: The table was filled with birthday presents.
Notes: Usually follows a location: 桌上摆满了…… “the table is covered with…”

English Words: verb: to keep warm; to retain heat
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 天气冷了，要多穿衣服保暖。
English Usage in a sentence: The weather has turned cold, so wear more clothes to keep warm.
Notes: Can describe clothing, buildings, food containers, or actions that prevent heat loss.

English Words: noun: stroke; brushstroke in a Chinese character
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: “永”字有五个基本笔画。
English Usage in a sentence: The character 永 has five basic strokes.
Notes: For Chinese character strokes. Do not confuse it with 比画 (bǐhua), “to gesture.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 墙上爬着一只小壁虎。
English Usage in a sentence: A small gecko was crawling on the wall.
Notes: A small lizard commonly found on walls in warm climates.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 高楼顶部通常装有避雷针。
English Usage in a sentence: The tops of tall buildings are usually fitted with lightning rods.
Notes: A metal conductor that protects a structure by directing lightning safely to the ground.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他用扁担挑着两桶水回家。
English Usage in a sentence: He carried two buckets of water home with a shoulder pole.
Notes: A pole balanced across the shoulders, traditionally used to carry loads at both ends.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我表妹今年刚上大学。
English Usage in a sentence: My younger female cousin just started university this year.
Notes: Usually a daughter of one’s mother’s sibling or father’s sister, who is younger than the speaker.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 学校门口贴着一张布告。
English Usage in a sentence: A public notice was posted at the school entrance.
Notes: More formal and old-fashioned than 通知; often a posted public announcement.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 将军命令部下做好准备。
English Usage in a sentence: The general ordered his subordinates to prepare.
Notes: Often used in military, historical, fantasy, or hierarchical settings.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把桌子擦洗干净。
English Usage in a sentence: Please scrub the table clean.
Notes: Combines wiping and washing; often used for cleaning surfaces or objects.

English Words: verb: to take apart; to unpack; to open up
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他把礼物盒拆开看里面是什么。
English Usage in a sentence: He opened the gift box to see what was inside.
Notes: Can mean opening packaging or dismantling an object into parts.

English Words: adverb: by the thousands; thousands of
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 成千上万的人来到现场观看表演。
English Usage in a sentence: Thousands upon thousands of people came to watch the performance.
Notes: Usually appears in 成千上万 “thousands upon thousands.” 成千 alone is less common.

English Words: verb: to remove; to get rid of; to eliminate
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们要想办法除掉这些杂草。
English Usage in a sentence: We need to find a way to get rid of these weeds.
Notes: Can mean removing unwanted things. For people/enemies, it sounds forceful and can imply killing.

English Words: verb: to wear; to dress oneself in
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 进入实验室前，请穿戴好防护装备。
English Usage in a sentence: Before entering the laboratory, please put on your protective equipment properly.
Notes: Usually refers collectively to clothing and accessories, especially proper or formal gear.

English Words: noun: hull; body of a boat/ship
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 船身在海浪中不断摇晃。
English Usage in a sentence: The body of the boat kept rocking in the waves.
Notes: Refers to the main physical body/hull of a vessel.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 过年前，家家户户都会贴春联。
English Usage in a sentence: Before Lunar New Year, every household puts up Spring Festival couplets.
Notes: Paired red banners with auspicious phrases, displayed during Lunar New Year.

English Words:
verb: to match; to pair; to combine
noun: matching combination; pairing
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她很会搭配衣服；这套黑白搭配简单却很好看。
English Usage in a sentence: She is very good at matching clothes; this black-and-white combination is simple but looks great.
Notes: Verb: 搭配衣服 / 搭配食材. Noun: 黑白搭配 / 颜色搭配.

English Words: verb: to answer correctly; to get right
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这道题你答对了。
English Usage in a sentence: You got this question right.
Notes: Opposite: 答错 “answer incorrectly.”

English Words: verb: to move; to touch emotionally; to win over
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她的故事深深打动了我。
English Usage in a sentence: Her story deeply moved me.
Notes: Usually refers to emotionally affecting someone; can also mean persuading/winning someone over.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个袋子的带子断了。
English Usage in a sentence: The strap on this bag has broken.
Notes: The exact meaning depends on context: a strap, ribbon, cord, or recording tape.

English Words: noun: that evening; the night in question
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 比赛结束当晚，队员们一起庆祝。
English Usage in a sentence: On the night the competition ended, the players celebrated together.
Notes: Refers to the evening/night of a specific day or event.

English Words: verb: to keep off rain; to shelter from rain
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这把伞太小了，挡不住雨。
English Usage in a sentence: This umbrella is too small to keep out the rain.
Notes: Usually refers to something physically protecting someone from rain.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请旅客按顺序登机。
English Usage in a sentence: Passengers, please board the aircraft in order.
Notes: Used at airports. 登机牌 means “boarding pass.”

English Words:
verb: to land; to come ashore
verb: to make landfall
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 飞机将在十分钟后登陆。
English Usage in a sentence: The aircraft will land in ten minutes.
Notes: For ships/people reaching land or aircraft landing. For signing into an account, use 登录, not 登陆.

English Words: verb: to ignite; to light a fire; to start an engine
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请先点火，再慢慢加热。
English Usage in a sentence: Please ignite the fire first, then heat it gradually.
Notes: Can refer to lighting a fire, igniting fuel, or starting a vehicle engine.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 现在是下午三点钟。
English Usage in a sentence: It is three o’clock in the afternoon now.
Notes: 点 is often enough in casual speech; 点钟 is a fuller spoken form.

English Words: noun: antithetical couplet; paired poetic inscription
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 门上贴着一副红色对联。
English Usage in a sentence: A pair of red couplets was pasted on the door.
Notes: Spring Festival couplets are called 春联; 对联 is the broader term for paired poetic lines.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把这张纸对折一次。
English Usage in a sentence: Please fold this sheet of paper in half once.
Notes: Also used for a 50% discount: 打对折 means “half price.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 学校生活可以是丰富多彩的。
English Usage in a sentence: School life can be rich and varied.
Notes: Can describe literal colours or figuratively varied experiences and culture.

English Words: verb: to amount to as many as; to reach as many as
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这次活动的参加者多达一千人。
English Usage in a sentence: The number of participants in this event reached as many as one thousand.
Notes: Usually precedes a surprisingly large number or quantity.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个问题有多重原因。
English Usage in a sentence: This problem has multiple causes.
Notes: Pronounced duōchóng when it means “multiple.” The same characters can be duōzhòng in questions such as 这个箱子有多重？ “How heavy is this box?”

English Words: verb: to work hard; to strive with determination
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他决定发奋学习，争取考上大学。
English Usage in a sentence: He decided to study hard and strive to get into university.
Notes: More literary than 努力; often used for determined effort in study or self-improvement.

English Words: verb: to finish work; to get off work
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我六点放工后再去找你。
English Usage in a sentence: I will come find you after I finish work at six.
Notes: Common in Singapore/Malaysia Chinese. In Mainland Chinese, 下班 is the usual term.

English Words: verb: to hurry on one’s journey; to travel quickly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 天快黑了，我们得赶路了。
English Usage in a sentence: It is getting dark, so we need to hurry on our way.
Notes: Usually means moving quickly to reach a destination on time.

English Words: verb: to sing loudly; to sing in praise of
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大家高唱校歌，为比赛加油。
English Usage in a sentence: Everyone sang the school song loudly to cheer for the competition.
Notes: Can be literal singing, or figurative in 高唱……的赞歌 “sing the praises of…”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 站在高处可以看得更远。
English Usage in a sentence: Standing in a high place lets you see farther.
Notes: Common phrase: 高处不胜寒, meaning high positions can feel lonely or difficult.

English Words: verb: to fly high; to soar
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 鸟儿张开翅膀，向天空高飞。
English Usage in a sentence: The bird spread its wings and soared into the sky.
Notes: Often used figuratively for pursuing lofty ambitions or leaving freely.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 城市里建起了许多高楼。
English Usage in a sentence: Many tall buildings have been built in the city.
Notes: Often means a tall building, especially in a city.

English Words:
noun: young master; son of a noble family
noun: polite form of address for a young man
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 那位公子衣着华丽；店主客气地问：“公子，您需要什么？”
English Usage in a sentence: The young master was elegantly dressed; the shopkeeper politely asked, “Sir, what do you need?”
Notes: Common in historical and fantasy settings. In modern speech, 先生 is more natural.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这次成功，大家都有功劳。
English Usage in a sentence: Everyone deserves credit for this success.
Notes: Often used to recognize someone’s contribution: 这是你的功劳.

English Words:
verb: to share; to share jointly
adjective: shared; common-use
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们可以共享这些资料；这间共享办公室供不同公司使用。
English Usage in a sentence: We can share these materials; this shared office is used by different companies.
Notes: Common in technology and services: 共享文件, 共享单车, 共享办公室.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 图书馆收藏了不少珍贵的古书。
English Usage in a sentence: The library has collected many valuable ancient books.
Notes: Usually refers to books or texts from ancient times, often historically valuable.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 远处传来阵阵鼓声。
English Usage in a sentence: Waves of drumbeats came from the distance.
Notes: Often used in festive, military, or dramatic descriptions.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 演讲结束后，观众热烈鼓掌。
English Usage in a sentence: After the speech ended, the audience applauded warmly.
Notes: Can show approval, encouragement, or celebration.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 几只海鸟在海面上飞翔。
English Usage in a sentence: Several seabirds were flying over the sea.
Notes: Refers to birds that live near or depend on the sea.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 天气太热，他只穿了一件汗衫。
English Usage in a sentence: The weather was so hot that he wore only an undershirt.
Notes: Often refers to a light sleeveless shirt or vest; 背心 is more common in many regions.

English Words:
noun: good shot; excellent play
interjection: great shot!
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他踢进了一个好球，观众都喊：“好球！”
English Usage in a sentence: He scored an excellent goal, and the audience all shouted, “Great shot!”
Notes: Common praise in ball sports for a skillful or successful play.

English Words: verb: to press one’s palms together
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他双手合十，向大家表示感谢。
English Usage in a sentence: He pressed his palms together to express his thanks to everyone.
Notes: Common in Buddhist, religious, respectful, or greeting contexts.

English Words: verb: to interconnect; to connect with each other
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这些设备可以通过网络互联。
English Usage in a sentence: These devices can interconnect through a network.
Notes: Often used in technology: 互联网 means “the Internet”; 互联互通 means interconnected access.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们跟着欢快的音乐跳舞。
English Usage in a sentence: The children danced to cheerful music.
Notes: Usually describes music, rhythm, mood, or movement.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 人们聚在一起欢庆新年的到来。
English Usage in a sentence: People gathered together to joyfully celebrate the arrival of the New Year.
Notes: More formal and festive than 庆祝.

English Words:
verb: to sway; to swing
verb: to wander around idly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 吊灯在风中晃荡；他整天在街上晃荡。
English Usage in a sentence: The hanging lamp swayed in the wind; he wandered around the streets all day.
Notes: The first meaning is physical swaying; the second is casually wandering without a clear purpose.

English Words:
verb: to reply by letter/message
noun: reply letter; reply message
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我今晚会回信；他的回信已经收到了。
English Usage in a sentence: I will reply tonight; his reply letter has already been received.
Notes: Traditionally for letters, but also used for replying to written messages or emails.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子最喜欢吃炸鸡腿。
English Usage in a sentence: The child likes eating fried chicken drumsticks the most.
Notes: Usually the lower leg/drumstick, though it may casually refer to a whole chicken leg.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孙女正在用积木搭房子。
English Usage in a sentence: The granddaughter is using building blocks to make a house.
Notes: Usually children’s blocks used for building shapes and structures.

English Words:
verb: to reduce the price; to discount
noun: price reduction; sale
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家店正在减价出售冬装；减价活动明天结束。
English Usage in a sentence: This shop is selling winter clothes at reduced prices; the sale ends tomorrow.
Notes: Similar to 降价. 特价 emphasizes a special promotional price.

English Words:
verb: to cut paper into designs
noun: Chinese paper-cut art
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 奶奶会剪纸；墙上贴着一幅红色剪纸。
English Usage in a sentence: Grandmother can make paper cuts; a red paper-cut artwork is pasted on the wall.
Notes: A traditional folk art made by cutting decorative patterns from paper.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 走到这条路的尽头，就能看到车站。
English Usage in a sentence: When you reach the end of this road, you will see the station.
Notes: Can refer to the end of a road, corridor, time period, or abstract process.

English Words: verb: to be in full bloom; to bloom all over
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 春天来了，花园里开满了鲜花。
English Usage in a sentence: Spring has arrived, and the garden is full of blooming flowers.
Notes: Usually used for flowers blooming densely over a place.

English Words:
noun: manual labourer
noun: hard physical labour
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 过去有些苦力靠搬运货物维生；搬这些箱子真是苦力活。
English Usage in a sentence: In the past, some manual labourers made a living carrying goods; moving these boxes is truly hard physical work.
Notes: Can sound old-fashioned or disrespectful when referring to a person; 体力劳动者 is more respectful/formal.

English Words:
adjective: tolerant; forgiving
verb: to tolerate; to forgive
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她很宽容，也愿意宽容别人的错误。
English Usage in a sentence: She is very tolerant and is willing to forgive other people’s mistakes.
Notes: Usually refers to being forgiving of faults, differences, or mistakes.

English Words:
noun: second child in a family
noun: number two; second-ranked person
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他是家里的老二；在这支队伍里，他是队长之后的老二。
English Usage in a sentence: He is the second child in his family; on this team, he is second only to the captain.
Notes: Can be a family-birth-order term or a casual label for second place/status.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 一颗泪珠从她的脸上滑下来。
English Usage in a sentence: A teardrop slid down her face.
Notes: A descriptive, poetic word for a tear.

English Words:
verb: to part; to say goodbye
noun: parting; separation
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 离别时，他们不舍地拥抱；这次离别让人难忘。
English Usage in a sentence: When parting, they hugged reluctantly; this separation was unforgettable.
Notes: More emotional and literary than 再见 or 分开.

English Words: verb: to resolve; to be determined to achieve an ambition
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他从小立志成为一名医生。
English Usage in a sentence: From a young age, he was determined to become a doctor.
Notes: Stronger and more formal than simply 想要; it implies a serious long-term ambition.

English Words: adjective: linked; interconnected; in a chain
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这是一起连环盗窃案件；孩子正在看连环画。
English Usage in a sentence: This is a series of linked theft cases; the child is reading a picture-story book.
Notes: Common in compounds: 连环画 “comic/picture-story book,” 连环案 “serial case,” 连环反应 “chain reaction.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 烈日下工作很容易中暑。
English Usage in a sentence: Working under the scorching sun can easily cause heatstroke.
Notes: More vivid than 阳光 or 太阳; usually describes strong summer sunshine.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 雨后路面很滑，开车要小心。
English Usage in a sentence: The road surface is slippery after the rain, so drive carefully.
Notes: Refers to the surface of a road, rather than the road as a whole.

English Words: fixed expression: someone soaked to the skin
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他忘了带伞，回家时淋得像落汤鸡。
English Usage in a sentence: He forgot to bring an umbrella and came home soaked to the skin.
Notes: A humorous comparison for a person completely soaked by rain or water.

English Words: fixed expression: at intervals of; every [period/distance]
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这班巴士每隔十五分钟来一趟。
English Usage in a sentence: This bus comes once every fifteen minutes.
Notes: Must be followed by a time, distance, or quantity interval.

English Words:
noun: dream; aspiration
verb: to dream of; to aspire to
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她的梦想是当老师；她梦想有一天能环游世界。
English Usage in a sentence: Her dream is to become a teacher; she dreams of travelling around the world one day.
Notes: Can refer to a personal life goal, not a dream experienced while asleep.

English Words: verb: to cover densely; to be densely distributed
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 夜空中密布着闪亮的星星。
English Usage in a sentence: The night sky was densely filled with shining stars.
Notes: Often used for clouds, stars, blood vessels, roads, or things spread densely across an area.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 明日的活动将在上午举行。
English Usage in a sentence: Tomorrow’s event will be held in the morning.
Notes: More formal/literary than 明天; often seen in notices, writing, and dramatic speech.

English Words: noun: Lunar New Year goods; New Year shopping
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 春节前，大家都会去市场买年货。
English Usage in a sentence: Before Lunar New Year, everyone goes to the market to buy New Year goods.
Notes: Includes food, decorations, gifts, and other items prepared for Lunar New Year.

English Words: verb: to get wrong; to mix up; to make a mistake with
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我弄错日期了，会议其实是明天。
English Usage in a sentence: I got the date wrong; the meeting is actually tomorrow.
Notes: Often used for names, dates, directions, facts, or objects being confused.

English Words:
noun: heating; central heating
noun: warm air
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 冬天房间里开着暖气，很舒服。
English Usage in a sentence: In winter, the heating is on in the room, which is very comfortable.
Notes: Usually refers to a heating system. In some contexts, it can literally mean warm air.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 婴儿正在地板上爬行。
English Usage in a sentence: The baby is crawling on the floor.
Notes: Used for babies, animals, vehicles moving slowly, or figuratively slow movement.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我只记得那部电影中的一个片段。
English Usage in a sentence: I remember only one fragment from that movie.
Notes: Can refer to a part of a film, text, memory, conversation, or period of time.

English Words: verb: to flutter; to wave in the wind
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 彩旗在风中飘扬。
English Usage in a sentence: The colourful flags fluttered in the wind.
Notes: Usually used for flags, hair, smoke, or fabric moving lightly in the wind.

English Words: verb: to judge fairly; to decide who is right
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你来给我们评评理，到底是谁不对？
English Usage in a sentence: Come and judge fairly for us—who exactly is in the wrong?
Notes: Often used when people are arguing and want a third party to judge.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他把钱袋放进了抽屉里。
English Usage in a sentence: He put the money bag into the drawer.
Notes: Usually a small bag for carrying coins or money; 钱包 is the modern everyday word for wallet.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们在青草上追逐玩耍。
English Usage in a sentence: The children ran and played on the green grass.
Notes: Often used in descriptive writing for fresh green grass.

English Words:
verb: to seek guidance; to learn from others’ experience
noun: to obtain Buddhist scriptures
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们去向经验丰富的同事取经；《西游记》中，唐僧去西天取经。
English Usage in a sentence: We went to learn from an experienced colleague; in Journey to the West, Tang Sanzang travels west to obtain Buddhist scriptures.
Notes: The figurative meaning “learn from others” is very common; the literal meaning is the famous Journey to the West reference.

English Words: verb: to name; to give a name to
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 父母给孩子取名为安宁。
English Usage in a sentence: The parents named their child Anning.
Notes: Usually used when naming a child, pet, shop, product, or project.

English Words:
adjective: daily-use; everyday
noun: daily necessities
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家店出售日用商品；牙膏是常见的日用品。
English Usage in a sentence: This shop sells everyday goods; toothpaste is a common daily necessity.
Notes: Usually appears in compounds such as 日用品 “daily necessities” and 日用百货.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们在海边的沙地上玩耍。
English Usage in a sentence: The children played on the sandy ground by the sea.
Notes: Refers to land or ground covered mainly in sand.

English Words:
noun: fool; idiot
noun: silly person; darling
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你这个傻瓜，怎么又忘了带钥匙？
English Usage in a sentence: You fool, how did you forget your keys again?
Notes: Can be a playful insult between close people, but can also be rude depending on tone.

English Words: verb: to dry in the sun; to sun-dry
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 妈妈把洗好的衣服拿到阳台晒干。
English Usage in a sentence: Mum took the washed clothes to the balcony to dry them in the sun.
Notes: 晒 means exposing something to sunlight; 晒干 emphasizes drying it completely.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 救护人员正在照顾事故中的伤者。
English Usage in a sentence: Paramedics are caring for the people injured in the accident.
Notes: Formal news/emergency term. 受伤的人 is more everyday.

English Words: verb: to be fooled; to be taken in; to fall for a trick
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 别相信这种广告，小心上当。
English Usage in a sentence: Do not believe this kind of advertisement; be careful not to get tricked.
Notes: Common phrase: 上当受骗 “to be deceived/scammed.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 学校每周一早上都会举行升旗仪式。
English Usage in a sentence: The school holds a flag-raising ceremony every Monday morning.
Notes: Common in schools, official ceremonies, and national events.

English Words: verb: to save money; to be economical
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 自己带午饭上班比较省钱。
English Usage in a sentence: Bringing your own lunch to work is more economical.
Notes: Focuses on spending less money, unlike 存钱 which means putting money aside as savings.

English Words: verb: to lose one’s hearing; to become deaf
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他因意外而失聪，但仍继续学习音乐。
English Usage in a sentence: He lost his hearing because of an accident, but still continued studying music.
Notes: A formal term for hearing loss. 听不见 is more everyday.

English Words: verb: to lose one’s sight; to become blind
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这场疾病可能导致失明。
English Usage in a sentence: This illness may lead to blindness.
Notes: A formal term for losing vision; often used in medical contexts.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他拜一位武术师父为师。
English Usage in a sentence: He became the apprentice of a martial-arts master.
Notes: Used for a master in martial arts, religion, traditional crafts, or apprenticeship. 师傅 is commonly used for tradespeople and drivers.

English Words: noun: people of the world; ordinary people
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他的作品受到世人的喜爱。
English Usage in a sentence: His work is loved by people around the world.
Notes: More literary than 人们; often used in philosophical, historical, or dramatic writing.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家店有很多不同式样的鞋子。
English Usage in a sentence: This shop has shoes in many different styles.
Notes: Similar to 款式; often used for clothing, objects, forms, and designs.

English Words: verb: to collect payment; to work as a cashier
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她在超市负责收银；顾客正在排队等候收银。
English Usage in a sentence: She is responsible for collecting payments at the supermarket; customers are queuing to check out.
Notes: Usually refers to taking payment at a shop. 收银员 means “cashier.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请到收银台付款。
English Usage in a sentence: Please pay at the checkout counter.
Notes: The place in a shop where customers pay.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 古人用兽皮制作衣物。
English Usage in a sentence: Ancient people used animal hides to make clothing.
Notes: Usually refers to animal skin/hide, often in historical, fantasy, or hunting contexts.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这只猫生病了，需要去看兽医。
English Usage in a sentence: This cat is ill and needs to see a veterinarian.
Notes: Professional term for an animal doctor.

English Words: verb: to lose to; to be defeated by
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们最后输给了更强的对手。
English Usage in a sentence: We ultimately lost to a stronger opponent.
Notes: Used for competitions, arguments, comparisons, or being surpassed by someone/something.

English Words: verb phrase: too numerous to count; countless
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 夜空中有数不尽的星星。
English Usage in a sentence: There are countless stars in the night sky.
Notes: Emphasizes a number so large that it cannot be counted.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子得了水痘，需要暂时在家休息。
English Usage in a sentence: The child has chickenpox and needs to rest at home for now.
Notes: A contagious viral illness, especially common in children.

English Words: noun: capital crime; crime deserving death
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 在古代，叛国常被视为死罪。
English Usage in a sentence: In ancient times, treason was often regarded as a capital crime.
Notes: Common in historical and fantasy settings. It can also be exaggerated humorously: 死罪可免，活罪难逃.

English Words:
noun: all four directions; all sides
noun: everywhere; all around
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 消息很快传到了四方；来自四方的游客聚集在这里。
English Usage in a sentence: The news quickly spread in all directions; tourists from all around gathered here.
Notes: Can mean east, west, south, and north, or people/places everywhere.

English Words: verb: to loosen; to let go of
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请松开我的手，我自己能走。
English Usage in a sentence: Please let go of my hand; I can walk by myself.
Notes: Opposite of 抓紧. Can apply to hands, knots, ropes, screws, or muscles.

English Words: verb: to take up a pen; to begin writing
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他提笔写下了给家人的第一封信。
English Usage in a sentence: He took up his pen and wrote his first letter to his family.
Notes: Often used for beginning to write, especially in narration or formal/literary writing.

English Words: noun: bowed string instrument; violin-family instrument
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她正在练习拉小提琴。
English Usage in a sentence: She is practising the violin.
Notes: 提琴 is a broad category. 小提琴 is violin; 中提琴 is viola; 大提琴 is cello.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 故事里的天使有一对白色翅膀。
English Usage in a sentence: The angel in the story has a pair of white wings.
Notes: Can be literal in religious/fantasy contexts or figurative for a very kind person.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他第一次跳伞时非常紧张。
English Usage in a sentence: He was very nervous the first time he went skydiving.
Notes: Can refer to military parachuting or recreational skydiving.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 工人用铁棒撬开了箱子。
English Usage in a sentence: The worker used an iron bar to pry open the box.
Notes: A solid bar/rod made of iron or metal.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她用一条头巾包住头发。
English Usage in a sentence: She wrapped her hair with a headscarf.
Notes: Can be worn for fashion, protection, work, or religious/cultural reasons.

English Words:
verb: to reunite as a family
noun: family reunion
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 中秋节是家人团圆的日子；今年我们终于能团圆了。
English Usage in a sentence: The Mid-Autumn Festival is a day for family reunion; this year we can finally reunite.
Notes: Usually refers to family members gathering after being apart.

English Words: verb: to bend over; to stoop
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他弯腰捡起了地上的书。
English Usage in a sentence: He bent over to pick up the book from the ground.
Notes: Can be literal or figurative: 弯腰道歉 “bow to apologize.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 祝你万事如意。
English Usage in a sentence: I wish that everything goes as you wish.
Notes: Usually appears in fixed expressions such as 万事如意 and 万事顺利.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 微风吹过，树叶轻轻摇动。
English Usage in a sentence: A gentle breeze blew past, making the leaves move softly.
Notes: More descriptive than 风; implies a light, pleasant wind.

English Words:
noun: the western paradise; Buddhist heaven
noun: the West, in Journey to the West
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 唐僧带着徒弟前往西天取经。
English Usage in a sentence: Tang Sanzang travelled west with his disciples to obtain Buddhist scriptures.
Notes: In Buddhist contexts, 西天 can mean the Western Paradise. In Journey to the West, it is the destination for obtaining scriptures.

English Words:
verb: to enter the water
verb: to launch a ship into water
noun: sewer/drainage water
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子还不敢下水游泳；新船今天正式下水。
English Usage in a sentence: The child still does not dare to enter the water to swim; the new ship was officially launched today.
Notes: The verb has different meanings depending on context. 下水道 means “sewer/drain.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们下周再讨论这个问题。
English Usage in a sentence: Let us discuss this issue again next week.
Notes: Refers to the week following the current one.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我在相册里找到了一张旧相片。
English Usage in a sentence: I found an old photograph in the album.
Notes: Common in Singapore/Malaysia and Taiwan. In Mainland Chinese, 照片 is more common.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这道咖喱用了很多香料。
English Usage in a sentence: This curry uses many spices.
Notes: Includes spices and aromatic ingredients used to add flavour or fragrance.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 刚出炉的面包香喷喷的。
English Usage in a sentence: The freshly baked bread smells wonderfully fragrant.
Notes: A vivid, informal description, especially for freshly cooked food.

English Words: noun: insight; understanding gained from experience
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 读完这本书后，请写下你的心得。
English Usage in a sentence: After reading this book, please write down your insights.
Notes: Refers to personal understanding or lessons gained through study, work, or experience.

English Words:
noun: new house; newly bought home
noun: bridal chamber; newlyweds’ room
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们刚搬进新房；婚礼当天，朋友们布置了新房。
English Usage in a sentence: They have just moved into their new home; on the wedding day, the friends decorated the newlyweds’ room.
Notes: The first meaning is common today. In wedding contexts, 新房 refers to the room/home prepared for newlyweds.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她是我大学的学妹。
English Usage in a sentence: She is a younger female schoolmate from my university.
Notes: Used by a student/alumnus to refer to a female student from the same school in a lower year.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他的眼睛不舒服，所以去眼科检查。
English Usage in a sentence: His eyes felt uncomfortable, so he went to the ophthalmology department for an examination.
Notes: The medical specialty/department for eye conditions.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这双靴子是用羊皮做的。
English Usage in a sentence: These boots are made of sheepskin.
Notes: Can refer to the skin/leather of a sheep. 羊皮纸 means “parchment.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 一群羊在山坡上吃草。
English Usage in a sentence: A flock of sheep is grazing on the hillside.
Notes: Refers collectively to a group of sheep.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 中药店里有各种各样的药材。
English Usage in a sentence: Chinese medicine shops have many kinds of medicinal ingredients.
Notes: Often refers to raw materials used in traditional Chinese medicine, rather than finished medicine.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他这周上夜班，白天需要睡觉。
English Usage in a sentence: He is working the night shift this week and needs to sleep during the day.
Notes: Opposite of 日班 “day shift.”

English Words:
noun: number one; first
noun: the first day of a month
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他是一号选手；我们约在十月一号见面。
English Usage in a sentence: He is contestant number one; we will meet on the first of October.
Notes: Can mean a number/rank, a date, or part of a name such as 一号线 “Line 1.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 仪仗队整齐地站在广场上。
English Usage in a sentence: The ceremonial guard stood neatly in the square.
Notes: Usually used in formal state, military, or ceremonial contexts. 仪仗队 means “honour guard.”

English Words:
verb: to hug; to embrace
noun: hug; embrace
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们见面后拥抱了一下；这个温暖的拥抱让她很感动。
English Usage in a sentence: They hugged when they met; this warm embrace moved her deeply.
Notes: Can be literal, or figurative: 拥抱变化 “embrace change.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 酒店的泳池晚上十点关闭。
English Usage in a sentence: The hotel swimming pool closes at ten at night.
Notes: Short for 游泳池.

English Words: verb: to use up completely; to exhaust
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他用尽力气才推开那扇门。
English Usage in a sentence: He used up all his strength just to push open that door.
Notes: Usually followed by a resource: 用尽力气, 用尽办法, 用尽积蓄.

English Words:
verb: to spend money
verb: to need money
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 买房很用钱，所以他们一直努力存钱。
English Usage in a sentence: Buying a home requires a lot of money, so they have been working hard to save.
Notes: Can mean spending money or requiring money. 花钱 is more common for a specific act of spending.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 古书旁放着一盏昏黄的油灯。
English Usage in a sentence: A dim oil lamp was placed beside the old book.
Notes: A lamp that burns oil; common in historical or old-fashioned settings.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我早餐喜欢喝豆浆配油条。
English Usage in a sentence: For breakfast, I like soy milk with fried dough sticks.
Notes: A long strip of deep-fried dough, often eaten for breakfast.

English Words:
noun: jade; jade stone
noun: valuable stone
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这块玉石在阳光下泛着温润的光。
English Usage in a sentence: This jade stone gave off a warm glow in the sunlight.
Notes: Can refer broadly to jade or valuable ornamental stone. 玉石俱焚 is a fixed expression meaning “perish together.”

English Words: verb: to care about; to mind; to attach importance to
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我不在乎别人怎么说。
English Usage in a sentence: I do not care what other people say.
Notes: Can mean caring deeply about someone/something, or minding an issue: 你在乎吗？

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这座城市过去以造船业闻名。
English Usage in a sentence: This city was once famous for its shipbuilding industry.
Notes: Can refer to the act of building ships or the shipbuilding industry.

English Words: verb: to block sunlight; to provide shade
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这顶帽子可以遮阳。
English Usage in a sentence: This hat can protect you from the sun.
Notes: Used for things that block direct sunshine: 遮阳伞, 遮阳帽, 遮阳板.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 救援直升机很快到达了现场。
English Usage in a sentence: The rescue helicopter quickly arrived at the scene.
Notes: The standard word for helicopter.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 明天中北部地区可能会有大雨。
English Usage in a sentence: The central and northern regions may experience heavy rain tomorrow.
Notes: Usually used in weather reports and geographic descriptions.

English Words: verb: to farm; to cultivate land
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 爷爷年轻时靠种地养家。
English Usage in a sentence: Grandfather supported his family by farming when he was young.
Notes: Similar to 种田. 种地 is broader and can include growing crops on any land.

English Words: noun: heavy labour; physically demanding work
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 搬这些家具是重活，不能一个人做。
English Usage in a sentence: Moving this furniture is heavy work and cannot be done by one person.
Notes: Refers to work requiring considerable physical strength.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她提着竹篮去市场买菜。
English Usage in a sentence: She carried a bamboo basket to the market to buy vegetables.
Notes: A basket woven from bamboo.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她目前是一名全职主妇。
English Usage in a sentence: She is currently a full-time homemaker.
Notes: Traditionally refers to a woman managing household work. 家庭主妇 is the fuller form.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他装作没看见，继续往前走。
English Usage in a sentence: He pretended not to see it and continued walking.
Notes: Often followed by a state/action: 装作不知道, 装作很镇定.

English Words: verb phrase: to bask in the sun; to get some sun
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 天气很好，我们去公园晒太阳吧。
English Usage in a sentence: The weather is nice; let us go to the park to bask in the sun.
Notes: Usually means sitting or resting in sunlight for warmth or enjoyment.

English Words: verb: to submit formally; to present for review
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请在截止日期前呈交申请表。
English Usage in a sentence: Please submit the application form before the deadline.
Notes: More formal than 提交; used for documents, reports, and applications.

English Words: verb: to present; to offer respectfully
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 学生们向老师呈献了一束鲜花。
English Usage in a sentence: The students presented a bouquet of flowers to the teacher.
Notes: Formal/respectful wording for offering something, especially in ceremonies or writing.

English Words: verb: to eat up completely; to finish all the food
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他很饿，一下子把饭都吃光了。
English Usage in a sentence: He was very hungry and quickly ate all the food.
Notes: Emphasizes that nothing is left. Also used figuratively for resources: 钱都花光了.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请帮我倒一杯水。
English Usage in a sentence: Please pour me a glass of water.
Notes: Usually means pouring water into a container. Depending on context, it can also mean pouring water out.

English Words:
verb: to protect against wind
adjective: windproof
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这件外套防风，适合在海边穿。
English Usage in a sentence: This jacket is windproof and suitable for wearing by the sea.
Notes: Common in clothing and building contexts: 防风外套, 防风玻璃.

English Words: verb phrase: to build a house
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们正在乡下盖房。
English Usage in a sentence: They are building a house in the countryside.
Notes: 盖 is a common everyday verb for constructing buildings.

English Words: determiner: all kinds of; various types of
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 商场里有各式各样的商品。
English Usage in a sentence: The shopping centre has all kinds of goods.
Notes: Usually appears in 各式各样 “of every kind.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 樱花是日本最具代表性的国花之一。
English Usage in a sentence: Cherry blossoms are among Japan’s most representative national flowers.
Notes: Refers to a flower symbolically associated with a country. Official status varies by country.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 能再次见到你，我是何其幸运。
English Usage in a sentence: How fortunate I am to be able to see you again.
Notes: A literary intensifier, usually used before an adjective: 何其美丽, 何其重要.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 湖水清澈得可以看见鱼。
English Usage in a sentence: The lake water is so clear that you can see the fish.
Notes: Refers to water in a lake.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 流星划过天空时，看起来像一个火球。
English Usage in a sentence: When the meteor crossed the sky, it looked like a fireball.
Notes: Can be literal, used in fantasy magic, or describe a very bright burning object.

English Words: verb: to guard the door; to watch over a place
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这只狗白天负责看门。
English Usage in a sentence: This dog is responsible for guarding the door during the day.
Notes: Can mean guarding an entrance or watching a house/place while others are away.

English Words:
noun: long-standing bad habit
noun: recurring old health problem
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他爱拖延是老毛病；一到下雨天，他的膝盖老毛病又犯了。
English Usage in a sentence: His habit of procrastinating is an old problem; whenever it rains, his old knee problem flares up again.
Notes: Can refer to an established personal flaw or a recurring medical issue.

English Words: verb: to sweat; to break into a sweat
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 天气太热了，他一直冒汗。
English Usage in a sentence: The weather is so hot that he keeps sweating.
Notes: Can result from heat, exercise, nervousness, fever, or fear.

English Words: noun: first line of a couplet; upper scroll
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请先读对联的上联，再读下联。
English Usage in a sentence: Please read the first line of the couplet before reading the second line.
Notes: In a Chinese couplet, the 上联 is the first/upper line, paired with 下联.

English Words: noun: second line of a couplet; lower scroll
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这副对联的下联写得很工整。
English Usage in a sentence: The second line of this couplet is written very neatly.
Notes: In a Chinese couplet, the 下联 is the second/lower line, paired with 上联.

English Words: verb: to raise pigs; pig farming
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他家以前靠养猪维持生活。
English Usage in a sentence: His family used to make a living by raising pigs.
Notes: Can refer to raising pigs as a farm activity or industry.

English Words: noun: medicine cost; medical drug expenses
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这次看病的药费不便宜。
English Usage in a sentence: The medication cost for this medical visit was not cheap.
Notes: Usually specifically the cost of medicine, separate from consultation or treatment fees.

English Words:
noun: one circle; one round
noun: one lap
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们绕着湖走了一圈；他的眼圈红了一圈。
English Usage in a sentence: We walked one lap around the lake; the area around his eyes turned red.
Notes: Can mean one complete loop/lap, or a ring-shaped area around something.

English Words: noun: sound of a bell; bell chime
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 远处传来了教堂的钟声。
English Usage in a sentence: The sound of church bells came from the distance.
Notes: Often used in descriptive writing, ceremonies, schools, or churches.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 农场里的猪舍每天都要清洗。
English Usage in a sentence: The pig pens on the farm need to be cleaned every day.
Notes: Refers to a building or enclosure for keeping pigs.

English Words: verb: to talk to oneself; to mutter
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他坐在窗边，自语着什么。
English Usage in a sentence: He sat by the window, muttering something to himself.
Notes: Usually appears in 自言自语 “talk to oneself.” 自语 alone is more literary.

English Words: noun: a hundred flowers; many flowers
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 春天来了，百花盛开。
English Usage in a sentence: Spring has arrived, and many flowers are in full bloom.
Notes: Often appears in fixed/literary phrases such as 百花齐放 and 百花盛开.

English Words: verb phrase: to hang high in the sky
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 一轮明月当空，照亮了小路。
English Usage in a sentence: A bright full moon hung high in the sky, lighting up the path.
Notes: Usually follows something in the sky: 明月当空, 烈日当空.

English Words: verb: to study diligently; to be diligent in learning
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他勤学好问，成绩一直很好。
English Usage in a sentence: He studies diligently and asks questions eagerly, so his grades have always been good.
Notes: Common in praise, school mottos, and formal writing.

English Words: verb: to frighten away; to scare off
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 突然的响声把鸟儿吓跑了。
English Usage in a sentence: The sudden sound frightened the birds away.
Notes: Usually means causing a person or animal to run away in fear.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们用雪堆了一间小雪屋。
English Usage in a sentence: The children built a small snow house out of snow.
Notes: Can describe any house made of snow; an Inuit-style ice house is commonly called an 冰屋.

English Words: verb: to hold up an umbrella; to use an umbrella
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 下雨了，你记得撑伞。
English Usage in a sentence: It is raining; remember to use an umbrella.
Notes: 撑 literally means holding something open/supporting it. Often used for umbrellas.

English Words: verb phrase: to put on shoes; to wear shoes
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 出门前记得穿鞋。
English Usage in a sentence: Remember to put on your shoes before going out.
Notes: 穿鞋 can mean putting shoes on or wearing shoes generally, depending on context.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们得先过河，才能到对面的村子。
English Usage in a sentence: We have to cross the river before we can reach the village on the other side.
Notes: Can be literal, or figurative in 过河拆桥 “tear down the bridge after crossing the river.”

English Words: verb: to be soaked by rain; to be rained on
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他没带伞，被雨淋得全身湿透。
English Usage in a sentence: He did not bring an umbrella and was soaked through by the rain.
Notes: Usually appears as 被雨淋 or 淋雨. 雨淋 alone is less common.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 爷爷每天早上都会去喂猪。
English Usage in a sentence: Grandfather goes to feed the pigs every morning.
Notes: 喂 means feeding animals or people who cannot feed themselves.

English Words: verb: to touch and find; to feel one’s way to
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 房间太黑了，我摸到墙边的开关才把灯打开。
English Usage in a sentence: The room was too dark, so I felt my way to the switch on the wall and turned on the light.
Notes: Emphasizes successfully finding something by touch, often when it cannot be seen.

English Words: verb phrase: to be unable to recognize
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你变化太大了，我差点认不出你。
English Usage in a sentence: You have changed so much that I almost did not recognize you.
Notes: Used when someone/something has changed so much that recognition is difficult.

English Words: verb phrase: to be unable to think of; cannot come up with
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我想不出一个合适的办法。
English Usage in a sentence: I cannot think of a suitable solution.
Notes: Usually followed by an answer, reason, idea, name, or solution.

English Words: noun: one sleep; a period of sleep
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我昨晚睡了一觉，今天精神好多了。
English Usage in a sentence: I had a sleep last night and feel much better today.
Notes: Common patterns: 睡一觉 “sleep for a while” and 一觉醒来 “upon waking up.”

English Words: fixed expression: so stupid; really silly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我居然把钥匙忘在家里，真笨！
English Usage in a sentence: I actually left my keys at home—so stupid!
Notes: Can be self-critical or teasing. Saying it directly to someone may sound insulting.

English Words: adverb: back; in the direction of where one came from
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 发现忘了拿手机后，他马上往回走。
English Usage in a sentence: After realizing he had forgotten his phone, he immediately walked back.
Notes: Usually used with movement verbs: 往回走, 往回跑, 往回拿.

English Words: noun: beside the pool; by the pond
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请不要在泳池边奔跑。
English Usage in a sentence: Please do not run by the swimming pool.
Notes: Can refer to the edge of a swimming pool, pond, or other body of water.

English Words: verb: to drop and break into pieces
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他不小心把杯子摔碎了。
English Usage in a sentence: He accidentally dropped the cup and broke it into pieces.
Notes: Usually implies something breaks because it falls or is thrown down.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们在院子里打水仗，玩得很开心。
English Usage in a sentence: The children had a water fight in the yard and had a great time.
Notes: Common phrase: 打水仗.

English Words: fixed expression: do not be afraid; do not worry
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 别怕，我会陪着你。
English Usage in a sentence: Do not be afraid; I will stay with you.
Notes: A reassuring phrase, often used to comfort someone.
