Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家餐厅的午餐套餐很划算。
English Usage in a sentence: This restaurant’s lunch set meal is good value.
Notes: Can refer to a meal combo or a package of services/products sold together.

English Words: verb: to exceed; to go beyond
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这次的费用超出了我们的预算。
English Usage in a sentence: The cost this time exceeded our budget.
Notes: Usually followed by a limit, range, expectation, or amount.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 农民辛勤地耕种土地。
English Usage in a sentence: The farmers cultivate the land diligently.
Notes: Often used to praise sustained hard work, especially by workers, parents, teachers, and farmers.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 传说这座岛上藏着宝藏。
English Usage in a sentence: Legend says that treasure is hidden on this island.
Notes: Usually valuable items such as gold, jewels, or historical artefacts. It can also figuratively mean something precious.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请在纸上画一个三角形图形。
English Usage in a sentence: Please draw a triangular shape on the paper.
Notes: Used in mathematics, design, computing, and diagrams.

English Words:
verb: to burn; to injure by heat
noun: burn injury
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他被热水烧伤了手；医生正在处理烧伤。
English Usage in a sentence: He burned his hand with hot water; the doctor is treating the burn injury.
Notes: Can be caused by fire, heat, steam, hot water, or chemicals.

English Words: verb: to use a plan/stratagem; to resort to a trick
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他用计把敌人引出了城。
English Usage in a sentence: He used a stratagem to lure the enemy out of the city.
Notes: Common in historical, military, and fantasy stories. 计 often implies a clever strategy or scheme.

English Words: verb: to obtain by deception; to swindle
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 骗子骗取了老人的钱财。
English Usage in a sentence: The scammer swindled the elderly person out of money.
Notes: Usually implies obtaining money, information, trust, or benefits dishonestly.

English Words:
verb: to occupy; to take control of
verb: to occupy/take up space
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 敌军占领了城市；这张桌子占领了太多空间。
English Usage in a sentence: The enemy army occupied the city; this table takes up too much space.
Notes: Can refer to military/political occupation or taking up physical/mental space.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 犯人被关在阴暗的牢房里。
English Usage in a sentence: The prisoner was kept in a dark jail cell.
Notes: More descriptive/literary than 监狱; specifically a room/cell for prisoners.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 消防员英勇地冲进火场救人。
English Usage in a sentence: The firefighter bravely rushed into the fire scene to rescue people.
Notes: Usually praises courage in dangerous or difficult circumstances.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 暴风雪导致许多道路关闭。
English Usage in a sentence: The blizzard caused many roads to close.
Notes: A severe storm with strong winds and heavy snow.

English Words: conjunction: in case; to guard against
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 出门时带把伞，以防下雨。
English Usage in a sentence: Bring an umbrella when going out in case it rains.
Notes: Usually followed by a possible problem: 以防万一, 以防下雨.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 村外有一口废弃的枯井。
English Usage in a sentence: There is an abandoned dry well outside the village.
Notes: A well that has dried up or no longer provides water.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她无私地帮助有困难的人。
English Usage in a sentence: She selflessly helps people in difficulty.
Notes: Often used to praise someone who acts without seeking personal benefit.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这首歌的节奏很欢快；你可以放慢工作的节奏。
English Usage in a sentence: The rhythm of this song is very lively; you can slow down the pace of your work.
Notes: Can refer to music, movement, speech, work, or life pace.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把鞋袜放进柜子里。
English Usage in a sentence: Please put the shoes and socks into the cabinet.
Notes: A collective term for shoes and socks.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这次活动吸引了众多游客。
English Usage in a sentence: This event attracted many tourists.
Notes: More formal than 很多; usually used for people, examples, choices, or items.

English Words:
adjective: upright; straight; well-proportioned
adjective: proper; correct
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请端正坐姿；他有端正的学习态度。
English Usage in a sentence: Please sit with proper posture; he has a proper attitude toward learning.
Notes: Can describe posture, facial features, handwriting, or a serious/correct attitude.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他闭目休息了一会儿。
English Usage in a sentence: He closed his eyes and rested for a while.
Notes: More literary than 闭上眼睛. It can also appear euphemistically in 闭目长眠, meaning to die.

English Words:
verb: to damage; to injure
noun: damage; injury
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 过度运动会损伤膝盖；医生检查了肌肉损伤。
English Usage in a sentence: Excessive exercise can damage the knees; the doctor examined the muscle injury.
Notes: Used for bodily injury, damage to equipment/materials, or harm to interests.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 石头击碎了窗户玻璃。
English Usage in a sentence: The stone shattered the window glass.
Notes: Usually means breaking something into pieces by striking it.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 医生说他的康复速度简直是个奇迹。
English Usage in a sentence: The doctor said that his recovery speed was practically a miracle.
Notes: Can describe an extraordinary event that seems almost impossible.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 战争给人们带来了深重的灾祸。
English Usage in a sentence: War brought severe calamity to people.
Notes: More serious and literary than 灾难; often refers to major suffering or misfortune.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 警车很快赶到了现场。
English Usage in a sentence: The police car quickly arrived at the scene.
Notes: A vehicle used by police officers.

English Words: noun: guns and artillery; firearms and cannons
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 战场上传来枪炮声。
English Usage in a sentence: The sound of guns and artillery came from the battlefield.
Notes: A collective term for weapons used in war.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请用盆子装一些水。
English Usage in a sentence: Please use a basin to hold some water.
Notes: A general container/basin, usually wider and larger than a bowl.

English Words: fixed expression: even a towering building starts from level ground
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 学习语言要一步一步来，万丈高楼平地起。
English Usage in a sentence: Learning a language must be done step by step; even a towering building starts from level ground.
Notes: Proverb stressing that great achievements begin with a basic foundation and gradual effort.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我去书局买了一本新书。
English Usage in a sentence: I went to the bookstore and bought a new book.
Notes: Common in Singapore/Malaysia and Taiwan. In Mainland Chinese, 书店 is more common; some 书局 are publishing houses.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她记性很好，很少忘记别人的名字。
English Usage in a sentence: She has a very good memory and rarely forgets people’s names.
Notes: Common patterns: 记性好, 记性差.

English Words: verb: to sell goods; to retail
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家店专门售货给附近居民。
English Usage in a sentence: This shop sells goods specifically to nearby residents.
Notes: More formal/old-fashioned than 卖东西. 售货员 means “salesperson/shop assistant.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家餐厅的炒墨鱼很好吃。
English Usage in a sentence: The stir-fried cuttlefish at this restaurant is delicious.
Notes: A marine animal related to squid; it releases dark ink when threatened.

English Words: verb: to dry and crack; to become fissured from dryness
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 天气太干，手指皮肤都干裂了。
English Usage in a sentence: The weather is so dry that the skin on my fingers has cracked.
Notes: Usually describes skin, soil, lips, wood, or paint becoming cracked because of dryness.

English Words:
verb: to set sail
verb: to begin a journey/venture
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 船在清晨起航；毕业后，他准备起航追求梦想。
English Usage in a sentence: The ship set sail in the morning; after graduation, he is ready to set out in pursuit of his dreams.
Notes: Literal for a ship departing, and figurative for starting a new stage or undertaking.

English Words: verb: to rush about; to travel around busily
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 为了照顾家人，他每天在两地之间奔波。
English Usage in a sentence: To care for his family, he travels busily between two places every day.
Notes: Implies tiring movement and effort, often for work, family, or responsibilities.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我隐约听见远处有钟声。
English Usage in a sentence: I faintly heard bell chimes in the distance.
Notes: Used when something can only barely be seen, heard, remembered, or understood.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这里的气候温和宜人。
English Usage in a sentence: The climate here is mild and pleasant.
Notes: Usually describes weather, scenery, environment, or atmosphere that makes people feel comfortable.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 你可以大胆提出自己的想法；他是个很大胆的人。
English Usage in a sentence: You can boldly put forward your ideas; he is a very daring person.
Notes: Can praise courage and initiative, though it may also imply taking a risk.

English Words: verb: to treat as; to regard as
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把这里当做自己的家。
English Usage in a sentence: Please treat this place as your own home.
Notes: Usually followed by a role/identity: 当做朋友, 当做礼物.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 门口挂着一块写有店名的木牌。
English Usage in a sentence: A wooden sign with the shop’s name is hanging at the entrance.
Notes: A sign or plaque made of wood.

English Words: verb: to avoid; to evade; to hide from
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他躲避着迎面而来的雨水。
English Usage in a sentence: He avoided the rain coming toward him.
Notes: Can refer to avoiding danger, people, responsibility, attacks, or unwanted situations.

English Words: noun: beside the wall; by a wall
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把箱子放在墙边。
English Usage in a sentence: Please put the box beside the wall.
Notes: Usually a location phrase: 墙边有…… “there is … by the wall.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子正在学习基本算术。
English Usage in a sentence: The child is learning basic arithmetic.
Notes: Mathematics involving basic number operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 雄壮的国歌在广场上响起。
English Usage in a sentence: The majestic national anthem rang out in the square.
Notes: Usually describes music, voices, mountains, scenery, or an impressive spirit.

English Words:
verb: to suspect; to distrust
noun: suspicion; doubt
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们因为误会而互相猜疑；猜疑会伤害朋友之间的关系。
English Usage in a sentence: They became suspicious of each other because of a misunderstanding; suspicion can hurt friendships.
Notes: Usually negative, implying distrust without clear proof.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 今天的天气糟透了。
English Usage in a sentence: Today’s weather is awful.
Notes: Strong informal expression. 糟透了 means “absolutely terrible.”

English Words:
verb: to remain still; to stop moving
adjective: stationary
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 画面突然静止了；静止的物体没有移动。
English Usage in a sentence: The image suddenly froze; a stationary object is not moving.
Notes: Used in science, video/media, and general descriptions of no movement.

English Words: verb: to be in prison; to serve a prison sentence
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他因犯罪被判坐牢。
English Usage in a sentence: He was sentenced to prison for committing a crime.
Notes: More conversational than 服刑; refers to being imprisoned.

English Words:
noun: fellow; buddy
noun: shop assistant; worker
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 伙计，过来帮我一下；店里的伙计正在整理货物。
English Usage in a sentence: Hey, buddy, come help me for a moment; the shop assistant is arranging the goods.
Notes: Can be a casual address, sometimes rough, or refer to an employee/assistant in a shop.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 古书里的掌柜正在柜台后算账。
English Usage in a sentence: The shopkeeper in the old story is calculating accounts behind the counter.
Notes: An old-fashioned term for the manager/owner of a shop, common in historical fiction.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 沙子的颗粒很细。
English Usage in a sentence: The grains of sand are very fine.
Notes: Small individual pieces of material, such as grains of sand, rice, powder, or soil.

English Words:
noun: style; shape; design
verb: to style; to shape
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这辆车的造型很特别；发型师正在给她造型。
English Usage in a sentence: This car’s design is very distinctive; the hairstylist is styling her hair.
Notes: Can describe the shape/design of an object or a person’s styled appearance.

English Words: verb: to arrive; to descend; to come upon
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 夜幕降临后，街上的灯都亮了。
English Usage in a sentence: After night fell, all the streetlights came on.
Notes: Often used for night, winter, disasters, opportunities, or important events arriving.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们应该尊重别人的选择；尊重是相处的基础。
English Usage in a sentence: We should respect other people’s choices; respect is the foundation of getting along.
Notes: Can refer to respecting people, opinions, rules, cultures, or personal boundaries.

English Words: verb: to extend; to stretch out
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这条公路一直延伸到远方。
English Usage in a sentence: This road extends all the way into the distance.
Notes: Can be physical, or figurative for extending an idea, topic, service, or influence.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们在海边的宾馆住了两晚。
English Usage in a sentence: We stayed for two nights in a hotel by the sea.
Notes: More common in Mainland Chinese; often a hotel or guesthouse.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他暗地里帮了我们很多忙。
English Usage in a sentence: He secretly helped us a lot.
Notes: Usually appears as 暗地里, meaning without others knowing.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 警方正在暗中调查这件事。
English Usage in a sentence: The police are secretly investigating this matter.
Notes: Similar to 暗地里, but more formal and often used in news or investigation contexts.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 运动会上，我们班赢了拔河比赛。
English Usage in a sentence: Our class won the tug-of-war contest at the sports meet.
Notes: A game/competition in which two teams pull opposite ends of a rope.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这袋白米可以煮很多碗饭。
English Usage in a sentence: This bag of white rice can cook many bowls of rice.
Notes: Common in Singapore/Malaysia. In Mainland Chinese, 大米 is more common.

English Words: verb: to fiddle with; to handle/play around with
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子一直摆弄桌上的玩具。
English Usage in a sentence: The child kept fiddling with the toys on the table.
Notes: Can be neutral for handling/arranging something, or mildly negative for playing with it unnecessarily.

English Words: verb: to pay a formal visit; to call on
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我明天会去拜会一位前辈。
English Usage in a sentence: I will pay a formal visit to a senior tomorrow.
Notes: More formal and respectful than 拜访 or 看望.

English Words: verb: to handle matters; to get things done
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他今天出门办事，下午才回来。
English Usage in a sentence: He went out to handle some matters today and will return in the afternoon.
Notes: Can mean handling personal/work affairs, or carrying out a task.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这枚戒指上镶着一颗蓝色宝石。
English Usage in a sentence: This ring is set with a blue gemstone.
Notes: A valuable decorative stone such as ruby, sapphire, or emerald.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 海上的暴风越来越强。
English Usage in a sentence: The storm at sea is becoming stronger and stronger.
Notes: Usually strong wind, often together with rain, snow, or waves.

English Words:
verb: to keep for future use
adjective: spare; backup
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请准备一把备用钥匙；这台电脑是备用的。
English Usage in a sentence: Please prepare a spare key; this computer is a backup.
Notes: Refers to something kept ready in case it is needed later.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 照片的背景是大海；先了解事件的背景再讨论。
English Usage in a sentence: The background of the photo is the sea; first understand the background of the event before discussing it.
Notes: Can be visual scenery or the historical/personal context behind something.

English Words:
verb: to memorize and recite a text
verb: to endorse; to vouch for
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 学生每天都要背书；这位专家愿意为产品背书。
English Usage in a sentence: Students have to memorize and recite texts every day; this expert is willing to endorse the product.
Notes: Most commonly means memorizing school text. Figuratively, it means publicly supporting or guaranteeing something.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 江水奔流不息。
English Usage in a sentence: The river water rushes on without stopping.
Notes: Usually describes fast-flowing water; it can figuratively describe time or powerful forces.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这项申请必须由本人提交。
English Usage in a sentence: This application must be submitted by the applicant in person.
Notes: Formal term used in forms, notices, and official speech.

English Words:
noun: tip of a pen/brush
noun: writing ability/work
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 笔头坏了，写不出字；他的笔头功夫很好。
English Usage in a sentence: The pen tip is damaged and cannot write; he is very skilled at writing.
Notes: Can mean the physical writing tip, or figuratively one’s writing skill.

English Words: noun: medical condition; state of an illness
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 医生说病人的病情已经稳定。
English Usage in a sentence: The doctor said the patient’s condition is now stable.
Notes: Used in medical contexts to describe how serious an illness is or how it is developing.

English Words: verb: to be critically ill; to be in critical condition
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 医生通知家人，老人已经病危。
English Usage in a sentence: The doctor informed the family that the elderly person is critically ill.
Notes: A serious medical term indicating life-threatening illness.

English Words:
verb: to remedy; to make up for
noun: remedial action

English Words: verb: to omit; to leave out; to abbreviate
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这句话省略了主语，但意思仍然清楚。
English Usage in a sentence: This sentence omits the subject, but its meaning is still clear.
Notes: Common in grammar, editing, and explanations of shortened information.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 句末的省略号表示说话还没有结束。
English Usage in a sentence: The ellipsis at the end of the sentence indicates that the speaker has not finished.
Notes: In Chinese typography, the standard ellipsis is usually six dots.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我按照食谱做了一道咖喱鸡。
English Usage in a sentence: I followed the recipe to make curry chicken.
Notes: Depending on context, it may mean one recipe, a recipe collection, or a dietary plan.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 警察用手势示意车辆停下。
English Usage in a sentence: The police officer signalled with a hand gesture for the vehicles to stop.
Notes: Can communicate instructions, meaning, or emotion.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 写作文前，老师让我们先列提纲。
English Usage in a sentence: Before writing the composition, the teacher asked us to make an outline.
Notes: An organized framework of the principal points in writing or a speech.

English Words:
verb: to omit; to overlook
noun: omission; oversight
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我不小心遗漏了一个名字；这处遗漏已经补上了。
English Usage in a sentence: I accidentally left out a name; this omission has now been corrected.
Notes: Implies that something was unintentionally left out.

English Words: noun: final; final part of a Chinese syllable
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: “妈”的声母是m，韵母是a。
English Usage in a sentence: In mā, the initial is m and the final is a.
Notes: A Mandarin phonetics term contrasting with 声母.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她穿着长裙，举止十分优雅。
English Usage in a sentence: She wore a long dress and behaved very gracefully.
Notes: Complimentary; may describe appearance, movement, behavior, or style.

English Words:
noun: radiance; brilliance; glory
adjective: glorious; brilliant
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 旭日发出耀眼的光辉；先贤留下了光辉的事迹。
English Usage in a sentence: The rising sun emitted dazzling radiance; the sages left behind glorious deeds.
Notes: Common figuratively in 光辉事迹, 光辉岁月, and 光辉形象.

English Words: verb: to pool or scrape together money
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大家一起凑钱给他买了一份礼物。
English Usage in a sentence: Everyone pooled their money to buy him a gift.
Notes: Implies gathering contributions or finding enough money from several sources.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 订书机里已经没有订书钉了。
English Usage in a sentence: There are no staples left in the stapler.
Notes: 订书机 means “stapler.”

English Words: verb: to hook fingers; to link hands with bent fingers
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 两个孩子勾手约定以后不再吵架。
English Usage in a sentence: The two children linked little fingers and promised not to quarrel again.
Notes: 拉钩 is the more common expression for making a pinky promise.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 护照封面上印着国徽。
English Usage in a sentence: The national emblem is printed on the cover of the passport.
Notes: A country’s officially recognized emblem.

English Words: verb: to recite or chant an incantation
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 巫师开始念咒，试图打开石门。
English Usage in a sentence: The sorcerer began chanting an incantation in an attempt to open the stone door.
Notes: Common in myths, fantasy stories, and religious or magical contexts.

English Words: verb: to apply fertilizer; to fertilize
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 农夫定期给菜园里的植物施肥。
English Usage in a sentence: The farmer regularly fertilizes the plants in the vegetable garden.
Notes: Used in agriculture and gardening.

English Words: verb: to spit; to spit phlegm
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请不要在公共场所随地吐痰。
English Usage in a sentence: Please do not spit indiscriminately in public places.
Notes: 随地吐痰 is common in public-health notices.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他拿出纸巾擤鼻涕。
English Usage in a sentence: He took out a tissue and blew his nose.
Notes: 擤 specifically means forcing mucus out through the nose.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 妈妈睡前给孩子读了一本绘本。
English Usage in a sentence: Mum read the child a picture book before bed.
Notes: Usually refers to a children’s book in which pictures play a major role.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 炒面里加一点酱青会更有味道。
English Usage in a sentence: Adding a little soy sauce to the fried noodles will give them more flavor.
Notes: A Singaporean and Malaysian Chinese term; 酱油 is more widely used elsewhere.

English Words: verb: to step forward; to stride
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他迈步走进了会议厅。
English Usage in a sentence: He stepped into the conference hall.
Notes: More descriptive or formal than simply saying 走.

English Words: fixed phrase: to stand or rise on tiptoe
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她踮起脚尖去拿架子上的书。
English Usage in a sentence: She stood on tiptoe to reach the book on the shelf.
Notes: 踮 means to raise the heels while balancing on the toes.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 雨后，天空中出现了一道彩虹。
English Usage in a sentence: After the rain, a rainbow appeared in the sky.
Notes: The measure word 道 is commonly used for rainbows.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 小心，地上有破碎的玻璃。
English Usage in a sentence: Be careful—there is broken glass on the ground.
Notes: May refer to the material or an object such as a windowpane.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们在海边放风筝。
English Usage in a sentence: The children are flying kites by the sea.
Notes: 放风筝 means “to fly a kite.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 汤里放一点胡椒会更香。
English Usage in a sentence: Adding a little pepper to the soup will make it more fragrant.
Notes: Usually means black or white pepper; 辣椒 means chili pepper.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 雨后，泥土里爬出了几条蚯蚓。
English Usage in a sentence: After the rain, several earthworms crawled out of the soil.
Notes: The usual measure word is 条.

English Words: onomatopoeia: gurgle; rumble; gulping or rolling sound
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他的肚子饿得咕噜咕噜叫。
English Usage in a sentence: His stomach was rumbling with hunger.
Notes: Also represents gulping, bubbling, or rolling sounds.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 新加坡植物园里种着许多美丽的胡姬花。
English Usage in a sentence: Many beautiful orchids grow in the Singapore Botanic Gardens.
Notes: A Singaporean and Malaysian Chinese term; 兰花 is more widely used elsewhere.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这道菜放了很多辣椒，非常辣。
English Usage in a sentence: A lot of chili was added to this dish, so it is very spicy.
Notes: Do not confuse it with 胡椒, “pepper.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 妈妈一早到巴刹买鱼和蔬菜。
English Usage in a sentence: Mum went to the wet market early in the morning to buy fish and vegetables.
Notes: A Singaporean and Malaysian term derived from Malay pasar; 市场 is more universal.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请按照说明书上的步骤安装这个书架。
English Usage in a sentence: Please assemble this bookshelf according to the steps in the instruction manual.
Notes: Usually refers to one stage or an ordered series of actions.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 蓝鲸是世界上最大的鲸鱼。
English Usage in a sentence: The blue whale is the largest whale in the world.
Notes: Despite 鱼 in the name, whales are mammals.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 保护森林对维持生态平衡十分重要。
English Usage in a sentence: Protecting forests is very important for maintaining ecological balance.
Notes: Common compounds include 生态环境, 生态系统, and 生态平衡.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请在正确答案旁画一个对号。
English Usage in a sentence: Please draw a check mark beside the correct answer.
Notes: Used in language, mathematics, computing, music, and other fields.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 一只蜗牛慢慢地爬过湿润的叶子。
English Usage in a sentence: A snail slowly crawled across the damp leaf.
Notes: Commonly associated with slow movement.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 一群乌鸦停在枯树上。
English Usage in a sentence: A group of crows perched in the dead tree.
Notes: Everyday Chinese does not always distinguish precisely between crows and ravens.

English Words:
verb: to depict; to describe in writing
noun: written depiction; descriptive writing
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 作者生动地描写了乡间景色；这段描写充满诗意。
English Usage in a sentence: The author vividly depicted the rural scenery; this descriptive passage is full of poetic feeling.
Notes: Emphasizes vivid literary or written portrayal; 描述 is broader and often more factual.

English Words:
verb: to narrate; to recount
noun: narration; account
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他按顺序叙述了事情的经过；这段叙述很清楚。
English Usage in a sentence: He recounted what happened in order; this narration is very clear.
Notes: Focuses on presenting events or information in an organized sequence.

English Words: idiom: to deceive oneself; literally, to cover one’s ears while stealing a bell
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 明知问题存在却假装看不见，只是掩耳盗铃。
English Usage in a sentence: Knowing that the problem exists but pretending not to see it is merely self-deception.
Notes: From a story about a thief who covered his ears so he could not hear the stolen bell ringing.

English Words: idiom: great luck and prosperity; highly auspicious
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大家在新年里互祝大吉大利。
English Usage in a sentence: Everyone wished one another great luck and prosperity during the New Year.
Notes: A festive blessing commonly used during Lunar New Year.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 那位服务员彬彬有礼地接待了每一位客人。
English Usage in a sentence: The server received every guest in a refined and courteous manner.
Notes: Strongly complimentary and slightly more polished than 有礼貌.

English Words:
noun: the headband-tightening spell from Journey to the West
noun: restrictive rule or form of control
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 唐僧念起紧箍咒；严格的规定也像一道紧箍咒，限制着他的行动。
English Usage in a sentence: Tang Sanzang recited the headband-tightening spell; the strict rules were also like a restraining spell limiting his actions.
Notes: An allusion to Journey to the West; often used figuratively for a severe restraint.

English Words: idiom: to use an inflexible method despite changed circumstances
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 时代已经改变，再照搬旧办法无异于刻舟求剑。
English Usage in a sentence: Times have changed, so copying the old method would be like using an inflexible approach despite changed circumstances.
Notes: From a story about marking a moving boat to locate a sword dropped into the water.

English Words: idiom: to make a last-minute effort; to cram at the last moment
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他平时没有复习，考试前才临时抱佛脚。
English Usage in a sentence: He did not revise regularly and only crammed at the last moment before the examination.
Notes: Often implies inadequate preparation and a desperate last-minute effort.

English Words: idiom: lost property is left untouched; society is honest and orderly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 当地民风淳朴，甚至可以说是路不拾遗。
English Usage in a sentence: The local people are so honest that one could say lost property is left untouched on the road.
Notes: A classical description of excellent public morality and social order.

English Words: idiom: unable to wait; eager to do something
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子们迫不及待地拆开礼物。
English Usage in a sentence: The children could not wait to open their presents.
Notes: Usually followed by 地 plus a verb.

English Words: idiom: thoughtful; as if deep in thought
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 听完老师的话，他若有所思地点了点头。
English Usage in a sentence: After hearing the teacher’s words, he nodded thoughtfully.
Notes: Describes an appearance suggesting quiet reflection.

English Words: idiom: perseverance can overcome enormous difficulties
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 只要有愚公移山的精神，再大的困难也能克服。
English Usage in a sentence: With the perseverance of the Foolish Old Man who moved mountains, even the greatest difficulties can be overcome.
Notes: From an ancient tale about an old man determined to remove two mountains.

English Words: idiom: crisscrossing; intersecting in every direction
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 城市里的道路纵横交错，很容易迷路。
English Usage in a sentence: The roads in the city crisscross in every direction, making it easy to get lost.
Notes: Used for roads, rivers, lines, roots, networks, and other intersecting structures.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 运动员以不屈不挠的精神完成了比赛。
English Usage in a sentence: The athlete completed the competition with indomitable determination.
Notes: Stronger and more emphatic than 不屈.

English Words: idiom: to deceive oneself; variant of 掩耳盗铃
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 以为没人指出错误，错误就不存在，这无异于掩耳盗钟。
English Usage in a sentence: Thinking that an error does not exist merely because nobody points it out is self-deception.
Notes: An older or less common variant; 掩耳盗铃 is the standard modern form.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他最近工作十分忙碌，几乎没有时间休息。
English Usage in a sentence: He has been extremely busy with work recently and has almost no time to rest.
Notes: Describes a person, period, schedule, or scene with much activity.

English Words:
adjective: peaceful; tranquil
noun: peace; tranquility
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 夜晚的湖面十分宁静；我很享受这里的宁静。
English Usage in a sentence: The lake is very tranquil at night; I greatly enjoy the peace here.
Notes: Usually suggests quietness together with a calm, peaceful mood.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 独自在异乡生活，他有时感到寂寞；这种寂寞很难向别人诉说。
English Usage in a sentence: Living alone away from home, he sometimes feels lonely; this loneliness is difficult to describe to others.
Notes: Concerns emotional loneliness; 寂静 concerns the absence of sound.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这名侦探具有敏锐的观察力。
English Usage in a sentence: This detective has keen powers of observation.
Notes: Commonly describes senses, observation, judgment, or awareness.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们在艰苦的环境中坚持完成了任务。
English Usage in a sentence: They persevered and completed the task under harsh conditions.
Notes: Emphasizes hardship requiring sustained effort or endurance.

English Words: verb: to treat an illness; to cure disease
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 医生的责任是为病人治病。
English Usage in a sentence: A doctor’s responsibility is to treat patients’ illnesses.
Notes: 治病 describes medical treatment; it does not guarantee that the illness is cured.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 机场在假期期间格外繁忙。
English Usage in a sentence: The airport is especially busy during the holiday period.
Notes: Often describes traffic, workplaces, transport hubs, schedules, or periods.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 老人拄着拐杖慢慢走过马路。
English Usage in a sentence: The elderly man crossed the road slowly with a walking stick.
Notes: 拄拐杖 means “to walk using a cane.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她跑步时扭伤了脚踝；医生说这次扭伤并不严重。
English Usage in a sentence: She sprained her ankle while running; the doctor said the sprain was not serious.
Notes: Usually concerns a joint such as the ankle, wrist, or waist.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 委员会的每位委员都参加了会议。
English Usage in a sentence: Every member of the committee attended the meeting.
Notes: The exact English title depends on the organization.

English Words: idiom: brilliantly colorful; a riot of colors
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 节日的街道挂满了五彩缤纷的彩旗。
English Usage in a sentence: The festival streets were filled with brilliantly colorful flags.
Notes: Describes a rich and lively variety of colors.

English Words: idiom: to refuse to mention; never to breathe a word about
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他对那次失败绝口不提。
English Usage in a sentence: He refused to say a word about that failure.
Notes: Implies deliberate and complete avoidance of a subject.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他爬上梯子修理屋顶。
English Usage in a sentence: He climbed the ladder to repair the roof.
Notes: Use 架 as a measure word: 一架梯子.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 广场中央立着一座英雄的雕像。
English Usage in a sentence: A statue of a hero stands in the center of the square.
Notes: 座 is a common measure word for statues.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这位艺术家以描绘自然景色而闻名。
English Usage in a sentence: This artist is famous for depicting natural scenery.
Notes: Can refer to visual artists, musicians, performers, and other creators.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她在椅子上放了一个柔软的垫子。
English Usage in a sentence: She placed a soft cushion on the chair.
Notes: The exact translation depends on its purpose and location.

English Words: verb: to hold or attend a meeting
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 老师们正在会议室开会。
English Usage in a sentence: The teachers are having a meeting in the conference room.
Notes: Context determines whether someone is holding or simply attending the meeting.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我找不到家门的钥匙了。
English Usage in a sentence: I cannot find the key to my front door.
Notes: Also used figuratively for the key to solving or understanding something.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 天空突然变暗，可能是暴风雨来临的前兆。
English Usage in a sentence: The sudden darkening of the sky may be a warning sign of an approaching storm.
Notes: Can indicate a sign of either a positive or negative event, though negative events are more common.

English Words:
noun: the non-everyday; the extraordinary
adjective: out of the ordinary; extraordinary
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 平静的校园生活中突然出现了非日常的事件。
English Usage in a sentence: An out-of-the-ordinary incident suddenly appeared in the peaceful school life.
Notes: Common in anime/light-novel writing, often contrasting 日常 “ordinary daily life” with supernatural, fantasy, or dramatic events.

English Words:
noun: scene; sight; view
noun: circumstance; situation
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 眼前的光景让他一时说不出话来。
English Usage in a sentence: The sight before him left him speechless for a moment.
Notes: More descriptive and literary than 景象 or 情景; can also mean a person’s current circumstances.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这两种做法之间没有太大的差别。
English Usage in a sentence: There is not much difference between these two approaches.
Notes: Very common in speech and writing. Common pattern: 有差别 / 没有差别.

English Words:
adjective: dazzling; brilliant; eye-catching
verb: to dazzle the eyes
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 阳光太耀眼了，他不由得眯起了眼睛。
English Usage in a sentence: The sunlight was so dazzling that he could not help squinting.
Notes: Can be literal for bright light or figurative for outstanding achievement or beauty.

English Words: noun: several steps; a few paces
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他在门口数步之外停了下来。
English Usage in a sentence: He stopped a few paces away from the door.
Notes: 数 here means “several,” not “to count.” Often appears in narration: 数步之外, 走了数步.

English Words:
noun: red traffic light
noun: warning sign; danger signal
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 前面的红灯亮了，我们得停下来。
English Usage in a sentence: The red light ahead came on, so we have to stop.
Notes: Also used figuratively, such as 亮红灯 “to raise a warning signal.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 耳机里突然传来一阵杂讯。
English Usage in a sentence: A burst of static suddenly came through the headphones.
Notes: Common in Taiwan and in translated fiction; 噪音 is more common in Mainland Chinese for general “noise.”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 雨后的沥青路面反射着路灯的光。
English Usage in a sentence: The wet asphalt road reflected the streetlights after the rain.
Notes: Used for road surfaces and construction material.

English Words: adjective: bright and beautiful; sunny and charming
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 今天阳光明媚，很适合出去散步。
English Usage in a sentence: The sunshine is bright and lovely today; it is perfect for a walk.
Notes: Often describes spring weather, sunshine, scenery, or a person’s bright appearance.

English Words:
adjective: dim; dull; faint
adjective: bleak; unpromising
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 房间里的灯光十分暗淡。
English Usage in a sentence: The lighting in the room was very dim.
Notes: Can describe literal light, colours, prospects, or mood.

English Words:
adjective: baffling; inexplicable; ridiculous
fixed expression: without rhyme or reason
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他突然生气，真让人觉得莫名其妙。
English Usage in a sentence: He suddenly got angry, which was really baffling.
Notes: Often has a slightly annoyed tone: 你莫名其妙！ means “You’re being ridiculous / making no sense!”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 山里的溪水非常清澈。
English Usage in a sentence: The mountain stream water is very clear.
Notes: Usually describes water, eyes, or a voice; clearer and more descriptive than 干净.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 猫的项圈上挂着一个小铃铛。
English Usage in a sentence: A small bell was hanging from the cat’s collar.
Notes: Usually refers to a small bell that makes a jingling sound.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她有一张白净无暇的脸。
English Usage in a sentence: She had a fair, clean, flawless face.
Notes: 白净 means fair and clean-looking; 无暇 means flawless. Descriptive wording, often for skin or appearance.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她今天穿了一条蓝色的连衣裙。
English Usage in a sentence: She is wearing a blue dress today.
Notes: Mainland Chinese term for a dress; 裙子 is broader and can also mean a skirt.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 小说中的精灵少女有着金发碧眼的外貌。
English Usage in a sentence: The elf girl in the novel has blonde hair and blue eyes.
Notes: Common descriptive phrase in fantasy and translated fiction; often used for Western-looking characters.

English Words: conjunction: as well as; and; together with
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请带上护照、机票以及身份证。
English Usage in a sentence: Please bring your passport, ticket, and identity card.
Notes: More formal than 和. Usually joins items in writing or careful speech.

English Words: verb: to be dressed in; to wear
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她身着一件白色长袍，站在窗边。
English Usage in a sentence: She was dressed in a white robe, standing by the window.
Notes: More literary/formal than 穿着; common in descriptions and reports.

English Words:
adverb: as if; seemingly
verb: to resemble
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她的声音仿佛从很远的地方传来。
English Usage in a sentence: Her voice seemed to come from a very distant place.
Notes: Common in narration and imagery; similar to 好像, but more literary.

English Words: verb: to envelop; to shroud; to hang over
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 夜色笼罩着整座城市。
English Usage in a sentence: Night enveloped the entire city.
Notes: Often used with darkness, fog, silence, fear, or an atmosphere.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 深夜的走廊里一片寂静。
English Usage in a sentence: The corridor was completely silent late at night.
Notes: Stronger and more atmospheric than 安静; often describes a place or scene.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 魔法师披着黑色长袍走进了大厅。
English Usage in a sentence: The mage entered the hall wearing a black robe.
Notes: Common in historical, fantasy, and religious settings.

English Words:
verb: to perplex; to confuse
noun: confusion; perplexity
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个奇怪的问题让他感到十分困惑。
English Usage in a sentence: This strange question left him very confused.
Notes: Can describe both the feeling and the thing causing confusion.

English Words:
noun: regret; pity
adjective: regrettable; unfortunate
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 很遗憾，我们今天无法见面。
English Usage in a sentence: Unfortunately, we cannot meet today.
Notes: Common polite phrase: 很遗憾…… “I’m sorry to say / unfortunately…”

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 销售额是评估公司表现的重要指标。
English Usage in a sentence: Sales revenue is an important indicator for evaluating company performance.
Notes: Common in business, statistics, engineering, and reports.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 沙漏里的沙子慢慢地流了下来。
English Usage in a sentence: The sand in the hourglass slowly flowed down.
Notes: A literal hourglass; frequently used symbolically for the passage of time.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这台电脑使用的是速度更快的处理器。
English Usage in a sentence: This computer uses a faster processor.
Notes: Usually refers to a CPU, though it can also be part of another technical term.

English Words: noun: circumstances; situation; lot in life
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他对自己目前的境遇感到无奈。
English Usage in a sentence: He felt helpless about his current circumstances.
Notes: More literary than 情况; often refers to someone’s difficult personal situation.

English Words: verb: to aim at; to take a quick look at
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他悄悄瞄了一眼门外。
English Usage in a sentence: He secretly took a quick glance outside the door.
Notes: Informal shortened form of 瞄准 or 瞄一眼. Often implies a brief or secret look.

English Words:
verb: to summon; to call forth
noun: summoning
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 国王召唤勇者来到王宫。
English Usage in a sentence: The king summoned the hero to the royal palace.
Notes: In fantasy, it often means magically summoning someone or something.

In Japanese subculture, light novels, and manga, 王道 (pronounced ōdō in Japanese, literally "the Royal Road") refers to the classic, mainstream, or classic formulaic storytelling style of a genre. It represents the golden standard, traditional tropes, and straight-laced execution that audiences expect.

It stands in direct contrast to 邪道 (jadō), which refers to subversions, deconstructions, dark turns, or unconventional, sub-genre twists.

Core Characteristics of 王道 (Ōdō)

Earnest & Righteous Protagonist: 

Classic Hero's Journey

Standard World-Building: Utilizes traditional fantasy settings (like classic high fantasy, guild systems, and straightforward magic) without weird gimmick twists.

Themes of Hope & Camaralty: Focuses heavily on teamwork, perseverance, justice, and emotional payoff.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我发誓绝不会泄露这个秘密。
English Usage in a sentence: I swear that I will never reveal this secret.

English Words: verb: to exert; to impose; to apply
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 对他人施加压力并不能解决问题。
English Usage in a sentence: Exerting pressure on others cannot solve the problem.
Notes: Common collocations include 施加压力、影响、惩罚. 施加危害 is awkward; 加以伤害 or 造成伤害 is more natural.

English Words: adjective/verb: Willful / headstrong / doing whatever one pleases without restraint.
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子不能因为任性就要求别人事事迁就。
English Usage in a sentence: A child cannot demand that everyone accommodate them simply because they are being willful.
Notes:
Acting purely according to one's own desires, feelings, or whims, regardless of consequences, social norms, or the feelings of others.

Depending on the context, its meaning ranges from negative self-indulgence to playful, affectionate headstrong behavior.

English Words: verb: to apologize for an offense; to seek forgiveness
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 大臣公开谢罪，并承担了责任。
English Usage in a sentence: The minister publicly apologized for the wrongdoing and accepted responsibility.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们需要全面了解事情的经过。
English Usage in a sentence: We need to understand the entire course of events fully.

English Words: verb: to protect oneself; to preserve oneself
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 在危险环境中，首先要学会自保。
English Usage in a sentence: In a dangerous environment, one must first learn to protect oneself.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家餐厅的内装简洁而现代。
English Usage in a sentence: The restaurant’s interior design is simple and modern.
Notes: Japanese source: 内装（ないそう）. In Mandarin, 室内装潢 or 内部装修 is often more natural.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 酒店为客人准备了豪华套房。
English Usage in a sentence: The hotel prepared a luxurious suite for the guest.
Notes: Can describe buildings, rooms, meals, lineups, or equipment.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 客人们正在酒店大厅等候。
English Usage in a sentence: The guests are waiting in the hotel lobby.

English Words: noun: cleric; member of the clergy
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 圣职者身穿白袍主持仪式。
English Usage in a sentence: The cleric conducted the ceremony in white robes.

English Words:
verb: to decorate
noun: decoration; ornament
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们用鲜花装饰大厅；墙上的装饰十分精美。
English Usage in a sentence: They decorated the hall with flowers; the decorations on the wall were exquisite.

English Words:
noun: the Middle Ages
adjective: medieval
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这座城堡保留了许多中世纪建筑特色。
English Usage in a sentence: This castle retains many features of medieval architecture.
Notes: 中世纪风格 is a common fantasy aesthetic; it does not necessarily indicate accurate medieval history.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家咖啡馆的氛围很轻松。
English Usage in a sentence: This café has a relaxed atmosphere.
Notes: Often interchangeable with 气氛, which is more common in mainland everyday speech.

English Words: noun: sense of reality; tangible feeling
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 拿到毕业证书后，我才终于有了毕业的实感。
English Usage in a sentence: Only after receiving my diploma did graduating finally feel real.
Notes: Japanese source: 実感（じっかん）. This Japanese-influenced use is understood in Chinese fandom, but 真实感 or 感觉自己真的…… is often more natural.

English Words: verb: to take one’s seat; to be seated
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请各位来宾尽快就座。
English Usage in a sentence: Guests, please take your seats as soon as possible.
Notes: Formal event language; casual speech normally uses 坐下.

English Words: formula: yes, sir/ma’am; as you command
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 侍卫低头回答：“遵命，陛下。”
English Usage in a sentence: The guard bowed and answered, “As you command, Your Majesty.”
Notes: Japanese source: 畏まりました（かしこまりました）, a highly polite ‘certainly.’ 遵命 sounds more like an order to a subordinate and suits the servant/fantasy setting.

English Words: verb: to urge; to press; to hurry someone
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 工作人员催促大家尽快登车。
English Usage in a sentence: The staff urged everyone to board quickly.
Notes: The EPUB says 催促我们就座, while the Japanese source uses an invitation/instruction to sit rather than impatient urging.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她在主题咖啡馆穿着女仆装工作。
English Usage in a sentence: She works at the themed café wearing a maid outfit.

English Words: idiom: extremely cautiously; with great care
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她小心翼翼地打开了旧盒子。
English Usage in a sentence: She opened the old box with great care.
Notes: Emphasizes careful action caused by fear of error, damage, or danger.

English Words: noun phrase: directly opposite; straight across from
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 银行就在车站的正对面。
English Usage in a sentence: The bank is directly opposite the station.
Notes: 正 emphasizes exact alignment; 对面 alone is more general.

English Words: quantifier/adverb: a little; a small amount; shortly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 汤里加少许盐，稍等少许即可食用。
English Usage in a sentence: Add a little salt to the soup and wait a short while before serving.
Notes: In 少许之后, it means ‘a short while later,’ though 片刻之后 is more idiomatic.

English Words: adverbial phrase: seeing this; at the sight
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 众人见状，立刻上前帮忙。
English Usage in a sentence: Seeing this, everyone immediately stepped forward to help.
Notes: Common in narrative writing; everyday speech usually says 看到这个情况.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这块丝绸在灯光下泛着柔和的光泽。
English Usage in a sentence: This silk has a soft sheen under the light.
Notes: Often describes hair, skin, fabric, metal, or polished surfaces.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 双方合作的大前提是彼此信任。
English Usage in a sentence: Mutual trust is the fundamental premise for cooperation between the two sides.
Notes: Japanese source: 大前提（だいぜんてい）. Common in Japanese argumentation; Chinese often simply uses 前提.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 国王授予他公爵爵位。
English Usage in a sentence: The king granted him the title of duke.

English Words: noun: family name; reputation of one’s house
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他发誓绝不做有辱家名的事。
English Usage in a sentence: He swore never to do anything that would disgrace the family name.

English Words:
adjective/verb: impolite; to be discourteous
formula: excuse me; pardon me
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 刚才是我失礼了，请您原谅。
English Usage in a sentence: I was discourteous just now; please forgive me.

English Words: noun: title of nobility; peerage rank
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个爵位可以由他的长子继承。
English Usage in a sentence: This title of nobility may be inherited by his eldest son.
Notes: Common fantasy and historical vocabulary; examples include 公爵、侯爵、伯爵.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 现任会长将在年底卸任。
English Usage in a sentence: The current chairperson will step down at the end of the year.
Notes: Opposite: 前任, predecessor/former officeholder.

English Words: honorific title: His Majesty the King; Your Majesty
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 国王陛下将在明日接见使节。
English Usage in a sentence: His Majesty the King will receive the envoy tomorrow.
Notes: 陛下 is reserved for a sovereign or emperor-level ruler.

English Words: adjective: sharing the same father but having different mothers; paternal half-sibling
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她有一个同父异母的哥哥。
English Usage in a sentence: She has an older paternal half-brother.

English Words: noun: right of succession to the throne
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 王子宣布放弃王位继承权。
English Usage in a sentence: The prince announced that he was giving up his right of succession to the throne.

English Words:
verb: to take an oath; to swear formally
noun: oath-taking
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 新任部长在仪式上宣誓就职；宣誓结束后，全场鼓掌。
English Usage in a sentence: The new minister took the oath of office at the ceremony; the audience applauded after the oath-taking.
Notes: Japanese source uses 宣言された先の言葉, ‘the statement she just declared,’ rather than the noun 宣誓.

English Words: discourse phrase: incidentally; by the way
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 顺带一提，明天的会议改到下午了。
English Usage in a sentence: Incidentally, tomorrow’s meeting has been moved to the afternoon.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 网站每天更新科技资讯。
English Usage in a sentence: The website updates its technology news every day.
Notes: Common in Taiwan and some Southeast Asian Chinese usage. Japanese source: 情報; mainland Mandarin more often uses 信息 or 资料.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 批评者毫不留情地指出了作品的问题。
English Usage in a sentence: The critic unsparingly pointed out the work’s problems.

English Words: adverb: must; be sure to; by all means
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 出发前务必检查护照。
English Usage in a sentence: Be sure to check your passport before departure.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她虽然有些胆怯，还是勇敢地开了口。
English Usage in a sentence: Although she was somewhat timid, she courageously spoke up.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她把头发染成了栗色。
English Usage in a sentence: She dyed her hair chestnut brown.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 学姐带我熟悉了校园环境。
English Usage in a sentence: A senior female student showed me around the campus.

English Words: idiom: to look troubled or reluctant
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 听到这个要求，他立刻面带难色。
English Usage in a sentence: He immediately looked troubled when he heard the request.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这句话不能只按字面意思理解。
English Usage in a sentence: This sentence cannot be understood solely by its literal meaning.
Notes: Translation issue: the Japanese source says リリアさんを信用すべきではない, ‘perhaps I should not trust Lilia.’ It does not mention literal meaning; 按字面意思理解 is an added and misleading rendering.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她突然尖叫起来；那声尖叫把大家都吓了一跳。
English Usage in a sentence: She suddenly screamed; the scream startled everyone.

English Words: noun/verb: mysterious disappearance; to vanish mysteriously
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 孩子突然失踪，村民都说他遭遇了神隐。
English Usage in a sentence: The child suddenly disappeared, and the villagers said he had been spirited away.

English Words: noun phrase: naturally airheaded character trait; ditzy archetype
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她常常误解别人的话，显得很有天然属性。
English Usage in a sentence: She often misunderstands what people say and comes across as naturally airheaded.
Notes: 属性 means a character trait/archetype; this is fandom language, not ordinary formal Chinese.

English Words: noun: flow velocity; rate of flow
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 工程师测量了河水的流速。
English Usage in a sentence: The engineer measured the river’s flow velocity.
Notes: Translation issue: Japanese source says 時間の流れ, ‘the passage/flow of time.’ 时间流速 is understandable in fantasy, but 时间流逝的速度 is more natural outside genre writing.

English Words: noun/adverb: an instant; in an instant
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 灯光在一瞬间全部熄灭了。
English Usage in a sentence: All the lights went out in an instant.
Notes: Japanese source here says 召喚された直後の時間, ‘the moment immediately after being summoned,’ not simply 一瞬間.

English Words: noun: food, clothing, and shelter; basic necessities
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 政府为灾民提供基本的衣食住保障。
English Usage in a sentence: The government provided disaster victims with basic food, clothing, and shelter.
Notes: Japanese source: 衣食住（いしょくじゅう）, a common Japanese collective term. Chinese more often says 衣食住行 or 衣食住等生活需要.

English Words:
adjective: luxurious; extravagant
verb: to indulge extravagantly
noun: luxury
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家酒店十分奢侈；他从不奢侈消费；对当时的他们来说，休息也是一种奢侈。
English Usage in a sentence: This hotel is extremely luxurious; he never spends extravagantly; for them at the time, even rest was a luxury.

English Words: verb/adjective: to be absent-minded; dazed; to lose consciousness
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他听到消息后失神地站在原地。
English Usage in a sentence: He stood there dazed after hearing the news.
Notes: Translation issue: Japanese source says 毒気を抜かれる, ‘to be disarmed/taken aback.’ It does not mean fainting; the EPUB expands this as 失神发呆.

English Words: conjunction: to the extent that; so that
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 雨下得太大，以至于比赛被迫取消。
English Usage in a sentence: The rain was so heavy that the match had to be cancelled.
Notes: Introduces a resulting consequence, often after an extreme degree or accumulated cause.

English Words:
adjective: corresponding; appropriate
verb: to correspond
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 能力越大，就要承担相应的责任；两组数据彼此相应。
English Usage in a sentence: The greater the ability, the corresponding responsibility one must bear; the two sets of data correspond to each other.
Notes: In 与之相应的危险, it means danger commensurate with or corresponding to the situation.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这场胜利成为战争的转捩点。
English Usage in a sentence: This victory became the turning point of the war.
Notes: Japanese source: ターニングポイント, the English loanword ‘turning point.’ 转折点 is much more common in modern Mandarin; 转捩点 is literary and more common in Taiwan.

English Words:
adjective: honest; upright
adverb: honestly; frankly
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他是个正直的人，也正直地说出了自己的想法。
English Usage in a sentence: He is an upright person and honestly stated what he thought.
Notes: Japanese source: 正直に話す, ‘speak honestly.’ In Mandarin, 老实说明 or 如实说明 is more idiomatic here.

English Words: idiom: to bluff or muddle through; to get by through deception
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他想用含糊的回答蒙混过关。
English Usage in a sentence: He tried to bluff his way through with a vague answer.

English Words: noun phrase: a certain extent; some degree
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个办法在一定程度上减轻了压力。
English Usage in a sentence: This method reduced the pressure to a certain extent.
Notes: Usually appears as 在一定程度上.

English Words: noun: policy; guiding principle; course of action
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 团队决定调整今后的工作方针。
English Usage in a sentence: The team decided to adjust its future course of action.
Notes: Japanese source discusses 身の振り方 and 方向性, how he should conduct himself and the direction to take; 方针 is a concise translation.

English Words: verb: to make a move; to use a technique; to play one’s hand
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 对手还没有出招，他就已经做好了准备。
English Usage in a sentence: Before his opponent made a move, he was already prepared.
Notes: Originally martial-arts language; figuratively means making a strategic move. Japanese source: どう出てくる, ‘how will she respond/what will she do?’

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 紧张时，我的心砰砰直跳。
English Usage in a sentence: My heart pounded when I was nervous.
Notes: 怦怦 is often preferred specifically for a beating heart.

English Words: noun/adjective: first generation; original holder of a title
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这辆车是该系列的初代车型。
English Usage in a sentence: This car is the first-generation model in the series.

English Words: noun: demon race; demons as a people
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 魔族与人类签订了和平条约。
English Usage in a sentence: The demon race signed a peace treaty with humanity.

English Words: verb/adjective: to be hostile to; hostile; opposing
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 两个阵营长期处于敌对状态。
English Usage in a sentence: The two camps remained hostile to each other for a long time.
Notes: Common pattern: 与……敌对 or 敌对关系.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 两国扩大了贸易往来，并开始直接贸易。
English Usage in a sentence: The two countries expanded commercial exchange and began trading directly.

English Words:
adjective: prosperous; flourishing
verb: to prosper; to promote prosperity
noun: prosperity
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 港口十分繁荣，贸易使城市繁荣，也带来了长期繁荣。
English Usage in a sentence: The port is prosperous; trade made the city flourish and brought lasting prosperity.
Notes: Japanese source: 盛ん, ‘active/thriving.’ 贸易繁荣 is natural Chinese.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 冒险者在森林里遇到了一只魔物。
English Usage in a sentence: The adventurer encountered a monster in the forest.

English Words: verb/noun: to suppress or subjugate by force; punitive expedition
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 骑士团出发讨伐山中的魔物；这次讨伐持续了三天。
English Usage in a sentence: The knights set out to subjugate the monsters in the mountains; the expedition lasted three days.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她到冒险者工会登记并领取任务。
English Usage in a sentence: She registered at the Adventurers’ Guild and accepted a quest.

English Words: noun: order or corps of knights
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 王国派骑士团保护边境。
English Usage in a sentence: The kingdom sent the order of knights to protect the border.

English Words: verb phrase: to rush or head to the battlefield
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 士兵们奉命奔赴战场。
English Usage in a sentence: The soldiers were ordered to head to the battlefield.
Notes: Translation issue: Japanese source says 戦う必要などありません, ‘there is no need for you to fight.’ 奔赴战场 is a more dramatic addition.

English Words: verb phrase: to join hands and cooperate
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 两国决定携手合作，共同应对危机。
English Usage in a sentence: The two countries decided to join hands and work together to address the crisis.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 文化交流可以成为两国人民之间的桥梁。
English Usage in a sentence: Cultural exchange can become a bridge between the peoples of two countries.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 后人不断称颂他的勇气与功绩。
English Usage in a sentence: Later generations continued to extol his courage and achievements.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 人们永远不会忘记他的伟大功绩。
English Usage in a sentence: People will never forget his great achievements.
Notes: Usually refers to significant public, military, political, or heroic accomplishments.

English Words: verb/noun: to pray or wish for; prayer; wish
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 人们在祭典上祈愿和平；她写下了自己的祈愿。
English Usage in a sentence: People prayed for peace at the festival; she wrote down her wish.
Notes: Japanese source: 願い, ‘wish,’ in 平和を願い. Chinese 祈愿 adds a religious or ceremonial tone.

English Words:
adverb: once; at one time
frequency phrase: every occurrence in a cycle
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他一度想要放弃；这个庆典十年一度举行。
English Usage in a sentence: He once wanted to give up; this celebration is held once every ten years.
Notes: In 十年一度, it means ‘once every ten years.’ More common Mandarin: 每十年一次 or 十年一次.

English Words: adjective: grand; magnificent; on a large scale
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 城市举行了盛大的庆典。
English Usage in a sentence: The city held a grand celebration.
Notes: Common with 仪式、庆典、婚礼、活动.

English Words:
verb: to undertake; to take responsibility for
noun: responsibility; role
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她担当项目负责人，也勇于承担自己的担当。
English Usage in a sentence: She serves as the project lead and is willing to shoulder her responsibilities.
Notes: Japanese source/book-edition wording: 担当（たんとう）, ‘be in charge.’ In Mandarin, 担任 is more natural for holding a role: 由各国贵族轮流担任负责人.

English Words: noun: protagonist; leading character; central figure
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她是小说的主角，也是今晚宴会的主角。
English Usage in a sentence: She is the protagonist of the novel and also the center of attention at tonight’s banquet.

English Words: verb: to decline; to turn down; to resign
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他礼貌地辞退了这份工作邀请。
English Usage in a sentence: He politely declined the job offer.

English Words:
verb: to act on behalf of
noun: agent; proxy; substitute
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 副经理将代理经理职务；公司已经安排了一名代理。
English Usage in a sentence: The deputy manager will act in the manager’s place; the company has appointed a substitute.
Notes: Japanese source phrase: 勇者代役, ‘a substitute hero.’ 勇者代理 is understandable, but 代役／替代者 is the more exact role.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 总统以国宾礼遇接待来访君主。
English Usage in a sentence: The president received the visiting monarch as a state guest.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家公司为员工提供优厚待遇。
English Usage in a sentence: This company provides its employees with generous pay and benefits.
Notes: Japanese source: 高待遇, favorable or privileged treatment. In employment contexts, 待遇 often means compensation and benefits.

English Words:
verb: to sightsee; to tour
noun: sightseeing; tourism
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 游客乘巴士观光；当地观光业十分发达。
English Usage in a sentence: The tourists went sightseeing by bus; the local tourism industry is highly developed.
Notes: Japanese source: 観光（かんこう）. In casual Mandarin, 游览 or 到处玩 may sound more natural depending on context.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 小镇每年都会举行丰收祭典。
English Usage in a sentence: The town holds a harvest festival every year.
Notes: Japanese source: お祭り, ‘festival.’ 祭典 is common in Japanese-influenced ACG translations; Mandarin more often uses 庆典 or 节庆活动 unless it is explicitly ritual.

English Words: letter opening: Dear…; Respectfully addressed to…
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 拜启：父亲、母亲，我在远方一切平安。
English Usage in a sentence: Dear Father and Mother, I am safe and well far from home.
Notes: Japanese epistolary formula: 拝啓（はいけい）. It is a formal letter opening, humorously used in the novel’s recurring closing line. In natural English it is usually simply ‘Dear Mother and Father.’

Chinese Usage in a Sentence:
这个文件具有只读属性，所以不能直接修改。
金属的导电性是一种重要的物理属性。
这把武器带有火属性。
English Usage in a sentence:
This file has the read-only attribute, so it cannot be modified directly.
Electrical conductivity is an important physical property of metals.
This weapon has the fire attribute.
Notes: Common in computing, science, and games. The exact English word depends on context.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 那名冒险者独自进入了危险的森林。
English Usage in a sentence: The adventurer entered the dangerous forest alone.
Notes: Common in fantasy, light novels, and RPGs.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 骑士拔出长剑保护公主。
English Usage in a sentence: The knight drew his sword to protect the princess.
Notes: Common in historical and fantasy settings.

English Words: adverb: without permission / on one's own authority
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请不要擅自进入这个房间。
English Usage in a sentence: Please do not enter this room without permission.
Notes: Usually implies acting without approval or authorization.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence:
他是历史上的重要人物。
这个故事里有很多有趣的人物。
English Usage in a sentence:
He is an important figure in history.
There are many interesting characters in this story.
Notes: Can refer to a real person or a character in a story.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 今年的收入是去年的两倍。
English Usage in a sentence: This year's income is twice that of last year.
Notes: Used to express multiplication, such as 两倍 (twice) and 三倍 (three times).

English Words: verb: to call / to refer to as
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这种现象被称作“海市蜃楼”。
English Usage in a sentence: This phenomenon is called a “mirage.”
Notes: Similar to 称为; often used when giving the name or term for something.

English Words:
verb: to associate / to connect mentally
noun: association
Chinese Usage in a Sentence:
看到这张照片，我联想到了小时候的生活。
这个名字容易让人产生不好的联想。
English Usage in a sentence:
Seeing this photo made me think of my childhood.
This name can easily create negative associations.
Notes: Often used for mental associations between ideas, memories, or images.

English Words: fixed expression: to stop here / that's enough
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 今天的讨论就到此为止吧。
English Usage in a sentence: Let's stop today's discussion here.
Notes: Used to indicate that something ends at this point.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她穿着一条水蓝色的裙子。
English Usage in a sentence: She was wearing a light blue dress.
Notes: A pale blue colour resembling clear water.

English Words:
adverb: slightly to the right
adjective: right-leaning / positioned to the right
Chinese Usage in a Sentence:
门的位置稍微偏右。
这个按钮在屏幕上偏右一些。
English Usage in a sentence:
The door is positioned slightly to the right.
This button is a little to the right on the screen.

English Words: verb: to pass through / to cross
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们穿过森林来到了村庄。
English Usage in a sentence: They passed through the forest and arrived at the village.
Notes: Used for moving through an area or from one side to another.

English Words: fixed expression: different from others / distinctive
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她的想法总是与众不同。
English Usage in a sentence: Her ideas are always different from everyone else's.
Notes: Usually has a neutral or positive sense of being distinctive.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这件衣服穿起来有点刺刺的。
English Usage in a sentence: This clothing feels a little prickly against the skin.
Notes: Colloquial reduplication describing a prickly or mildly stinging sensation.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我的胃有点不舒服。
English Usage in a sentence: My stomach feels a little uncomfortable.
Notes: Refers specifically to the stomach organ.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个大厅可以容纳几百人。
English Usage in a sentence: This hall can accommodate several hundred people.
Notes: Used for the capacity of spaces, containers, or organizations.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请站在栏杆的外侧。
English Usage in a sentence: Please stand on the outer side of the railing.
Notes: Opposite of 内侧.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 女仆端着餐盘走进房间。
English Usage in a sentence: The maid entered the room carrying a tray.
Notes: As a verb, often means holding something level with both hands, especially dishes or drinks.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 女仆把最后一盘菜端上了桌。
English Usage in a sentence: The maid brought the final dish to the table.
Notes: 盘 is commonly used as the measure word for a plate or dish of food.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence:
你误解我的意思了。
两人之间产生了很深的误解。
English Usage in a sentence:
You misunderstood what I meant.
A serious misunderstanding developed between the two.
Notes: Can refer to misunderstanding words, intentions, or situations.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 米饭是许多亚洲地区的主食。
English Usage in a sentence: Rice is a staple food in many parts of Asia.
Notes: Refers to the main carbohydrate or staple component of a meal.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这家店提供各种不同的料理。
English Usage in a sentence: This restaurant serves many different kinds of cuisine.
Notes: In this sense, common in Japanese-influenced Chinese; 菜 or 菜肴 is often more natural in Mainland Mandarin.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我买的是这本书的新版。
English Usage in a sentence: I bought the new edition of this book.
Notes: Common in 新版, 旧版, 电影版, and 限定版.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个面包又香又软。
English Usage in a sentence: This bread is fragrant and soft.
Notes: Can describe texture, physical flexibility, or figuratively a weak/soft stance.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 晚餐准备了几道法式料理。
English Usage in a sentence: Several French-style dishes were prepared for dinner.
Notes: Common before food, clothing, architecture, and other styles associated with France.

English Words:
verb: to send / to issue / to distribute
measure word: shot / round
Chinese Usage in a Sentence:
文件我已经发了。
再来一发。
English Usage in a sentence:
I already sent the file.
One more shot.
Notes: The verb 发 can independently mean to send, issue, or distribute something. As a measure word, it counts shots, bullets, or artillery rounds, as in 一发 and 三发子弹. 发 also has the pronunciation fà meaning hair, but bare 发 is uncommon for everyday “hair”; 头发 is normally used instead.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她的脸颊因为寒冷而泛起了红晕。
English Usage in a sentence: Her cheeks flushed red from the cold.
Notes: This term is standard and widely used in Singaporean Mandarin Chinese, commonly found in CN.csv.

English Words:
Noun: fever

Verb: to emit heat, to have a fever
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 机器运转过度开始发热，让他急得满身是汗，甚至怀疑自己是不是也发热了。
English Usage in a sentence: The machine started to emit heat from overworking, making him sweat so anxiously that he wondered if he had a fever too.
Notes: This term is standard and widely used in Singaporean Mandarin Chinese, though "发烧" is more common for a medical fever in casual speech.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 经过短暂的休息，他紧绷的神经稍稍放松了一些。
English Usage in a sentence: After a short rest, his tense nerves relaxed slightly.
Notes: This term is used in Singaporean Mandarin Chinese, but "稍微" (shāo wēi) is often preferred in daily colloquial conversations.

English Words: verb: to stagger / to offset / to avoid overlapping
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我们把出发时间错开，以免遇上人群。
English Usage in a sentence: We staggered our departure times to avoid the crowd.
Notes: Used for times, positions, schedules, or objects arranged so they do not overlap.

English Words: verb: to strike up a conversation / to speak to someone
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他犹豫了一会儿，才主动上前搭话。
English Usage in a sentence: He hesitated for a moment before going over to strike up a conversation.
Notes: Usually means initiating casual conversation with someone.

English Words: verb: to act foolishly / to do something stupid
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 别在这种时候犯傻。
English Usage in a sentence: Don't do anything stupid at a time like this.
Notes: Colloquial; often used when someone behaves irrationally or foolishly.

English Words: verb: to withdraw / to leave / to stand down
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 国王挥了挥手，让侍从退下。
English Usage in a sentence: The king waved his hand and told the attendants to leave.
Notes: Common command from someone of higher status to a subordinate in historical or fantasy settings.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 多年过去了，这座城市依旧十分繁华。
English Usage in a sentence: Many years have passed, but the city is still prosperous.
Notes: Similar to 仍然, often with a slightly more written tone.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 国王召集了所有大臣商议此事。
English Usage in a sentence: The king summoned all the ministers to discuss the matter.
Notes: Usually involves someone intentionally gathering a group together.

English Words: phrase: summoned here / gathered by being summoned
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这些骑士都是为了会议而被召集而来的。
English Usage in a sentence: These knights were all summoned here for the meeting.
Notes: 而来 indicates arriving as the result of the preceding action.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 每个人都必须坚守自己的岗位。
English Usage in a sentence: Everyone must remain at their post.
Notes: Common in workplaces, organizations, and duty assignments.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 闲聊就到这里，我们进入正题吧。
English Usage in a sentence: That's enough small talk; let's get to the main point.
Notes: Common expression: 进入正题.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 骑士立刻拔剑挡在公主面前。
English Usage in a sentence: The knight immediately drew his sword and stood in front of the princess.
Notes: Common in historical, martial-arts, and fantasy settings.

English Words: verb: to equate / to be equivalent to
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 不能把失败等同于没有能力。
English Usage in a sentence: Failure cannot be equated with a lack of ability.
Notes: Common pattern: 等同于.

English Words: adverb: toward each other / facing one another
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 两名骑士拔剑相向。
English Usage in a sentence: The two knights drew their swords against each other.
Notes: Usually used in phrases describing two sides confronting or moving toward each other.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这是支持他观点的强有力证据。
English Usage in a sentence: This is strong evidence supporting his argument.
Notes: Common with 证据, 支持, 措施, and leadership.

English Words: verb: to wave / to swing / to brandish
Chinese Usage in a Sentence:
她向我挥了挥手。
骑士挥剑砍向魔物。
English Usage in a sentence:
She waved her hand at me.
The knight swung his sword at the monster.
Notes: The object determines the action: 挥手 means to wave a hand; 挥剑 means to swing or brandish a sword.

English Words:
verb: to gather / to assemble
noun: gathering / concentration
Chinese Usage in a Sentence:
人群逐渐聚集在广场上。
魔力的聚集引起了异常现象。
English Usage in a sentence:
The crowd gradually gathered in the square.
The concentration of magical power caused an abnormal phenomenon.
Notes: Can describe people gathering or substances, energy, or resources becoming concentrated.

English Words: phrase: to gather and come / to come together
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 听到钟声后，人们从四面八方聚集而来。
English Usage in a sentence: After hearing the bell, people came gathering from all directions.
Notes: 而来 emphasizes movement toward a place as a result of gathering.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我并无此意，请不要误会。
English Usage in a sentence: That was not my intention, so please don't misunderstand.
Notes: 此意 can refer to either an intended meaning or an intention.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这只不过是孩子们的恶作剧。
English Usage in a sentence: It was nothing more than a prank by the children.
Notes: Usually playful, although the prank may still cause trouble.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 不要因为身份不同就对别人抱有偏见。
English Usage in a sentence: Don't be prejudiced against others simply because of their status.
Notes: Common pattern: 对……抱有偏见.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她做事一直非常细致。
English Usage in a sentence: She has always been very meticulous in her work.
Notes: Can describe careful work or something containing fine detail.

English Words: adjective: extremely detailed / penetrating into fine details
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他的观察细致入微。
English Usage in a sentence: His observations are extremely detailed.
Notes: Rarely used alone; most commonly appears in 细致入微 or 体贴入微.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他只是一个平凡的普通人。
English Usage in a sentence: He is merely an ordinary person.
Notes: Usually contrasts with exceptional, special, or extraordinary.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这些照片可以作为设计素材使用。
English Usage in a sentence: These photographs can be used as design material.
Notes: Common in writing, art, design, games, and media production.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence:
这件商品的品质很好。
她拥有善良正直的品质。
English Usage in a sentence:
This product is of very good quality.
She possesses kind and upright qualities.
Notes: Can refer to the quality of goods or a person's moral qualities.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这部作品得到了许多评论家的称赞。
English Usage in a sentence: The work received praise from many critics.
Notes: Common for art, literature, film, politics, and cultural commentary.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 我雇了一个人帮忙搬东西。
English Usage in a sentence: I hired someone to help move the things.
Notes: Can stand alone as a verb, although 雇用 and 雇佣 are more formal.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence:
这个数值是相对的，不是绝对的。
这里的生活相对安静。
English Usage in a sentence:
This value is relative, not absolute.
Life here is relatively quiet.
Notes: As an adverb, it commonly means comparatively or relatively.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这个房间的面积较小。
English Usage in a sentence: This room is relatively small.
Notes: 较 means comparatively; common in written comparison.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这辆车虽然很旧，但因为保养到位，看起来依然很好。
English Usage in a sentence: The car is old, but because it has been properly maintained, it still looks good.
Notes: 到位 means something has been done adequately or properly.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 请把这封信连同文件一起交给他。
English Usage in a sentence: Please give him this letter along with the documents.
Notes: Connects something with another item that is included together.

English Words: verb: to spread out / to unfold / to roll out

她把地图铺开在桌上。
计划很快在全国铺开。
English Usage in a sentence:
She spread the map out on the table.
The plan was quickly rolled out nationwide.
Notes: Can describe physically spreading something or figuratively expanding an activity.

English Words:
noun: mark / marker / label
verb: to mark / to label

地图上有一个红色标记。
请把重要的位置标记出来。
English Usage in a sentence:
There is a red marker on the map.
Please mark the important locations.
Notes: Common in software, maps, documents, and physical objects.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 她计划明年去西班牙旅行。
English Usage in a sentence: She plans to travel to Spain next year.
Notes: Country name.

English Words:
noun: center / central area
adjective: central

广场中央有一座雕像。

English Usage in a sentence:
There is a statue in the center of the square.
This is the central hall.
Notes: Can describe a physical center or a central governing authority depending on context.

English Words:
adjective: main / primary
adverb: mainly / primarily

这是主要原因。
这里主要居住着人族。
English Usage in a sentence:
This is the main reason.
This area is inhabited primarily by humans.
Notes: Very common in both speech and writing.

English Words: verb: to depict / to portray / to describe
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 这幅画描绘了古代王国的景象。
English Usage in a sentence: This painting depicts a scene from the ancient kingdom.
Notes: Can refer to visual depiction or descriptive writing.

English Words:
verb: to collectively call
noun: collective term

These races are collectively called demons.
'Demon race' is the collective term for these races.
Notes: Common when several different things share one general name.

English Words: verb: to settle / to take up residence
Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 他们最终决定在这个城市定居。
English Usage in a sentence: They eventually decided to settle in this city.
Notes: Implies establishing a permanent or long-term residence.

Chinese Usage in a Sentence: 传送门连接着两个不同的次元。
English Usage in a sentence: The portal connects two different dimensions.
Notes: In ACG and science-fiction contexts, commonly refers to alternate dimensions or worlds.

English Words:
particle: of
pronoun: it / them / that

这是王族之剑。
